Activities: - Script/notebook executions with timestamps - Which entities were used (with column-level detail) - Which entities were generated - Associated agents (user, software) - Git commit hash and dirty state

Field Derivations: - Which output columns came from which source datasets - Column-level provenance (prov:qualifiedDerivation) - Auto-populated on read so provenance flows through merge/join/concat

Metadata: - Content hash (detects when data actually changes) - Creation timestamp (only updated when content changes) - Source relationships

docs.title: Accessing Lineage
docs.text:
# Read and transform data
df = pd.read_csv('input.csv', project_path=PROJECT_PATH)
result = df[df['value'] > 100].groupby('category').sum()

# Access lineage through metadata (preferred)
print(result.metadata.lineage.sources)
print(result.metadata.lineage.get_licenses())

# Check field derivations
if result.metadata.lineage.field_derivations:
    for fd in result.metadata.lineage.field_derivations:
        print(f"  {fd.output_field} <- {fd.source_entity}.{fd.source_field}")

# Check activity details
if result.metadata.lineage.activity:
    activity = result.metadata.lineage.activity
    print(f"Activity: {activity.id}")
    print(f"Started: {activity.started_at}")
    for agent in activity.was_associated_with:
        print(f"Agent: {agent.label} ({agent.type.value})")

docs.title: Field-Level Derivations
docs.text:
When you read a dataset, sunstone automatically records which columns came from which source. This propagates through operations:

# Read: each column gets a derivation record
schools = pd.read_csv('schools.csv', project_path=PROJECT_PATH)
# schools.metadata.lineage.field_derivations contains:
#   FieldDerivation(output_field='name', source_entity='school-data', source_field='name')
#   FieldDerivation(output_field='enrollment', source_entity='school-data', source_field='enrollment')
#   ...

# Merge: derivations from both sources are combined
merged = pd.merge(schools, teachers, on='school_id')
# merged has derivations from both 'school-data' and 'teacher-data'

docs.title: Lineage Persistence
docs.text:
When you save a DataFrame, the output is registered in datasets.yaml and its lineage, including PROV-O activity tracking, is written to datasets.lock.yaml:

result.to_csv(
    'outputs/summary.csv',
    slug='summary',
    name='Summary Results',
    index=False
)

This adds to datasets.yaml:

outputs:
  - title: Summary Results
    name: summary
    path: outputs/summary.csv
    schema:
      fields:
        - name: category
          type: string
        - name: value
          type: number

and to datasets.lock.yaml:

outputs:
  - slug: summary
    data_hash: sha256:abc123...
    created_at: '2026-02-04T10:30:00'
    sources:
      - slug: input-data
        prov:wasAttributedTo: Example Org
        dct:license: CC-BY-4.0
    activity:
      id: exec-20260204T103000-abc123
      agents:
        - id: stig
          type: prov:Person
        - id: sunstone-py
          type: prov:SoftwareAgent
          version: '1.19.0'
      used:
        - entity: input-data
      started_at: '2026-02-04T10:29:55'
      ended_at: '2026-02-04T10:30:00'
    field_derivations:
      - output_field: category
        source_entity: input-data
        source_field: category
      - output_field: value
        source_entity: input-data
        source_field: value

docs.title: Lineage Propagation
docs.text:
Lineage automatically propagates through operations:

# Read two sources
schools = pd.read_csv('schools.csv', project_path=PROJECT_PATH)  # source 1
teachers = pd.read_csv('teachers.csv', project_path=PROJECT_PATH)  # source 2

# Merge combines lineage from both
merged = pd.merge(schools, teachers, on='school_id')

# Result tracks both sources
print(len(merged.metadata.lineage.sources))  # 2

docs.title: Content Hash Optimization
docs.text:
The content hash prevents unnecessary timestamp updates:

# First save
result.to_csv('output.csv', slug='output', name='Output')
# lineage.created_at = '2026-02-04T10:00:00'

# Re-run with same result
result.to_csv('output.csv', slug='output', name='Output')
# lineage.created_at = '2026-02-04T10:00:00'  (unchanged!)

# Re-run with different result
result_v2.to_csv('output.csv', slug='output', name='Output')
# lineage.created_at = '2026-02-04T11:00:00'  (updated!)

docs.title: DataFrame Metadata
docs.text: Every DataFrame carries a metadata container that holds lineage and per-field annotations. This metadata flows through operations and is persisted to datasets.yaml on write.

docs.title: The Metadata Container
docs.text:
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv', project_path=PROJECT_PATH)

df.metadata.slug = 'my-analysis'
df.metadata.name = 'My Analysis'
df.metadata.description = 'Analysis of school enrollment data'

# RDF prefixes and custom properties
df.metadata.rdf_prefixes = {'schema': 'http://schema.org/'}
df.metadata.custom_properties = {'schema:about': 'Education'}

# Lineage is accessed through metadata
print(df.metadata.lineage.sources)

docs.title: Per-Field Metadata
docs.text:
Annotate individual columns with descriptions, units, and source tracking:

df.set_field_metadata('enrollment', description='Total enrolled students', unit='students')
df.set_field_metadata('area_km2', description='School district area', unit='km^2')
df.set_field_metadata('density', description='Students per square kilometer', unit='students / km^2')

Field metadata is written to datasets.yaml alongside the field schema:

schema:
  fields:
    - name: enrollment
      type: integer
      description: Total enrolled students
      si:unit: students
    - name: area_km2
      type: number
      description: School district area
      si:unit: km^2

docs.title: Primary Key
docs.text:
Declare the column(s) that uniquely identify a row with schema.primaryKey, next to schema.fields. It follows the Frictionless Table Schema: a single field name or a list of field names, each of which must be declared in schema.fields.

outputs:
  - title: Population
    name: population
    path: outputs/population.csv
    schema:
      fields:
        - name: country
          type: string
        - name: year
          type: integer
        - name: value
          type: number
      primaryKey: [country, year]

sunstone package build/push writes it to schema.primaryKey of the resource in datapackage.json, always as a list.

docs.title: Deprecation: df.lineage
docs.text: The old df.lineage accessor still works but is deprecated. Use df.metadata.lineage instead.

docs.title: Plugin System
docs.text: Reading, writing, and URL fetching are handled by a plugin registry. Built-in handlers cover common formats and URL schemes; external plugins are discovered automatically via entry points.

docs.title: Built-in Support
docs.text:
Formats: CSV, JSON, Excel, Parquet, TSV

URL schemes: - Local file paths (built-in) - http:// and https:// (built-in, with SSRF protection) - gs:// (requires sunstone-py[gcs]) - s3:// and r2:// (requires sunstone-py[s3])

docs.title: Using the Plugin Registry
docs.text:
from sunstone.plugins import PluginRegistry
from pathlib import Path

registry = PluginRegistry.get('/path/to/project')

# Fetch a file from any supported URL
registry.fetch('gs://my-bucket/data.csv', Path('data/local.csv'))

docs.title: Writing Custom Plugins
docs.text:
Implement one or more plugin protocols (AuthProvider, URLHandler, FormatHandler) and register via entry points:

# In your plugin's pyproject.toml
[project.entry-points."sunstone.plugins"]
my-plugin = "my_package:MyPlugin"

docs.title: Plugin Configuration
docs.text:
Configuration uses cascading precedence:

  1. datasets.yaml → plugins.<name> section (highest priority)
  2. pyproject.toml → [tool.sunstone.plugins.<name>]
  3. Environment variables → SUNSTONE_PLUGIN_<NAME>_<KEY>

docs.title: Unit-Aware Arithmetic
docs.text: sunstone-py integrates with Pint for unit-aware column operations. When columns have units set via set_field_metadata(), arithmetic operations validate unit compatibility.

docs.title: Unit Modes
docs.text:
export SUNSTONE_UNIT_MODE=auto  # or: strict, relaxed (default)

from sunstone.units import set_unit_mode
set_unit_mode('auto')
Mode Behavior relaxed No unit validation (default) strict Raises UnitError on incompatible operations auto Auto-converts compatible units, warns on mismatch

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from sunstone.units import set_unit_mode
set_unit_mode('auto')

df.set_field_metadata('distance_km', unit='km')
df.set_field_metadata('distance_miles', unit='mile')

# In auto mode, merging DataFrames with km and miles on the same
# column will automatically convert to a common unit

docs.title: QUDT Round-Tripping
docs.text: Units stored as QUDT URIs in datasets.yaml are preserved through read/write cycles. The original URI is stored in FieldSchema.unit_source so it round-trips without loss.

docs.title: License Compatibility
docs.text:
sunstone-py treats licenses as a first-class part of lineage: every input declares a source.license, every output declares an effective license (its own, its packages[] entry, or the top-level package.license), and the compatibility between them is checked automatically at write time.

There are three layers of license handling, intentionally graded from soft to hard:

  1. Lint (sunstone lint) — R005 flags a dataset that has no license at all; R006 flags a license string that isn't a recognised SPDX identifier or LicenseRef-* form.
  2. CLI audit (sunstone license check) — runs the compatibility engine across every output's wasDerivedFrom chain and exits non-zero on conflict. Use it in CI. See the CLI Guide.
  3. Write-time enforcement — to_csv() / to_parquet() raise LicenseCompatibilityError when the target license is incompatible with a source license in the current session lineage. When no target license is declared, one is auto-derived from the sources (inheriting a single source's license, or picking the most restrictive license that satisfies all sources) and persisted to datasets.yaml. Pass check_license=False to skip on a specific write.

docs.title: How the Compatibility Engine Works
docs.text:
Each license in the embedded registry is described by five boolean properties — public_domain, attribution, share_alike, non_commercial, no_derivatives — plus a family tag for ShareAlike. A (source → target) pair is checked against this rule set:

Source property Constraint on target (any) Target must not be no_derivatives: no output carries a NoDerivatives license (lint R010), except a declared copy (see below). Auto-derivation never picks one. public_domain None — compatible with anything. share_alike Target must also be share_alike and share the same family. (CC-BY-SA-4.0 and CC-BY-SA-3.0 are different families on purpose — Creative Commons treats them as one-way upgradable, not mutually equivalent.) no_derivatives No target is compatible: adapted material may not be shared. Record permission from the rights holder to lift this (see below). non_commercial Target must also be non_commercial. attribution (without SA/NC) Target must be attribution or share_alike (SA implies attribution).

A check fails as soon as any source/target pair violates the rules; the resulting LicenseCompatibilityResult lists every conflict and a suggestions list of registry licenses that would satisfy all known sources. The most-restrictive ordering — used by get_most_restrictive_license() and by suggestion ranking — is NoDerivatives > ShareAlike > NonCommercial > Attribution > Public Domain.

docs.title: Embedded License Registry
docs.text:
The registry is the one license list used by lint R006, sunstone dataset validate and the compatibility engine. Anything outside it must use a LicenseRef-* identifier or proprietary; those pass R006 but are reported as unknown_sources by the compatibility engine and excluded from the rule check.

SPDX id Class CC0-1.0, PDDL-1.0, LicenseRef-US-PD Public domain CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-3.0, CC-BY-3.0-IGO Attribution only ODC-By-1.0, LicenseRef-OGL-3.0, NLOD-1.0, NLOD-2.0, LicenseRef-GODL-India Attribution only CC-BY-SA-4.0, CC-BY-SA-3.0, ODbL-1.0 Attribution + ShareAlike (each is its own family) CC-BY-NC-4.0, CC-BY-NC-3.0, CC-BY-NC-3.0-IGO Attribution + NonCommercial CC-BY-ND-4.0 Attribution + NoDerivatives CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0 Attribution + NonCommercial + NoDerivatives CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, CC-BY-NC-SA-3.0, CC-BY-NC-SA-3.0-IGO Attribution + NonCommercial + ShareAlike (each is its own family) Unlicense, public-domain Public domain MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause Attribution only GPL-2.0-*, GPL-3.0-*, LGPL-3.0-*, MPL-2.0 Attribution + ShareAlike (one family per license and version)

Adding a license is a one-line append to _REGISTRY_ENTRIES in src/sunstone/licenses.py. The full set is also available programmatically via sunstone.licenses.known_licenses().

docs.title: Recording Permission from the Rights Holder
docs.text:
When the rights holder grants terms beyond the source license (for example, permission to share derivatives of a NoDerivatives or proprietary source; an ND source cannot feed any output without one), record the grant under dct:rights on the source. Its dct:license is the license granted for derivatives, and the compatibility engine uses it in place of the source's dct:license:

source:
  dct:license: CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0
  dct:rights:
    rdfs:label: Example Org permits sharing derived tables under CC-BY-4.0
    dct:license: CC-BY-4.0
    dct:date: '2026-10-19'
    rdfs:seeAlso: audit/permissions/example-org.pdf

Keep dct:license as the license the publisher states. Point rdfs:seeAlso at the written grant.

docs.title: Unmodified Copies
docs.text:
An output that copies one source without modifying it is not a derivative, so it may keep the source license, NoDerivatives included. Declare it with prov:wasQuotedFrom:

outputs:
  - title: UN member states (copy)
    name: un-member-states-copy
    path: outputs/un-member-states.csv
    prov:wasQuotedFrom: un-member-states

The output then inherits the source license (an explicit license other than the source's goes through the normal check). Writes fail unless the output reads only that source and every output column is a column in the source's schema.fields. Selecting rows or columns is allowed. Values are not compared, so do not declare a copy for a transformed column.

docs.title: Worked Example
docs.text:
A source un-members is licensed CC-BY-NC-4.0. You merge it with a CC-BY-4.0 input and try to publish under CC-BY-4.0:

result.to_csv(
    "outputs/derived.csv",
    slug="derived",
    name="Derived Data",
    license="CC-BY-4.0",
)
# raises LicenseCompatibilityError:
#   CC-BY-NC-4.0 is NonCommercial: derivatives must also be NonCommercial, not CC-BY-4.0
#   Suggested compatible target licenses: CC-BY-NC-4.0, CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, CC-BY-NC-3.0-IGO

The fix is to widen the output to a NonCommercial license — or, if you have rights to do so, to remove the NC source from the lineage. The engine does not let you "wash out" a NonCommercial source by mixing it with a permissive one; that is the correct behaviour under Creative Commons.

docs.title: Auto-Derived Target Licenses
docs.text:
When the output has source licenses but no declared target (no license: on the dataset, no packages[].license / package.license covering it, and no license= argument to the writer), the writer derives a target automatically:

  • One unique source license — the output inherits it.
  • Multiple compatible source licenses — the writer picks the most restrictive license that satisfies every source (e.g., CC-BY-4.0 + CC-BY-NC-4.0 → CC-BY-NC-4.0).
  • Mutually incompatible sources, or unknown licenses among multiples — LicenseCompatibilityError. The writer refuses to guess; declare an explicit license: to proceed.

Any auto-derived license is persisted to datasets.yaml so future reads and sunstone license check runs see it as declared.

docs.title: Conflicting Licenses
docs.text: An explicitly declared target license that is incompatible with a source license is always a hard failure (LicenseCompatibilityError) — silently publishing under the wrong license can be a legal problem. Combine sunstone lint --warnings-as-errors (catches missing licenses at lint time) with sunstone license check (catches conflicts) in CI to make both classes hard failures before publish.

docs.title: Dataset Metadata
docs.text: Every dataset in datasets.yaml has rich metadata:

docs.title: Required Fields
docs.text:
- title: Human-Readable Name
  name: machine-readable-name
  path: path/to/file.csv
  schema:
    fields:
      - name: column_name
        type: string  # or number, integer, boolean, date, datetime

docs.title: Optional Fields
docs.text:
min_sunstone_version: 1.20.0

# Top-level publishing configuration (applies to all outputs)
publish:
  enabled: true
  to: gs://bucket-name/path/
  flatten: false  # optional: flatten directory structure

inputs:
  - title: Example Dataset
    name: example
    path: data/example.csv
    licenses:
      - name: CC-BY-4.0

    # How the local copy was obtained
    prov:generatedAtTime: '2025-01-15'
    prov:wasGeneratedBy:
      dct:type: manual-download  # or api, web-scraping, etc.

    # Source attribution for inputs
    source:
      title: Data Provider Dataset
      dcat:downloadURL: https://example.com/data.csv
      dcat:landingPage: https://example.com/dataset
      # dcat:accessURL: https://example.com/api  # indirect access (API, query form)
      dct:publisher:                    # organisation that makes the data available
        rdfs:label: Data Provider Name
        skos:altLabel: DPN
      dct:creator:                      # optional: authors or producing organisations
        - rdfs:label: Organisation or Person
      dct:license: CC-BY-4.0

    # Strict mode flag
    strict: true

outputs:
  - title: Output Dataset
    name: output-example
    path: outputs/example.csv
    licenses:
      - name: CC-BY-4.0

    # Strict mode flag
    strict: true

# Lineage (sources, activity, hashes) is written to datasets.lock.yaml, not datasets.yaml.

docs.title: Publishing Configuration
docs.text:
The top-level publish section controls how data packages are published:

publish:
  enabled: true                              # Required: enable publishing
  to: gs://bucket/datasets/project-name/     # GCS upload destination
  as: https://data.example.com/project-name/ # Optional: public URL base for datapackage.json
  flatten: false                             # Optional: flatten directory structure

Path Resolution:

  • If to ends with .json: Used as the datapackage filename
  • gs://bucket/countries.json → datapackage at gs://bucket/countries.json

  • Data files in gs://bucket/ (relative to datapackage directory)

  • If to doesn't end with .json: Treated as a directory

  • gs://bucket/datasets/project/ → datapackage at gs://bucket/datasets/project/datapackage.json
  • Data files in gs://bucket/datasets/project/

Public URL Option (as):

When your GCS bucket is served via a CDN or custom domain, use as to set the public-facing URLs in datapackage.json:

publish:
  to: gs://my-bucket/datasets/project/      # Files uploaded here
  as: https://data.example.com/project/     # URLs in datapackage.json use this base
  • Files are uploaded to gs://my-bucket/datasets/project/outputs/data.csv
  • But datapackage.json contains: "path": "https://data.example.com/project/outputs/data.csv"

This allows data consumers to fetch files directly from your public URL.

Flatten Option:

  • flatten: false (default): Preserves directory structure from path

  • path: outputs/data/file.csv → gs://bucket/project/outputs/data/file.csv

  • flatten: true: Puts all files in same directory as datapackage.json

  • path: outputs/data/file.csv → gs://bucket/project/file.csv

docs.title: Validation Tools
docs.text:
Check notebooks and scripts for correct import usage:

import sunstone

# Check a single notebook
result = sunstone.check_notebook_imports('analysis.ipynb')
print(result.summary())

# Check all notebooks in project
results = sunstone.validate_project_notebooks('/path/to/project')
for path, result in results.items():
    if not result.is_valid:
        print(f"\n{path}:")
        print(result.summary())

What validation checks: - Files use from sunstone import pandas as pd instead of plain pandas - No direct pandas imports in data processing code - Proper usage of project_path parameter

docs.title: Project Path Configuration
docs.text:
read_csv, read_excel, read_json, read_dataset, and the DataFrame constructor all need to know which project's datasets.yaml to consult. They accept a project_path= argument; when none is given, they fall back to a process-wide default, and finally to Path.cwd().

import sunstone
from sunstone import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path

# 1. Set once for the entire process (recommended in notebooks/scripts)
sunstone.set_project_path(Path(__file__).parent)
df = pd.read_csv('inputs/data.csv')          # uses configured path

# 2. Pass explicitly per call (overrides the default)
df = pd.read_csv('inputs/data.csv', project_path='/other/project')

# 3. Scoped override
with sunstone.use_project_path('/temporary/project'):
    df = pd.read_csv('inputs/other.csv')
# default is restored after the with block

# Read or clear the configured default
print(sunstone.get_project_path())
sunstone.clear_project_path()

The configured value is held in a contextvars.ContextVar, so it is safe across threads and async tasks.

docs.title: Organizing Datasets Across Files
docs.text:
For projects with many datasets, datasets.yaml can pull in additional files via an include: directive:

# datasets.yaml
package:
  name: my-project
  licenses:
    - name: CC-BY-4.0

include:
  - datasets/inputs.yaml
  - datasets/outputs.yaml

# Top-level inputs/outputs/packages here are still allowed
inputs: []
outputs: []

Each included file may declare its own inputs:, outputs:, and packages: lists. Top-level configuration that affects the whole project (defaults, rdfPrefixes, package, publish, min_sunstone_version) is not allowed in included files — only in the main datasets.yaml.

Other rules:

  • Includes are not nested — an included file cannot itself contain an include: key.
  • Name collisions across files are an error: every dataset name and every package name must be unique across the merged set.
  • Paths are relative to the file containing the include: directive.

docs.title: SUNSTONE_DATAFRAME_STRICT
docs.text:
Enable strict mode globally:

export SUNSTONE_DATAFRAME_STRICT=1
# or
export SUNSTONE_DATAFRAME_STRICT=true

# Now all operations are strict by default
df = pd.read_csv('input.csv')  # strict=True implied

docs.title: Start Relaxed, Lock for Production
docs.text:
1. Development: Use relaxed mode for exploration
  2. Refinement: Review auto-generated datasets.yaml entries
  3. Production: Lock datasets with sunstone dataset lock

docs.title: Lint Before You Ship
docs.text: Run sunstone lint to catch missing licenses, units, descriptions, and names that don't follow project conventions before publishing. In CI, use sunstone lint --warnings-as-errors to make recommended-but-not-required metadata mandatory. See the CLI Guide for the full rule list.

docs.title: Document Sources Thoroughly
docs.text:
inputs:
  - title: UN Member States
    name: un-members
    path: inputs/un_members.csv
    description: |
      Downloaded from the official UN website.
      Data accurate as of January 2025.
    prov:generatedAtTime: '2025-01-15'
    prov:wasGeneratedBy:
      dct:type: manual-download
    source:
      title: Member States
      dcat:landingPage: https://www.un.org/en/about-us/member-states
      dct:publisher:
        rdfs:label: United Nations
        skos:altLabel: UN
      dct:license: CC0-1.0

docs.title: Use Descriptive Names
docs.text:
# Good
name: school-enrollment-by-district
name: teacher-demographics-2025

# Avoid
name: data1
name: output
name: final_final_v2

docs.title: Track Operations Explicitly
docs.text:
# Instead of chaining without description
result = df.apply(complex_function)

# Add operation description for lineage
result = df.apply_operation(
    complex_function,
    description="Apply enrollment adjustment factors"
)

docs.title: Version Your Datasets
docs.text:
outputs:
  - title: School Summary v2.1
    name: school-summary-v2-1
    path: outputs/school-summary-v2.1.csv

Or use the version field in package metadata when building data packages.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Data Package standard provides excellent extensibility for augmenting descriptors with custom metadata, including semantic annotations from knowledge graphs, domain-specific properties, and organizational metadata.

docs.title: RDF Triple Support in datasets.yaml
docs.text: Sunstone supports RDF (Resource Description Framework) triples in datasets.yaml with automatic prefix expansion when generating datapackage.json. This makes it easy to add semantic metadata using familiar prefixed names that get expanded to full URIs in the final package.

docs.title: Defining RDF Prefixes
docs.text:
Define RDF namespace prefixes at the dataset level or in a defaults: section:

defaults:
  rdfPrefixes:
    si: "https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#"
    si30: "https://sunstone.institute/rdf/threat/"
    dcat: "http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#"
    prov: "http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#"

outputs:
  - title: Climate Dataset
    name: climate-dataset
    path: outputs/climate.csv
    # RDF properties using prefixes
    si:monitorsThreat: si30:27
    si:category: environmental
    dcat:theme: climate
    schema:
      fields:
        - name: year
          type: integer

docs.title: Prefix Expansion
docs.text:
When you build a datapackage, prefixes in both property names and values are automatically expanded to full URIs:

# In datasets.yaml
si:monitorsThreat: si30:27

Becomes:

// In datapackage.json
"https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#monitorsThreat": "https://sunstone.institute/rdf/threat/27"

docs.title: Using Full URIs Directly
docs.text:
You can also use full URIs directly without prefixes:

outputs:
  - title: My Dataset
    name: my-dataset
    path: outputs/data.csv
    https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#datasetType: observational
    schema: {fields: [...]}

docs.title: Object values
docs.text:
An RDF property may take an object. It is emitted as a JSON-LD node: keys inside it are RDF properties (expanded the same way) or @id/@type.

prov:wasGeneratedBy:
  "@type": prov:Activity
  dct:type: manual-download

docs.title: Default Properties
docs.text:
Use the defaults: section to apply RDF properties to all datasets:

defaults:
  rdfPrefixes:
    si: "https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#"
  si:organization: "Sunstone Institute"
  si:license: "CC-BY-4.0"

outputs:
  - title: Dataset 1
    name: dataset-1
    path: outputs/data1.csv
    si:theme: climate  # Inherits prefixes from defaults
    schema: {fields: [...]}

  - title: Dataset 2
    name: dataset-2
    path: outputs/data2.csv
    si:theme: biodiversity  # Also inherits prefixes
    schema: {fields: [...]}

Both datasets will include the default si:organization and si:license properties with expanded URIs in the generated datapackage.

docs.title: Overriding Default Prefixes
docs.text:
Dataset-level prefix definitions override defaults:

defaults:
  rdfPrefixes:
    si: "https://old.example.com/vocab#"

outputs:
  - title: My Dataset
    name: my-dataset
    path: outputs/data.csv
    rdfPrefixes:
      si: "https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#"  # Overrides default
    si:property: value
    schema: {fields: [...]}

docs.title: Automatic RDF Type Properties
docs.text:
Every generated datapackage.json automatically includes RDF type properties for DCAT (Data Catalog Vocabulary) compatibility:

  • Package level: "rdf:type": "dcat:Dataset" (automatically expanded to full URIs)
  • Resource level: "rdf:type": "dcat:Distribution" (automatically expanded to full URIs)

Example generated datapackage:

{
  "name": "my-project",
  "http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type": "http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#Dataset",
  "resources": [
    {
      "name": "my-resource",
      "http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type": "http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#Distribution",
      "path": "data.csv",
      ...
    }
  ]
}

This makes all generated datapackages compatible with DCAT-based data catalogs and semantic web tools without any additional configuration.

docs.title: Methodology URL Handling
docs.text:
The https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#methodology property receives special handling. When its value is not already a URI, it is resolved as a relative URI against the package base URI (publish.as). All referenced methodology files are uploaded alongside other resources during sunstone package push.

This applies regardless of how the property is specified — via an si: prefix, a different prefix mapped to the same namespace, or as a full URI directly. The property can appear at the top level (via defaults:), on individual resources, or both — each resource can reference its own methodology file.

  • Local build (sunstone package build): Without publish.as, the value is kept as a relative path
  • Publishing (sunstone package push): The value is resolved against publish.as to produce a full URL, and all referenced local files are uploaded

Configure the package base URI with publish.as:

publish:
  enabled: true
  to: gs://my-bucket/datasets/project/    # GCS destination for upload
  as: https://cdn.example.com/datasets/project/  # Package base URI

defaults:
  rdfPrefixes:
    si: "https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#"
  dcat-si:methodology: docs/default-methodology.md  # Shared methodology for all datasets

outputs:
  - title: Climate Dataset
    name: climate-dataset
    path: outputs/climate.csv
    dcat-si:methodology: docs/climate-methodology.md  # Per-dataset override
    schema:
      fields:
        - name: year
          type: integer

  - title: Biodiversity Dataset
    name: biodiversity-dataset
    path: outputs/biodiversity.csv
    # Inherits docs/default-methodology.md from defaults
    schema:
      fields:
        - name: species
          type: string

When published, each resource's datapackage.json entry will contain the resolved methodology URL, and all unique local methodology files are uploaded:

{
  "https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#methodology": "https://cdn.example.com/datasets/project/docs/climate-methodology.md"
}

If the value already contains a full URI, it's preserved as-is. However, if the URI starts with the publish.as base URI, the corresponding local file is still uploaded.

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
Here's a complete example showing RDF properties in datasets.yaml and the resulting datapackage.json:

datasets.yaml: 

min_sunstone_version: 1.20.0
defaults:
  rdfPrefixes:
    si: "https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#"
    si30: "https://sunstone.institute/rdf/threat/"
    dcat: "http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#"
  si:publisher: "Sunstone Institute"

outputs:
  - title: Climate Impact Dataset
    name: climate-impact
    path: outputs/climate.csv
    si:monitorsThreat: si30:27
    si:category: environmental
    dcat:theme: http://eurovoc.europa.eu/2107
    schema:
      fields:
        - name: year
          type: integer
        - name: temperature
          type: number

Generated datapackage.json: 

{
  "name": "my-project",
  "http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type": "http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#Dataset",
  "resources": [
    {
      "name": "climate-impact",
      "title": "Climate Impact Dataset",
      "path": "outputs/climate.csv",
      "type": "table",
      "format": "csv",
      "http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type": "http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#Distribution",
      "https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#monitorsThreat": "https://sunstone.institute/rdf/threat/27",
      "https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#category": "environmental",
      "http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#theme": "http://eurovoc.europa.eu/2107",
      "https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#publisher": "Sunstone Institute",
      "schema": {
        "fields": [
          {"name": "year", "type": "integer"},
          {"name": "temperature", "type": "number"}
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}

All prefixes are automatically expanded to full URIs, and the DCAT type properties are added automatically.

docs.title: Custom Properties with Namespaces
docs.text: The Data Package specification supports custom properties using the namespace:propertyName convention. This allows you to add any metadata without conflicting with standard properties.

docs.title: Basic Example
docs.text:
{
  "name": "my-package",
  "myorg:internal_id": "12345",
  "myorg:department": "research",
  "resources": []
}

docs.title: Semantic Metadata at Multiple Levels
docs.text: Custom properties can be added at any level of the descriptor, making it ideal for semantic web integration and knowledge graph alignment.

docs.title: 1. Package Level
docs.text:
Add semantic metadata to describe the entire dataset:

{
  "$schema": "https://datapackage.org/profiles/2.0/datapackage.json",
  "name": "climate-observations",
  "title": "Climate Observation Dataset",
  "dct:conformsTo": "http://schema.org/Dataset",
  "dct:subject": [
    "http://dbpedia.org/resource/Climate_change",
    "http://dbpedia.org/resource/Temperature"
  ],
  "dct:spatial": "http://sws.geonames.org/3144096/",
  "schema:temporalCoverage": "2020-01-01/2024-12-31",
  "resources": [...]
}

docs.title: 2. Resource Level
docs.text:
Annotate individual data resources with semantic concepts:

{
  "resources": [
    {
      "name": "temperatures",
      "path": "data/temperatures.csv",
      "type": "table",
      "dct:subject": "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_01000267",
      "si:methodology": "http://example.org/methodology/automated-sensor",
      "prov:wasGeneratedBy": "http://example.org/activity/sensor-collection-2024",
      "schema": {...}
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: 3. Field Level (Schema)
docs.text:
Add semantic annotations to individual fields for precise meaning:

{
  "schema": {
    "fields": [
      {
        "name": "temperature",
        "type": "number",
        "title": "Air Temperature",
        "qudt:unit": "http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/DEG_C",
        "sosa:observedProperty": "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000146",
        "constraints": {
          "minimum": -50,
          "maximum": 50
        }
      },
      {
        "name": "location_id",
        "type": "string",
        "dct:references": "http://www.geonames.org/",
        "skos:exactMatch": "http://www.w3.org/2003/01/geo/wgs84_pos#SpatialThing"
      },
      {
        "name": "species_code",
        "type": "string",
        "dwc:scientificName": "Taxonomic reference",
        "rdfs:seeAlso": "http://rs.gbif.org/vocabulary/gbif/taxonomic_status.xml"
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: 1. Knowledge Graph Integration
docs.text:
Link datasets to ontologies and knowledge graphs:

{
  "name": "biodiversity-survey",
  "dct:conformsTo": [
    "http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/",
    "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/envo.owl"
  ],
  "schema:isBasedOn": "http://example.org/research/project/12345",
  "resources": [...]
}

docs.title: 2. Provenance Tracking
docs.text:
Use W3C PROV vocabulary for data lineage:

{
  "name": "processed-data",
  "prov:wasDerivedFrom": "http://example.org/dataset/raw-data",
  "prov:wasGeneratedBy": {
    "prov:activity": "data-cleaning-2024-01",
    "prov:atTime": "2024-01-15T10:00:00Z",
    "prov:wasAssociatedWith": "http://example.org/agent/data-team"
  },
  "resources": [...]
}

docs.title: 3. Domain-Specific Metadata
docs.text:
Add field-specific vocabularies for specialized domains:

{
  "schema": {
    "fields": [
      {
        "name": "sample_id",
        "type": "string",
        "obi:hasURI": "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0000066",
        "lab:protocol": "http://example.org/protocols/sampling-v2"
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: 4. Organizational Metadata
docs.text:
Internal tracking and workflow properties:

{
  "name": "my-dataset",
  "myorg:project_id": "PRJ-2024-001",
  "myorg:status": "approved",
  "myorg:confidentiality": "internal",
  "myorg:retention_period": "P7Y",
  "myorg:owner": "research-team-alpha",
  "resources": [...]
}

docs.title: Recommended Namespace Prefixes
docs.text:
Consider using established vocabulary prefixes for interoperability:

Prefix Namespace Purpose si: https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab# Sunstone Institute vocabulary dct: http://purl.org/dc/terms/ Dublin Core Terms rdfs: http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema# RDF Schema schema: http://schema.org/ Schema.org vocabulary dcat: http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat# Data Catalog Vocabulary prov: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov# Provenance Ontology skos: http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core# Simple Knowledge Organization dwc: http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/ Darwin Core (biodiversity) dcat-si: https://sunstone.institute/rdf/data# Sunstone dataset-level terms (methodology) geo: http://www.opengis.net/ont/geosparql# OGC GeoSPARQL (geometry classes and datatypes) sosa: http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/ Sensor, Observation, Sample, Actuator qudt: http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/ Quantities, Units, Dimensions obi: http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_ Ontology for Biomedical Investigations

docs.title: 1. Use Consistent Namespaces
docs.text:
Choose a namespace prefix for your organization and use it consistently:

{
  "myorg:property1": "value",
  "myorg:property2": "value"
}

docs.title: 2. Document Your Extensions
docs.text:
Add a README or separate documentation explaining your custom properties:

{
  "name": "my-dataset",
  "myorg:metadata_version": "1.0",
  "myorg:schema_documentation": "https://example.org/docs/metadata-schema",
  "resources": [...]
}

docs.title: 3. Preserve Standard Properties
docs.text:
Never override or conflict with standard Data Package properties:

{
  // Good: Custom property with namespace
  "myorg:title": "Internal title",
  "title": "Public title",

  // Bad: Don't redefine standard properties
  // "resources": "something else"
}

docs.title: 4. Use URIs for Semantic References
docs.text:
When linking to knowledge graphs, use full URIs:

{
  "dct:subject": "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_01000267",
  // Not: "dct:subject": "ENVO_01000267"
}

docs.title: 5. Validate with Custom Profiles
docs.text:
For strict validation of your extensions, create a custom profile:

{
  "$schema": "https://example.org/profiles/myorg-datapackage.json",
  "name": "my-dataset",
  "myorg:required_property": "value",
  "resources": [...]
}

docs.title: Complete Example: Semantic Research Dataset
docs.text:
{
  "$schema": "https://datapackage.org/profiles/2.0/datapackage.json",
  "name": "ocean-temperature-study",
  "title": "Ocean Temperature Observations 2020-2024",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Multi-year ocean temperature study from coastal monitoring stations",

  // Semantic metadata
  "schema:keywords": ["oceanography", "climate", "temperature"],
  "dcat:theme": ["http://eurovoc.europa.eu/2107"],
  "dct:conformsTo": "http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/",
  "dct:spatial": "http://sws.geonames.org/3144096/",

  // Provenance
  "prov:wasDerivedFrom": "http://example.org/dataset/raw-sensor-data",
  "prov:wasGeneratedBy": {
    "prov:activity": "quality-control-pipeline-v2",
    "prov:atTime": "2024-01-15T10:00:00Z"
  },

  // Organizational
  "myorg:project_id": "OCEAN-2024-001",
  "myorg:funding_source": "NSF Grant #12345",
  "myorg:data_classification": "public",

  "licenses": [{
    "name": "CC-BY-4.0",
    "path": "https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/"
  }],

  "resources": [
    {
      "name": "temperature-readings",
      "type": "table",
      "path": "data/temperatures.csv",
      "title": "Temperature Observations",

      // Resource-level semantics
      "sosa:observationType": "http://example.org/observation/sea-surface-temperature",
      "example:instrumentType": "http://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/L05/current/134/",

      "schema": {
        "fields": [
          {
            "name": "timestamp",
            "type": "datetime",
            "title": "Observation Time",
            "constraints": {"required": true}
          },
          {
            "name": "station_id",
            "type": "string",
            "title": "Monitoring Station ID",
            "dct:references": "http://example.org/stations/",
            "constraints": {"required": true}
          },
          {
            "name": "temperature",
            "type": "number",
            "title": "Sea Surface Temperature",

            // Field-level semantics
            "sosa:observedProperty": "http://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/P07/current/CFSN0381/",
            "qudt:unit": "http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/DEG_C",
            "skos:definition": "Temperature measured at 1 meter below sea surface",

            "constraints": {
              "required": true,
              "minimum": -2,
              "maximum": 40
            }
          },
          {
            "name": "depth_meters",
            "type": "number",
            "title": "Measurement Depth",
            "qudt:unit": "http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/M",
            "constraints": {"minimum": 0}
          },
          {
            "name": "quality_flag",
            "type": "integer",
            "title": "QC Flag",
            "myorg:qc_version": "v2.1",
            "categories": [
              {"value": 0, "label": "good"},
              {"value": 1, "label": "suspect"},
              {"value": 2, "label": "bad"}
            ]
          }
        ],
        "primaryKey": ["timestamp", "station_id"]
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
1. Any level is extensible - Add custom properties at package, resource, or field level
  2. Use namespaces - Prefix custom properties to avoid conflicts
  3. JSON flexibility - Custom properties can be strings, objects, arrays, etc.
  4. Standard tools preserve - Custom properties pass through standard Data Package tools
  5. Perfect for semantics - Ideal for linking to knowledge graphs, ontologies, and vocabularies
  6. No validation by default - Create custom profiles if you need validation of extensions

This extensibility makes Data Package an excellent choice for FAIR data principles and semantic web integration while maintaining simplicity and interoperability.

docs.title: Data Packages How-To
docs.text: This guide explains how to configure datasets.yaml to define, build, and publish data packages using the sunstone CLI.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A Sunstone project's datasets.yaml declares inputs (source data), outputs (produced data), and packages (what to publish and where). The sunstone package build and sunstone package push commands use this configuration to produce Data Package v2 bundles.

docs.title: Inputs and Outputs
docs.text:
Every project starts with inputs: and outputs: sections. Inputs describe the raw data you consume; outputs describe what your scripts produce.

min_sunstone_version: 1.20.0
inputs:
  - title: Raw Survey Data
    name: raw-survey-data
    path: inputs/survey_raw.csv
    source:
      title: National Statistics Office
      dcat:downloadURL: https://example.org/survey-2025.csv
      dct:publisher:
        rdfs:label: National Statistics Office
      dct:license: CC-BY-4.0
    prov:generatedAtTime: '2025-06-01'
    prov:wasGeneratedBy:
      '@type': prov:Activity
      dct:type: manual-download
    schema:
      fields:
        - name: respondent_id
          type: integer
        - name: region
          type: string
        - name: score
          type: number

outputs:
  - title: Survey Summary
    name: survey-summary
    path: outputs/survey_summary.csv
    schema:
      fields:
        - name: region
          type: string
        - name: mean_score
          type: number
        - name: respondent_count
          type: integer

Inputs need a source: block to record provenance. Outputs get their lineage tracked automatically when you write data using sunstone.pandas.

docs.title: Single Package
docs.text:
For projects that produce one data package, use the singular package: key with a top-level publish: block:

min_sunstone_version: 1.20.0
package:
  title: Regional Survey Results
  description: Aggregated survey scores by region.
  version: "1.0.0"
  licenses:
    - name: CC-BY-4.0
  keywords:
    - survey
    - regional-statistics
  contributors:
    - title: Data Team
      roles:
        - creator

publish:
  enabled: true
  to: gs://my-bucket/datasets/survey-results/

inputs:
  - title: Raw Survey Data
    name: raw-survey-data
    path: inputs/survey_raw.csv
    # ... fields, source, etc.

outputs:
  - title: Survey Summary
    name: survey-summary
    path: outputs/survey_summary.csv
    # ... fields

When you run sunstone package build, all outputs are bundled into a single datapackage.json. When you run sunstone package push, everything is uploaded to the publish.to destination.

docs.title: Publish options
docs.text: Field Description enabled Set to true to enable publishing. to Destination URL (e.g. gs://bucket/path/, s3://bucket/path/). gs:// needs sunstone-py[gcs]; s3:///r2:// need sunstone-py[s3]. Supports ${VAR} expansion. as Optional public URL base. If set, resource paths in datapackage.json use this instead of the upload URL. flatten If true, strip subdirectories from file paths when uploading (e.g. outputs/data.csv becomes data.csv).

docs.title: Multiple Packages
docs.text:
When a project produces datasets that should be published as separate packages (different audiences, licenses, or destinations), use the plural packages: key:

min_sunstone_version: 1.20.0
packages:
  - name: survey-public
    title: Public Survey Results
    description: Anonymized regional aggregates.
    version: "1.0.0"
    licenses:
      - name: CC-BY-4.0
    datasets:
      - survey-summary
    publish:
      enabled: true
      to: gs://public-bucket/survey/

  - name: survey-internal
    title: Internal Survey Data
    description: Full survey data with respondent details.
    version: "1.0.0"
    datasets:
      - survey-summary
      - survey-detailed
    publish:
      enabled: true
      to: gs://internal-bucket/survey/

inputs:
  - title: Raw Survey Data
    name: raw-survey-data
    path: inputs/survey_raw.csv
    # ...

outputs:
  - title: Survey Summary
    name: survey-summary
    path: outputs/survey_summary.csv
    # ...

  - title: Survey Detailed
    name: survey-detailed
    path: outputs/survey_detailed.csv
    # ...

docs.title: Key differences from single package
docs.text:
• Each entry must have name and datasets.
  • datasets is a list of dataset names referencing entries in inputs: or outputs:. All names are validated at load time.
  • Each entry has its own publish: block — there is no top-level publish: (this is enforced).
  • You cannot use both package: and packages: in the same file.
  • A dataset name can appear in multiple packages.

docs.title: Build output
docs.text:
With multiple packages, sunstone package build creates one file per package:

datapackage.json        # first package
datapackage.1.json      # second package

docs.title: Push behavior
docs.text: sunstone package push iterates over each package that has publish.enabled: true and uploads its datasets and datapackage.json to the configured destination.

docs.title: Package Metadata
docs.text:
Both package: and packages: entries support the same metadata fields:

Field Type Description title string Human-readable package title. description string Longer description (supports multiline YAML). version string Semantic version (e.g. "1.0.0"). licenses list SPDX licenses, e.g. [{name: CC-BY-4.0}]. keywords list Search keywords. contributors list People or organizations (each with title, optional roles, path, email). homepage string URL to project homepage. id string Globally unique identifier (URI, DOI, etc.). image string URL to a representative image.

docs.title: Putting It All Together
docs.text:
A typical project lifecycle:

  1. Define inputs with source provenance in datasets.yaml.
  2. Write your analysis using sunstone.pandas — lineage is tracked automatically.
  3. Define outputs with field schemas.
  4. Add package configuration (package: or packages:).
  5. Validate: sunstone dataset validate
  6. Build locally: sunstone package build
  7. Publish: sunstone package push --yes

docs.title: Minimal complete example
docs.text:
min_sunstone_version: 1.20.0
package:
  title: UN Member States
  version: "1.0.0"
  licenses:
    - name: CC-BY-4.0

publish:
  enabled: true
  to: gs://my-bucket/datasets/un-members/

inputs:
  - title: Official UN Member States
    name: official-un-member-states
    path: inputs/un_member_states_raw.csv
    source:
      title: United Nations
      dcat:downloadURL: https://example.org/member_states.csv
      dct:publisher:
        rdfs:label: United Nations
      dct:license: CC-BY-NC-3.0-IGO
    prov:generatedAtTime: '2025-10-08'
    prov:wasGeneratedBy:
      '@type': prov:Activity
      dct:type: manual-download
    schema:
      fields:
        - name: Member State
          type: string
        - name: ISO Code
          type: string

outputs:
  - title: Current UN Member States
    name: current-un-member-states
    path: outputs/current_un_member_states.csv
    schema:
      fields:
        - name: Country
          type: string
        - name: ISO Code
          type: string
        - name: Date of Admission
          type: date

Run the workflow:

# Run your analysis script
uv run python create_un_members_dataset.py

# Validate
sunstone dataset validate

# Build the datapackage.json locally
sunstone package build

# Push to cloud storage
sunstone package push --yes

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Data Package is a comprehensive data standard and data definition language (DDL) designed to improve data management, sharing, and interoperability. Version 2 of the standard provides a modernized framework for describing datasets that enhances the findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability (FAIR) of data.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Create a standardized framework for describing datasets
  • Provide a simple yet extensible data definition language
  • Enable structured data packaging and delivery
  • Facilitate easier data discovery and integration
  • Support comprehensive dataset documentation

docs.title: Design Philosophy
docs.text:
• Simple: Easy to understand and implement
  • Extensible: Can be customized for specific use cases
  • Language-agnostic: Works across different programming languages
  • Interoperable: Compatible with existing data standards
  • FAIR-focused: Promotes best practices in data management

docs.title: Adoption
docs.text: The Data Package standard is used by major organizations including: - European Commission - GitHub - GBIF (Global Biodiversity Information Facility) - Dryad - And many research institutions worldwide

docs.title: Software Support
docs.text: Open-source tools and libraries are available for multiple languages including Python, JavaScript, R, and more.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The Data Package v2 standard consists of four core specifications that work together:

  1. Data Package: Container format for describing a coherent collection of data
  2. Data Resource: Format for describing individual data files or sources
  3. Table Schema: Detailed description of tabular data structure
  4. Table Dialect: Specification for how tabular data is physically stored

docs.title: Descriptor
docs.text: A descriptor is a JSON object that contains metadata about a data package, resource, or schema. Descriptors can: - Be stored in JSON files (e.g., datapackage.json) - Include custom properties using namespace:propertyName convention - Reference profiles for validation

docs.title: Profile
docs.text: A profile is a URL that: - Resolves to a valid JSON Schema descriptor - Is versioned and immutable - Serves as a metadata version identifier - Enables validation of descriptors

docs.title: Tabular Data
docs.text: Tabular data consists of: - Rows with consistent fields - Optional header row defining field names - Multiple possible formats (CSV, Excel, JSON, databases, etc.)

docs.title: Data Representation
docs.text:
• Physical representation: How data appears in files (text, binary, etc.)
  • Logical representation: "Ideal" data with defined types and structures

docs.title: 1. Data Package Specification
docs.text: A Data Package is a simple container format for describing a coherent collection of data in a single package.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• MUST have a descriptor file (preferably named datapackage.json)
  • MUST include at least one resource
  • Descriptor contains metadata about the package and its resources

docs.title: Required Properties
docs.text: • resources (array): List of data resources (REQUIRED)

docs.title: Recommended Properties
docs.text:
• name: Unique, human-readable identifier (lowercase alphanumeric)
  • id: Globally unique identifier (UUID, DOI, etc.)
  • licenses: Licensing information
  • profile: Profile URL for validation

docs.title: Standard Properties
docs.text: Property Type Description $schema string Profile URL (default: https://datapackage.org/profiles/2.0/datapackage.json) name string Unique identifier, invariant across updates id string Globally unique identifier title string Human-readable title description string Detailed description (supports Markdown) version string Semantic version created string Creation datetime (ISO 8601) homepage string URL to package homepage licenses array License objects sources array Raw data source objects contributors array Contributor objects keywords array Search keywords image string Representative image URL resources array Data resource objects (REQUIRED)

docs.title: Example: Minimal Data Package
docs.text:
{
  "name": "my-package",
  "resources": [
    {
      "name": "my-data",
      "path": "data.csv"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Example: Complete Data Package
docs.text:
{
  "$schema": "https://datapackage.org/profiles/2.0/datapackage.json",
  "name": "gdp-data",
  "title": "A nice title",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "created": "1985-04-12T23:20:50.52Z",
  "licenses": [
    {
      "name": "ODC-PDDL-1.0",
      "path": "http://opendatacommons.org/licenses/pddl/",
      "title": "Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License v1.0"
    }
  ],
  "sources": [
    {
      "title": "World Bank and OECD",
      "path": "http://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.CD"
    }
  ],
  "contributors": [
    {
      "title": "Joe Bloggs",
      "email": "[email protected]",
      "path": "http://www.bloggs.com",
      "roles": ["creator"]
    }
  ],
  "resources": [
    {
      "name": "gdp",
      "path": "data/gdp.csv",
      "type": "table",
      "schema": {
        "fields": [
          {
            "name": "country",
            "type": "string"
          },
          {
            "name": "year",
            "type": "integer"
          },
          {
            "name": "gdp",
            "type": "number"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
A typical Data Package directory structure:

my-package/
├── datapackage.json
├── README.md
├── data/
│   ├── mydata.csv
│   └── otherdata.csv
└── scripts/
    └── process.py

docs.title: 2. Data Resource Specification
docs.text: A Data Resource describes and packages a single data resource, such as an individual table or file.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Provide a locator for data with optional rich metadata.

docs.title: Required Properties
docs.text: • name: Unique identifier within the package (lowercase alphanumeric)

docs.title: Data Location (one required)
docs.text:
• path: URL or file system path to data file(s)
  • data: Inline data representation

docs.title: Recommended Properties
docs.text:
• type: Resource type (e.g., table for tabular data)
  • title: Human-readable label
  • description: Detailed description
  • format: File extension (e.g., csv, json, xlsx)
  • mediatype: MIME type (e.g., text/csv)
  • encoding: Character encoding (e.g., utf-8)

docs.title: Tabular Data Properties
docs.text: When type is table: - schema: Table Schema describing structure - dialect: Table Dialect describing physical format

docs.title: Path Property
docs.text:
The path property can be: - A single file: "path": "data.csv" - Multiple files: "path": ["data1.csv", "data2.csv"] - A URL: "path": "http://example.com/data.csv" - A relative POSIX path: "path": "data/myfile.csv"

Security restrictions: - Cannot use absolute paths (/path/to/file) - Cannot use parent paths (../file) - Cannot reference hidden folders

docs.title: Example: Basic Resource
docs.text:
{
  "name": "solar-system",
  "path": "http://example.com/solar-system.csv",
  "title": "The Solar System",
  "format": "csv",
  "mediatype": "text/csv",
  "encoding": "utf-8"
}

docs.title: Example: Tabular Resource with Schema
docs.text:
{
  "name": "population",
  "type": "table",
  "path": "data/population.csv",
  "title": "Population Data",
  "format": "csv",
  "schema": {
    "fields": [
      {
        "name": "country",
        "type": "string"
      },
      {
        "name": "population",
        "type": "integer"
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: Example: Inline Data
docs.text:
{
  "name": "countries",
  "data": [
    {"code": "US", "name": "United States"},
    {"code": "GB", "name": "United Kingdom"},
    {"code": "NO", "name": "Norway"}
  ]
}

docs.title: Example: Multiple Files
docs.text:
{
  "name": "annual-reports",
  "path": [
    "data/2020.csv",
    "data/2021.csv",
    "data/2022.csv"
  ],
  "format": "csv"
}

docs.title: 3. Table Schema Specification
docs.text: Table Schema is a format for declaring schemas for tabular data, providing type checking and validation capabilities.

docs.title: Core Properties
docs.text: Property Type Description fields array Field descriptors (REQUIRED) $schema string Profile URL missingValues array Defines how missing values are represented primaryKey string/array Unique row identifier(s) foreignKeys array Links between tables

docs.title: Field Properties
docs.text:
Each field in the fields array has:

Property Type Description name string Field name (REQUIRED) type string Data type (recommended) format string Specific format for the type title string Human-readable title description string Field description example any Example value constraints object Validation rules categories array Categorical values with labels categoriesOrdered boolean Whether categories have order

docs.title: Field Types
docs.text: Type Description Example string Text data "Hello World" number Decimal numbers 3.14, -42.5 integer Whole numbers 42, -17 boolean True/false true, false date Calendar date 2024-01-15 datetime Date and time 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z time Time of day 10:30:00 year Year 2024 yearmonth Year and month 2024-01 duration Time duration P1Y2M (ISO 8601) geopoint Geographic coordinates [45.5231, -122.6765] geojson GeoJSON geometry {...} object JSON object {"key": "value"} array JSON array [1, 2, 3] any Unspecified/mixed type any value

docs.title: Field Constraints
docs.text: Constraint Type Description required boolean Field cannot be null unique boolean All values must be unique minLength integer Minimum string length maxLength integer Maximum string length minimum number Minimum value maximum number Maximum value pattern string Regular expression validation enum array Restrict to specific values

docs.title: Example: Basic Table Schema
docs.text:
{
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "id",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    {
      "name": "name",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "name": "price",
      "type": "number"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Example: Schema with Constraints
docs.text:
{
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "id",
      "type": "integer",
      "constraints": {
        "required": true,
        "unique": true
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "email",
      "type": "string",
      "format": "email",
      "constraints": {
        "required": true
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "price",
      "type": "integer",
      "constraints": {
        "minimum": 100,
        "maximum": 150,
        "required": true
      }
    }
  ],
  "primaryKey": "id"
}

docs.title: Example: Categories
docs.text:
Categories allow you to define labeled values, useful for coded data:

{
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "fruit",
      "type": "integer",
      "categories": [
        {"value": 0, "label": "apple"},
        {"value": 1, "label": "orange"},
        {"value": 2, "label": "banana"}
      ],
      "categoriesOrdered": true
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Example: Foreign Keys
docs.text:
Foreign keys create relationships between tables:

{
  "resources": [
    {
      "name": "population-by-state",
      "schema": {
        "fields": [
          {"name": "state-code", "type": "string"},
          {"name": "population", "type": "integer"}
        ],
        "foreignKeys": [
          {
            "fields": ["state-code"],
            "reference": {
              "resource": "state-codes",
              "fields": ["code"]
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "state-codes",
      "schema": {
        "fields": [
          {"name": "code", "type": "string"},
          {"name": "name", "type": "string"}
        ],
        "primaryKey": "code"
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Example: Missing Values
docs.text:
Define how missing or null values are represented:

{
  "fields": [
    {"name": "temperature", "type": "number"},
    {"name": "notes", "type": "string"}
  ],
  "missingValues": [
    {"value": "", "label": "OMITTED"},
    {"value": "-99", "label": "REFUSED"},
    {"value": "N/A", "label": "NOT_APPLICABLE"}
  ]
}

docs.title: 4. Table Dialect Specification
docs.text: Table Dialect describes how tabular data is physically stored in a file, supporting various formats like CSV, TSV, JSON, Excel, and databases.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Define parsing rules for tabular data files
  • Ensure data interoperability across different formats
  • Provide configuration for delimiters, quotes, line terminators, etc.

docs.title: Standard Properties
docs.text: Property Type Default Description $schema string - Profile URL header boolean true Whether first row contains field names headerRows array [1] Row numbers containing headers delimiter string , Field delimiter character lineTerminator string \r\n Row separator quoteChar string " Quote character doubleQuote boolean true Whether quotes are escaped by doubling escapeChar string - Escape character (alternative to doubleQuote) skipInitialSpace boolean false Ignore whitespace after delimiter commentChar string - Comment line prefix caseSensitiveHeader boolean false Whether header names are case-sensitive

docs.title: Supported Formats
docs.text: The Table Dialect specification supports: - Delimited formats: CSV, TSV, pipe-delimited - Structured formats: JSON, YAML - Spreadsheets: Excel (.xlsx, .xls), OpenOffice (.ods) - Databases: SQL tables, query results

docs.title: Example: Semicolon-Delimited CSV
docs.text:
{
  "delimiter": ";",
  "quoteChar": "'",
  "header": true
}

docs.title: Example: Tab-Delimited with Comments
docs.text:
{
  "delimiter": "\t",
  "lineTerminator": "\n",
  "commentChar": "#",
  "header": true
}

docs.title: Example: No Header Row
docs.text:
{
  "header": false,
  "delimiter": ",",
  "quoteChar": "\""
}

docs.title: Example: Custom Quote Escaping
docs.text:
{
  "delimiter": ",",
  "quoteChar": "\"",
  "doubleQuote": false,
  "escapeChar": "\\"
}

docs.title: Example: Multiline Headers
docs.text:
{
  "headerRows": [1, 2],
  "delimiter": ","
}

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Table Dialect focuses on formatting, not data types or schema
  • Character encoding is handled separately (not part of dialect)
  • Backward compatible with the older "CSV Dialect" specification
  • Orthogonal to Table Schema (they work together but are independent)

docs.title: Complete Example: Multi-Resource Package
docs.text:
Here's a comprehensive example showing all specifications working together:

datapackage.json:

{
  "$schema": "https://datapackage.org/profiles/2.0/datapackage.json",
  "name": "population-and-cities",
  "title": "Country Population and Major Cities",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Population data by country with major cities information",
  "created": "2024-01-15T10:00:00Z",
  "licenses": [
    {
      "name": "CC-BY-4.0",
      "title": "Creative Commons Attribution 4.0",
      "path": "https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/"
    }
  ],
  "contributors": [
    {
      "title": "Data Team",
      "email": "[email protected]",
      "roles": ["author", "maintainer"]
    }
  ],
  "keywords": ["population", "demographics", "cities"],
  "resources": [
    {
      "name": "countries",
      "type": "table",
      "path": "data/countries.csv",
      "title": "Country Population Data",
      "format": "csv",
      "mediatype": "text/csv",
      "encoding": "utf-8",
      "dialect": {
        "delimiter": ",",
        "header": true,
        "quoteChar": "\""
      },
      "schema": {
        "fields": [
          {
            "name": "country_code",
            "type": "string",
            "title": "ISO Country Code",
            "constraints": {
              "required": true,
              "unique": true,
              "pattern": "^[A-Z]{2}$"
            }
          },
          {
            "name": "country_name",
            "type": "string",
            "title": "Country Name",
            "constraints": {
              "required": true
            }
          },
          {
            "name": "population",
            "type": "integer",
            "title": "Total Population",
            "constraints": {
              "minimum": 0
            }
          },
          {
            "name": "area_km2",
            "type": "number",
            "title": "Area in km²"
          },
          {
            "name": "last_updated",
            "type": "date"
          }
        ],
        "primaryKey": "country_code",
        "missingValues": [
          {"value": "", "label": "NOT_PROVIDED"},
          {"value": "N/A", "label": "NOT_APPLICABLE"}
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "cities",
      "type": "table",
      "path": "data/cities.csv",
      "title": "Major Cities",
      "format": "csv",
      "schema": {
        "fields": [
          {
            "name": "city_id",
            "type": "integer",
            "constraints": {
              "required": true,
              "unique": true
            }
          },
          {
            "name": "city_name",
            "type": "string",
            "constraints": {
              "required": true
            }
          },
          {
            "name": "country_code",
            "type": "string",
            "constraints": {
              "required": true,
              "pattern": "^[A-Z]{2}$"
            }
          },
          {
            "name": "population",
            "type": "integer",
            "constraints": {
              "minimum": 0
            }
          },
          {
            "name": "coordinates",
            "type": "geopoint",
            "title": "City Coordinates"
          }
        ],
        "primaryKey": "city_id",
        "foreignKeys": [
          {
            "fields": ["country_code"],
            "reference": {
              "resource": "countries",
              "fields": ["country_code"]
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "regions",
      "title": "World Regions Lookup",
      "data": [
        {"code": "EU", "name": "Europe"},
        {"code": "AS", "name": "Asia"},
        {"code": "AF", "name": "Africa"},
        {"code": "NA", "name": "North America"},
        {"code": "SA", "name": "South America"},
        {"code": "OC", "name": "Oceania"}
      ],
      "schema": {
        "fields": [
          {"name": "code", "type": "string"},
          {"name": "name", "type": "string"}
        ],
        "primaryKey": "code"
      }
    }
  ]
}

This example demonstrates: - Multiple resources (CSV files and inline data) - Complete metadata (licenses, contributors, keywords) - Detailed table schemas with various field types - Constraints and validation rules - Primary and foreign keys for referential integrity - Table dialect specification for CSV parsing - Missing value definitions

docs.title: Custom Properties
docs.text:
Descriptors can include custom properties using namespace conventions:

{
  "name": "my-package",
  "myorg:internal_id": "12345",
  "myorg:department": "research",
  "resources": [ ]
}

docs.title: Resource Caching
docs.text:
The _cache property provides fallback locations when primary data sources are unavailable:

{
  "name": "remote-data",
  "path": "https://example.com/data.csv",
  "_cache": "cache/data.csv"
}

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
Specify custom profiles for validation:

{
  "profile": "https://example.com/profiles/custom-package.json",
  "name": "my-package",
  "resources": [ ]
}

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
1. FAIR Data Principles: Enhances findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability
  2. Self-Describing: Metadata travels with data
  3. Validation: Schemas enable automatic validation
  4. Standardization: Consistent format across organizations
  5. Documentation: Built-in comprehensive metadata
  6. Versioning: Track changes and evolution
  7. Relationships: Foreign keys enable data linking
  8. Type Safety: Strong typing for data fields

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Research Data Management: Package research datasets with complete provenance
  • Open Data Publishing: Government and public sector data sharing
  • Data Integration: ETL pipelines with standardized formats
  • Data Catalogs: Build searchable data repositories
  • Data Quality: Validate data against schemas
  • Collaborative Projects: Share data with clear documentation
  • Archival: Long-term data preservation with metadata

docs.title: Tools and Software
docs.text:
The Data Package ecosystem includes:

  • Open Data Editor: Visual tool for creating and editing data packages
  • Frictionless Framework (Python): Create, validate, and transform packages
  • JavaScript libraries: Browser and Node.js support
  • R packages: Integration with R workflows
  • Command-line tools: Automation and scripting

docs.title: Comparison with v1
docs.text:
Data Package v2 builds on v1 with improvements including:

  • Enhanced Table Schema with categories and ordered categories
  • More flexible missing values with labels
  • Table Dialect specification (evolved from CSV Dialect)
  • Better profile system for validation
  • Improved foreign key definitions
  • Extended metadata properties

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Official Website: https://datapackage.org/
  • Specifications:
  • Data Package: https://datapackage.org/standard/data-package/
  • Data Resource: https://datapackage.org/standard/data-resource/
  • Table Schema: https://datapackage.org/standard/table-schema/
  • Table Dialect: https://datapackage.org/standard/table-dialect/
  • GitHub: https://github.com/frictionlessdata
  • Open Knowledge Foundation: https://okfn.org/

docs.title: Related Standards
docs.text: Data Package v2 is inspired by and compatible with: - DataCite - Zenodo - DCAT (Data Catalog Vocabulary) - CKAN - Schema.org

docs.title: datasets.yaml key reference
docs.text:
Generated by scripts/gen_schemas.py from src/sunstone/vocab/. Do not edit by hand.

Every key is one of: a Data Package 2.0 property (dp) for its level, a sunstone config key (config), a JSON-LD keyword (jsonld), or an RDF property (rdf: prefix:local or an absolute IRI). RDF properties are allowed at every level; the rows marked rdf below are the ones a rule asks for. Rule levels follow RFC 2119 (MUST, SHOULD, MAY).

Editor support: add # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://sunstoneinstitute.github.io/sunstone-py/schemas/datasets.schema.json as the first line of datasets.yaml.

docs.title: Agents and identifiers
docs.text:
Agent objects (dct:publisher, each dct:creator entry) carry rdfs:label (full name), optional skos:altLabel (short name) and optional "@id" (IRI). Repeat an agent within one file with a YAML anchor: dct:publisher: &fao {rdfs:label: ..., skos:altLabel: FAO} on first use, dct:publisher: *fao after. Anchors do not cross include files.

A source with a DOI puts it in "@id": "@id": https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aqrep.2022.101316.

docs.title: Document
docs.text:
Path: .

Key Class Rule Description Example min_sunstone_version config MUST Minimum sunstone-py version for this project min_sunstone_version: "1.20.0" dcat-si:methodology rdf SHOULD The document describing the method actually applied to produce a dataset or data package: sources, acquisition, processing and limitations. Unlike prov:hadPlan, it is documentation of what was done, not a plan of intent attached to an activity. Unlike schema:measurementTechnique, it covers the whole resource, not the measurement of one variable. dcat-si:methodology: METHODOLOGY.md defaults config MAY Values applied to every dataset (rdfPrefixes and RDF properties) defaults: ... include config MAY YAML files whose inputs, outputs and packages are merged in include: [data/extra.yaml] inputs config MAY Input datasets (list) inputs: ... lint config MAY Lint configuration (disable) lint: ... outputs config MAY Output datasets (list) outputs: ... package config MAY Single package metadata package: ... packages config MAY Package definitions (list) packages: ... plugins config MAY Per-plugin configuration, keyed by plugin name plugins: ... publish config MAY Publish destination for the single package publish: ... rdfPrefixes config MAY Prefix to namespace map rdfPrefixes: {ex: https://example.org/ns#}

docs.title: Dataset
docs.text:
Path: inputs / outputs

Key Class Rule Description Example licenses dp MUST Licenses (list of {name, path, title}) licenses: [{name: CC-BY-4.0}] name dp MUST Identifier, lowercase kebab-case name: un-member-states path dp MUST File path relative to the descriptor, or URL path: inputs/un_members.csv prov:generatedAtTime rdf MUST The time at which an entity was completely created and is available for use. prov:generatedAtTime: '2026-01-02' prov:wasGeneratedBy rdf MUST How the data was obtained: a prov:Activity node, e.g. {dct:type: manual-download}. prov:wasGeneratedBy: {'@type': prov:Activity, dct:type: manual-download} title dp MUST Human-readable title title: Official UN Member States dcat:theme rdf SHOULD A main category of the resource. A resource can have multiple themes. dcat:theme: https://sunstone.institute/rdf/threats#01 dct:spatial rdf SHOULD Spatial characteristics of the resource. dct:spatial: Norway dct:temporal rdf SHOULD Temporal characteristics of the resource. dct:temporal: '2020/2024' description dp SHOULD Description, Markdown allowed description: One row per member state. source config SHOULD Single upstream source of an input; emitted as Data Package sources[0]. Use source in datasets.yaml, not the Data Package sources array. source: {title: ..., dcat:downloadURL: ...} $schema dp MAY Profile URL of this resource $schema: ... bytes dp MAY Size of the file in bytes bytes: ... data dp MAY Inline data instead of path data: ... dcat:keyword rdf MAY A keyword or tag describing a resource. dcat:keyword: [aquaculture, salmon] dct:accrualPeriodicity rdf MAY The frequency with which items are added to a collection. dct:accrualPeriodicity: ... dct:conformsTo rdf MAY An established standard to which the described resource conforms. dct:conformsTo: ... dct:language rdf MAY A language of the resource. dct:language: ... dct:references rdf MAY A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise pointed to by the described resource. dct:references: ... dct:source rdf MAY A related resource from which the described resource is derived. dct:source: ... dct:subject rdf MAY A topic of the resource. dct:subject: ... dialect dp MAY Table dialect (delimiter, quoteChar, header, ...) dialect: ... encoding dp MAY Character encoding (utf-8) encoding: ... format dp MAY File format (csv, json, parquet, ...) format: ... hash dp MAY Content hash (sha256:...) hash: ... homepage dp MAY Home page URL homepage: ... mediatype dp MAY Media type (text/csv) mediatype: ... prov:wasQuotedFrom rdf MAY An entity is derived from an original entity by copying, or 'quoting', some or all of it. prov:wasQuotedFrom: un-member-states publish config MAY Per-dataset publish settings: enabled, as_name, public, dialect (to, flatten and as are deprecated) publish: ... rdfPrefixes config MAY Prefix to namespace map for this dataset rdfPrefixes: ... rdfs:seeAlso rdf MAY Further information about the subject resource. rdfs:seeAlso: ... schema dp MAY Table schema (fields, primaryKey, ...) schema: {fields: [...], primaryKey: id} sources dp MAY Raw sources (list of {title, path, email, version}) sources: ... strict config MAY Strict mode: lineage cannot change strict: ... type dp MAY Resource type (table) type: ...

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
Path: inputs.source

Key Class Rule Description Example @id jsonld MUST (one of) JSON-LD identifier of the node. On a source: the DOI as https://doi.org/, or another persistent IRI. "@id": https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aqrep.2022.101316 dcat:downloadURL rdf MUST (one of) The URL of the downloadable file in a given format. E.g. CSV file or RDF file.
