"""RDF format handler (Turtle, N-Triples, JSON-LD) for AssetKind.GRAPH.

rdflib is imported lazily inside read() to keep import time down.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import PurePosixPath
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, BinaryIO
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from .asset import AssetKind

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .handlers_meta import ContentDescriptor

# short format -> (rdflib format name, media type)
_FORMATS: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {
    "ttl": ("turtle", "text/turtle"),
    "nt": ("nt", "application/n-triples"),
    "jsonld": ("json-ld", "application/ld+json"),
}
_ALIASES = {
    "turtle": "ttl",
    "ntriples": "nt",
    "n-triples": "nt",
    "json-ld": "jsonld",
    "text/turtle": "ttl",
    "application/n-triples": "nt",
    "application/ld+json": "jsonld",
}


class RdfFormatHandler:
    __sunstone_handler_protocol__ = 2

    def supports_native_metadata_extraction(self) -> bool:
        return False

    def supports_sunstone_metadata_embedding(self) -> bool:
        return False

    def supports_metadata(self) -> bool:
        return False

    def supported_kinds(self) -> tuple:
        return (AssetKind.GRAPH,)

    def _resolve_format(self, path: str, format: str | None) -> str | None:
        if format is not None:
            key = format.lower().lstrip(".")
            key = _ALIASES.get(key, key)
            return key if key in _FORMATS else None
        parsed = urlparse(path)
        file_path = parsed.path if parsed.scheme else path
        suffix = PurePosixPath(file_path).suffix.lower().lstrip(".")
        return suffix if suffix in _FORMATS else None

    def can_read(self, path: str, format: str | None) -> bool:
        return self._resolve_format(path, format) is not None

    def can_write(self, path: str, format: str | None) -> bool:
        return self._resolve_format(path, format) is not None

    def read(self, stream: BinaryIO, **kwargs: object) -> Any:
        import rdflib

        from .asset import Asset
        from .lineage import Metadata

        fmt = self._resolve_format(str(kwargs.pop("path", None) or ""), kwargs.pop("format", None)) or "ttl"  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        kwargs.pop("dialect", None)
        rdflib_format, media_type = _FORMATS[fmt]

        raw = stream.read()
        graph = rdflib.Graph()
        graph.parse(data=raw.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(raw, bytes) else raw, format=rdflib_format)
        return Asset(payload=graph, kind=AssetKind.GRAPH, metadata=Metadata(), extras={"media_type": media_type})

    def write(self, asset: object, stream: BinaryIO, **kwargs: object) -> None:
        fmt = self._resolve_format(str(kwargs.pop("path", None) or ""), kwargs.pop("format", None)) or "ttl"  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        kwargs.pop("dialect", None)
        graph: Any = asset.as_graph() if hasattr(asset, "as_graph") else asset
        stream.write(graph.serialize(format=_FORMATS[fmt][0], encoding="utf-8"))

    def content_descriptors(self) -> tuple["ContentDescriptor", ...]:
        from .handlers_meta import ContentDescriptor

        return tuple(ContentDescriptor(content_type=media, content_encoding=None) for _, media in _FORMATS.values())

    def extensions(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return tuple(f".{ext}" for ext in _FORMATS)

"""Client side of `sunstone package push` to `sunstone:` namespaces.

sunstone-py builds a PushPackage and hands it to a PackagePushHandler plugin,
which talks to the data-platform push API. See docs/sunstone-push.md.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Mapping

SEGMENT_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$")
PUSH_ZONES = ("projects", "shared")
_SCHEME = "sunstone:"


class PushError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a package cannot be pushed to a sunstone: namespace."""


def sanitize_segment(value: str) -> str:
    """Map a datasets.yaml slug to a URL path segment ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)."""
    segment = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_]+", "_", value).strip("_")
    if not segment:
        raise PushError(f"Cannot derive a dataset name from {value!r}; set publish.as_name")
    if not re.match(r"[A-Za-z_]", segment):
        segment = "_" + segment
    return segment


def parse_namespace(destination: str) -> str:
    """Validate a `sunstone:<zone>/<path>` destination and return `<zone>/<path>`."""
    if not destination.startswith(_SCHEME):
        raise PushError(f"Namespace destinations start with sunstone:, got {destination!r}")
    if destination.startswith(_SCHEME + "//"):
        raise PushError("sunstone: URLs have no host form; use sunstone:<zone>/<namespace>")
    path = destination[len(_SCHEME) :].strip("/")
    if "@" in path:
        raise PushError("publish.to names a namespace; drop the @ref and use --branch")
    segments = path.split("/")
    for segment in segments:
        if not SEGMENT_RE.match(segment):
            raise PushError(
                f"Invalid namespace segment {segment!r} in {destination}: segments match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*"
            )
    zone = segments[0]
    if zone == "ext":
        raise PushError("The ext/ zone is written only by 'sunstone data import'; package push to ext/ is refused")
    if zone not in PUSH_ZONES:
        raise PushError(f"Unknown zone {zone!r}: publish.to must start with projects/ or shared/")
    if len(segments) < 2:
        raise PushError("publish.to must name a namespace below the zone, e.g. sunstone:projects/my_study")
    return "/".join(segments)


def normalize_branch(name: str) -> str:
    """Normalize a git branch name to a data-platform branch name (01-graph-sor section 2.2)."""
    if not name:
        raise PushError("Branch name is empty")
    branch = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "-", name)
    branch = re.sub(r"-{2,}", "-", branch)
    if not re.match(r"[A-Za-z_]", branch):
        branch = "_" + branch
    return branch[:128]


def default_branch(project_path: Path, environ: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> str:
    """Return the push branch: GITHUB_HEAD_REF, GITHUB_REF_NAME, then the current git branch.

    Never falls back to main.
    """
    env = os.environ if environ is None else environ
    for var in ("GITHUB_HEAD_REF", "GITHUB_REF_NAME"):
        value = env.get(var)
        if value:
            return normalize_branch(value)
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "symbolic-ref", "--short", "-q", "HEAD"],
            cwd=project_path,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
        ).stdout.strip()
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        out = ""
    if not out:
        raise PushError(
            "Cannot determine the target branch (no git branch, GITHUB_HEAD_REF or GITHUB_REF_NAME). Pass --branch."
        )
    return normalize_branch(out)

git symbolic-ref works on a fresh repo with no commits and fails on a detached HEAD, which is what we want.

import hashlib
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import pandas as pd

from sunstone.asset import AssetKind
from sunstone.lineage import DatasetMetadata, PublishConfig
from sunstone.push import build_push_package


def _manager(root: Path) -> MagicMock:
    m = MagicMock()
    m.project_path = root
    m.get_absolute_path.side_effect = lambda loc: root / loc
    return m


def _ds(slug: str, location: str, **kw) -> DatasetMetadata:
    return DatasetMetadata(name=slug.title(), slug=slug, location=location, dataset_type="output", **kw)


def _meta(ds, kind, media_type):
    return {"name": ds.slug, "kind": kind.value, "mediatype": media_type}


def _build(tmp_path, datasets, **kw):
    staging = tmp_path / "staging"
    staging.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    return build_push_package(
        "sunstone:projects/my_study",
        datasets,
        _manager(tmp_path),
        PublishConfig(enabled=True, to="sunstone:projects/my_study", public=True, dialect={"delimiter": ";"}),
        _meta,
        {"name": "my-study", "title": "My study"},
        staging,
        **kw,
    )


def test_csv_becomes_parquet_table(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "out").mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "out" / "emissions.csv").write_text("country,value\nNO,1\nSE,2\n")

    pkg = _build(tmp_path, [_ds("co2-emissions", "out/emissions.csv")])

    assert pkg.namespace == "projects/my_study"
    assert pkg.public is True
    assert pkg.dialect == {"delimiter": ";"}
    assert pkg.metadata["title"] == "My study"

    assert res.slug == "co2-emissions"
    assert res.name == "co2_emissions"

    assert res.path.suffix == ".parquet"
    assert res.media_type == "application/vnd.apache.parquet"
    assert res.metadata["mediatype"] == "text/csv"
    assert pd.read_parquet(res.path)["value"].tolist() == [1, 2]
    assert res.sha256 == hashlib.sha256(res.path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    assert res.size == res.path.stat().st_size

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .datasets import DatasetsManager
    from .lineage import DatasetMetadata, PublishConfig
    from .plugins import PluginRegistry

ResourceMetadataFn = Callable[["DatasetMetadata", AssetKind, str], Optional[dict[str, Any]]]

_MEDIA_TYPES = {
    ".parquet": "application/vnd.apache.parquet",
    ".csv": "text/csv",
    ".tsv": "text/tab-separated-values",
    ".ttl": "text/turtle",
    ".nt": "application/n-triples",
    ".jsonld": "application/ld+json",
    ".geojson": "application/geo+json",
    ".topojson": "application/json",
}


def media_type_for(path: Path) -> str:
    """Media type for a file to upload, from its extension."""
    return _MEDIA_TYPES.get(path.suffix.lower()) or mimetypes.guess_type(path.name)[0] or "application/octet-stream"


def resource_kind(ds: "DatasetMetadata", registry: "PluginRegistry") -> AssetKind:
    """AssetKind of a dataset, from the format handler that reads it."""
    handler = registry.find_format_reader(ds.location, ds.format)
    if handler is None:
        raise PushError(
            f"No format handler for '{ds.slug}' ({ds.location}). "
            "GeoJSON/TopoJSON needs sunstone-py[geo]."
        )
    kinds = tuple(handler.supported_kinds()) if hasattr(handler, "supported_kinds") else (AssetKind.TABULAR,)
    return kinds[0]


def _sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def _dataset_name(ds: "DatasetMetadata") -> str:
    as_name = ds.publish.as_name if ds.publish else None
    if as_name:
        if not SEGMENT_RE.match(as_name):
            raise PushError(f"publish.as_name {as_name!r} on '{ds.slug}' must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
        return as_name
    return sanitize_segment(ds.slug)


def _to_parquet(source: Path, ds: "DatasetMetadata", registry: "PluginRegistry", staging_dir: Path) -> Path:
    """Write a tabular dataset as Parquet for upload. Parquet sources are used as-is."""
    if source.suffix.lower() == ".parquet":
        return source
    handler = registry.find_format_reader(source, ds.format)
    assert handler is not None  # resource_kind() already resolved it
    with open(source, "rb") as f:
        result = handler.read(f, path=source.as_posix(), format=ds.format, dialect=ds.dialect)
    df = result.payload if hasattr(result, "payload") else result  # legacy handlers return a DataFrame
    out = staging_dir / f"{ds.slug}.parquet"
    df.to_parquet(out, index=False)
    return out


def build_push_package(
    destination: str,
    datasets: list["DatasetMetadata"],
    manager: "DatasetsManager",
    publish_config: "PublishConfig",
    resource_metadata_fn: ResourceMetadataFn,
    package_metadata: dict[str, Any],
    staging_dir: Path,
    *,
    allow_outside_project: bool = False,
) -> PushPackage:
    """Resolve datasets into a PushPackage: one resource per dataset, tables as Parquet."""
    from .packaging import _validate_path_containment, is_lfs_pointer
    from .plugins import PluginRegistry

    namespace = parse_namespace(destination)
    project_root = manager.project_path.resolve()
    registry = PluginRegistry.get(manager.project_path)
    resources: list[PushResource] = []
    names: dict[str, str] = {}

    for ds in datasets:
        if not allow_outside_project:
            _validate_path_containment(ds.location, project_root, context=f"dataset '{ds.slug}' location")
        source = manager.get_absolute_path(ds.location)
        if source.is_dir():
            raise PushError(f"Directory stores are not supported by namespace push yet: '{ds.slug}' ({ds.location})")
        if is_lfs_pointer(source):
            raise PushError(f"{ds.location} is a Git LFS pointer. Run 'git lfs pull' before pushing.")

        name = _dataset_name(ds)
        if name in names:
            raise PushError(
                f"Datasets '{names[name]}' and '{ds.slug}' both map to {namespace}/{name}; set publish.as_name"
            )
        names[name] = ds.slug

        kind = resource_kind(ds, registry)
        metadata = resource_metadata_fn(ds, kind, media_type_for(source))
        if metadata is None:
            continue
        upload = _to_parquet(source, ds, registry, staging_dir) if kind is AssetKind.TABULAR else source
        resources.append(
            PushResource(
                slug=ds.slug,
                name=name,
                path=upload,
                kind=kind,
                media_type=media_type_for(upload),
                sha256=_sha256(upload),
                size=upload.stat().st_size,
                metadata=metadata,
            )
        )

    if not resources:
        raise PushError(f"No resources to push to {destination}")
    return PushPackage(
        destination=destination,
        namespace=namespace,
        resources=tuple(resources),
        metadata=package_metadata,
        public=publish_config.public,
        dialect=publish_config.dialect,
    )

Behavior: 1. --env is a free string, default prod. When it is dev or prod, the CLI keeps setting SUNSTONE_PUBLIC_DATASETS_FOLDER as today. For namespace pushes it sets SUNSTONE_DATA_ENV=<env> before calling the plugin, so sunstone env config selects the deployment. 2. For each destination group: if a PackagePushHandler claims it, push through the plugin. Else if it starts with sunstone:, fail with an install hint. Else use the blob store, which needs --yes when --env prod. 3. --branch (normalized) or default_branch() is resolved only for plugin pushes.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _PushRun:
    """Options shared by every destination group in one `package push`."""

    env: str
    branch: Optional[str]
    yes: bool
    force: bool
    replace: bool
    allow_outside_project: bool


def _namespace_resource_metadata(
    manager: DatasetsManager, publish_config: PublishConfig
) -> "Callable[[DatasetMetadata, AssetKind, str], Optional[dict[str, Any]]]":
    from .asset import AssetKind

    def build(ds: DatasetMetadata, kind: AssetKind, media_type: str) -> Optional[dict[str, Any]]:
        if kind is AssetKind.TABULAR:
            return build_resource_dict(ds, manager, publish_config)
        data_path = manager.get_absolute_path(ds.location)
        return _build_non_frictionless_resource_dict(ds, manager, publish_config, data_path, media_type)

    return build


def push_group_to_namespace(
    handler: Any,
    dest_url: str,
    datasets: list[DatasetMetadata],
    manager: DatasetsManager,
    project_slug: str,
    publish_config: PublishConfig,
    run: _PushRun,
    package_entry: Optional[PackageEntry] = None,
) -> None:
    """Push a group of datasets to a sunstone: namespace through a PackagePushHandler plugin."""
    import tempfile

    from .push import PushError, PushOptions, build_push_package, default_branch, normalize_branch

    try:
        branch = normalize_branch(run.branch) if run.branch else default_branch(manager.project_path)
    except PushError as e:
        typer.echo(f"Error: {e}", err=True)
        sys.exit(1)

    if package_entry:
        package_metadata = _package_metadata_to_dict(package_entry.metadata)
    else:
        pkg_meta = manager.get_package_metadata()
        package_metadata = _package_metadata_to_dict(pkg_meta) if pkg_meta else {}
    package_metadata = {"name": package_entry.name if package_entry and package_entry.name else project_slug, **package_metadata}
    top_level_props = manager.get_top_level_custom_properties()
    if top_level_props:
        rdf_prefixes = {**STANDARD_RDF_PREFIXES, **manager.get_default_rdf_prefixes()}
        package_metadata.update(expand_custom_properties(top_level_props, rdf_prefixes))

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="sunstone-push-") as staging:
        try:
            package = build_push_package(
                dest_url,
                datasets,
                manager,
                publish_config,
                _namespace_resource_metadata(manager, publish_config),
                package_metadata,
                Path(staging),
                allow_outside_project=run.allow_outside_project,
            )
        except (PushError, PathTraversalError) as e:
            typer.echo(f"Error: {e}", err=True)
            sys.exit(1)
        os.environ["SUNSTONE_DATA_ENV"] = run.env
        options = PushOptions(env=run.env, branch=branch, yes=run.yes, force=run.force, replace=run.replace)
        result = handler.push(package, options)

    for status in result.datasets:
        line = f"{package.namespace}/{status.name}: {status.status}"
        if status.iri:
            line += f" {status.iri}"
        if status.message:
            line += f" ({status.message})"
        typer.echo(line)
    if not result.ok:
        typer.echo(f"Error: push {result.push_id} to {dest_url}@{branch} failed", err=True)
        sys.exit(1)
    typer.echo(f"✓ Pushed {len(package.resources)} dataset(s) to {dest_url}@{branch} (push {result.push_id})")


def _push_destination(
    dest_url: str,
    datasets: list[DatasetMetadata],
    manager: DatasetsManager,
    project_slug: str,
    publish_config: PublishConfig,
    run: _PushRun,
    package_entry: Optional[PackageEntry] = None,
) -> None:
    """Send one destination group to a push plugin if one claims it, else to the blob store."""
    from .plugins import PluginRegistry

    handler = PluginRegistry.get(manager.project_path).find_package_push_handler(dest_url)
    if handler is not None:
        push_group_to_namespace(
            handler, dest_url, datasets, manager, project_slug, publish_config, run, package_entry
        )
        return
    if dest_url.startswith("sunstone:"):
        typer.echo(
            f"Error: no plugin handles {dest_url}. Install the sunstone-data plugin to push to sunstone: namespaces.",
            err=True,
        )
        sys.exit(1)
    if run.env == "prod" and not run.yes:
        typer.echo(f"Error: pushing to the prod blob store ({dest_url}) needs --yes", err=True)
        sys.exit(1)
    push_group_to_blob_store(
        dest_url,
        datasets,
        manager,
        project_slug,
        publish_config,
        allow_outside_project=run.allow_outside_project,
        package_entry=package_entry,
    )

@package_app.command("push")
def package_push(
    env: str = typer.Option("prod", "--env", help="Target environment, as configured with 'sunstone env'"),
    datasets_file: str = typer.Option("datasets.yaml", "-f", "--file", help="Path to datasets.yaml"),

    ),

    force: bool = typer.Option(
        False, "--force", help="Allow force operations (incompatible schema, version overwrite, deletes)"
    ),
    replace: bool = typer.Option(False, "--replace", help="Retract metadata not in this push (a force operation)"),
    allow_outside_project: bool = typer.Option(

"""dcat-si:methodology is defined in rdf/data.ttl (sunstone-py reads it from here)."""

from rdflib import OWL, RDF, RDFS, Graph, Literal, URIRef

DCAT_SI = "https://sunstone.institute/rdf/data#"
METHODOLOGY = URIRef(DCAT_SI + "methodology")
DCAT_RESOURCE = URIRef("http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#Resource")
FOAF_DOCUMENT = URIRef("http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/Document")
FOAF_PAGE = URIRef("http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/page")
DATA_ONTOLOGY = URIRef("https://sunstone.institute/rdf/data")


def _graph(repo_root) -> Graph:
    g = Graph()
    g.parse(repo_root / "rdf" / "data.ttl", format="turtle")
    return g


def test_methodology_is_an_object_property(repo_root):
    g = _graph(repo_root)
    assert (METHODOLOGY, RDF.type, OWL.ObjectProperty) in g


def test_methodology_has_english_label_and_comment(repo_root):
    g = _graph(repo_root)
    assert g.value(METHODOLOGY, RDFS.label) == Literal("methodology", lang="en")
    comment = g.value(METHODOLOGY, RDFS.comment)
    assert isinstance(comment, Literal) and comment.language == "en" and len(str(comment)) > 20


def test_methodology_domain_and_range(repo_root):
    g = _graph(repo_root)
    assert g.value(METHODOLOGY, RDFS.domain) == DCAT_RESOURCE
    assert g.value(METHODOLOGY, RDFS.range) == FOAF_DOCUMENT


def test_methodology_is_a_foaf_page(repo_root):
    g = _graph(repo_root)
    assert (METHODOLOGY, RDFS.subPropertyOf, FOAF_PAGE) in g


def test_methodology_is_defined_by_data_ontology(repo_root):
    g = _graph(repo_root)
    assert g.value(METHODOLOGY, RDFS.isDefinedBy) == DATA_ONTOLOGY


def test_methodology_comment_distinguishes_neighbours(repo_root):
    comment = str(_graph(repo_root).value(METHODOLOGY, RDFS.comment))
    assert "prov:hadPlan" in comment and "schema:measurementTechnique" in comment


def test_methodology_not_in_vocab_namespace_of_data_ttl(repo_root):
    """data.ttl must not redeclare vocab:methodology; only the dcat-si term lives here."""
    g = _graph(repo_root)
    assert (URIRef("https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#methodology"), None, None) not in g

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy sunstone-py's generated datasets.yaml key reference into the dataset skill.

Usage:
    scripts/sync-dataset-reference.py [--sunstone-py ~/git/sunstone/sunstone-py] [--dest PATH] [--check]

Exit codes: 0 written or current, 1 stale (--check), 2 source missing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DEFAULT_SRC = Path.home() / "git" / "sunstone" / "sunstone-py"
DEFAULT_DEST = REPO / "plugins" / "sunstone-core" / "skills" / "dataset" / "references" / "datasets-yaml-reference.md"
REL = Path("docs") / "datasets-yaml-reference.md"


def _version(sunstone_py: Path) -> str:
    text = (sunstone_py / "pyproject.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    m = re.search(r'^version\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', text, re.MULTILINE)
    return m.group(1) if m else "unknown"


def render(sunstone_py: Path) -> str:
    body = (sunstone_py / REL).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    header = (
        f"<!-- Synced from sunstone-py {_version(sunstone_py)} {REL.as_posix()} "
        "by scripts/sync-dataset-reference.py. Do not edit. -->\n"
    )
    return header + body


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--sunstone-py", default=str(DEFAULT_SRC))
    ap.add_argument("--dest", default=str(DEFAULT_DEST))
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    src = Path(args.sunstone_py)
    if not (src / REL).exists():
        print(f"error: {src / REL} not found", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    dest = Path(args.dest)
    text = render(src)
    if args.check:
        current = dest.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if dest.exists() else ""
        if current == text:
            print(f"{dest} is current")
            return 0
        print(f"{dest} is stale; run scripts/sync-dataset-reference.py", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    dest.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {dest}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

The capture rule requires, on the source: `title`; `dct:publisher` as an object with `rdfs:label`; a link (`dcat:downloadURL` for a file, `dcat:landingPage` for a page, or `"@id"` for a DOI); `dct:license`. On the dataset: `prov:generatedAtTime` and `prov:wasGeneratedBy` with `dct:type`. Add `skos:altLabel` on the publisher, `dct:issued` and `dct:modified` when the publisher's page shows them. A publication (paper, report) is written as in "Restructuring sources" below. Check with:


The capture is done only when that command prints no violations.
  • [ ] Step 2: Add the key loop

Insert a new section immediately after the "## Platform quick reference" section (before "## The capture rule"):

## Writing keys in datasets.yaml

Every key in `datasets.yaml` is one of three things: a Data Package 2.0 property for its level (`title`, `name`, `path`, `schema`, `licenses`, ...), a sunstone config key (`inputs`, `source`, `publish`, `rdfPrefixes`, ...), or an RDF property written as `prefix:local` (`dct:publisher`, `prov:wasAttributedTo`, `si:unit`). Nothing else is allowed, and `sunstone lint` reports any other key as R301.

Never invent a key. To record a concept that has no key in [datasets-yaml-reference.md](references/datasets-yaml-reference.md):

```bash
sunstone vocab search "<concept>" --at <path> --json   # e.g. --at inputs.source, --at outputs.schema.fields
sunstone vocab search --at inputs.source                # every allowed key at that level, with its rule level
```

Pick a result from the output (the first hit is usually right; prefer `dct`, `dcat`, `prov` over `schema`, and `si` only for sunstone-specific concepts). Use its `curie` as the key. If no result fits, leave the concept out and tell the user; do not write a key the search did not return.

A key may take an object value when the property points at a thing with its own properties:

```yaml
prov:wasGeneratedBy:
  '@type': prov:Activity
  dct:type: manual-download
```

Keys inside the object follow the same rules (`@id` and `@type` are also allowed).

Projects created before sunstone-py 1.20 use older keys (`slug`, `location`, `fields`, `attributedTo`, `acquiredAt`, ...). They still load, with one `FutureWarning` per file. Run `sunstone migrate` once to rewrite `datasets.yaml`, its include files and `datasets.lock.yaml`; it keeps comments, moves a DOI from `location.*` to `"@id"`, keeps the old `attributedTo` text as `prov:wasAttributedTo`, and reports keys it cannot map, each with suggestions from `sunstone vocab search`. It never splits free text: that is the next section.

## Restructuring sources

Most existing sources are free text: `title` holds a whole citation and `prov:wasAttributedTo` mixes authors, affiliation and publisher. sunstone-py 2.0 requires every source to carry its parts, and `sunstone lint` reports what is missing (R102 is an error, R311 a warning, R315 an error). Do this once per project, source by source:

1. Run `sunstone lint --json` and collect every violation whose `path` starts with `inputs[...].source`.
2. For each source, read `title` and `prov:wasAttributedTo` and split them into parts. Put each part under its key; never leave a part in two places.

| Part | Key | Example |
|---|---|---|
| DOI or persistent IRI | `"@id"` | `"@id": https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aqrep.2022.101316` |
| Work title only | `title` | `title: Utilization of feed resources in the production of Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) in Norway` |
| Publisher | `dct:publisher` | `{rdfs:label: Elsevier}`; `{rdfs:label: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, skos:altLabel: FAO}` |
| Authors | `dct:creator` | `[{rdfs:label: 'Aas, T. S.'}, {rdfs:label: 'Asgard, T. E.'}]` |
| Year | `dct:issued` | `'2022'` |
| Journal, volume, pages | `dct:isPartOf` | `{rdfs:label: 'Aquaculture Reports 26, 101316'}` |
| Full citation as published | `dct:bibliographicCitation` | the citation string, when the publisher gives one |
| Links | `dcat:downloadURL`, `dcat:landingPage` | the file, the page; never a `doi.org` URL |
| License | `dct:license` | SPDX id |

3. Keep the original `prov:wasAttributedTo` text until every part is placed, then delete it (it is MAY, so keeping it is not an error; deleting it keeps the file short).
4. Define each agent once per file. On the first use write `dct:publisher: &fao` followed by the object; on every later use in the same file write `dct:publisher: *fao`. Include files anchor their own agents.
5. Rerun `sunstone lint --json --warnings-as-errors`. Done when no violation has a `path` under `source`.

A statistics release has a publisher and no authors; a paper has authors and a publisher (the journal's publisher, not the authors' institution). When a part is not known, leave the key out; do not guess a year or an author.

Before, from a real project:

```yaml
    source:
      title: Mottet, de Haan, Falcucci, Tempio, Opio & Gerber (2017), Livestock: On our plates or eating at our table? A new analysis of the feed/food debate, Global Food Security 14, 1-8
      dcat:landingPage: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gfs.2017.01.001
      prov:wasAttributedTo: Mottet, A.; de Haan, C.; Falcucci, A.; Tempio, G.; Opio, C.; Gerber, P. (FAO); published by Elsevier in Global Food Security
      dct:license: CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0
```

After:

```yaml
    source:
      "@id": https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gfs.2017.01.001
      title: "Livestock: On our plates or eating at our table? A new analysis of the feed/food debate"
      dct:publisher: &elsevier
        rdfs:label: Elsevier
      dct:creator:
        - rdfs:label: Mottet, A.
        - rdfs:label: de Haan, C.
        - rdfs:label: Falcucci, A.
        - rdfs:label: Tempio, G.
        - rdfs:label: Opio, C.
        - rdfs:label: Gerber, P.
      dct:issued: '2017'
      dct:isPartOf:
        rdfs:label: Global Food Security 14, 1-8
      dct:license: CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0
```

The next Elsevier paper in the same file writes `dct:publisher: *elsevier`.

**Attributes (Python names; the YAML keys differ):**
- `name` (str): Source title (YAML `title`)
- `location` (SourceLocation): `.data` (`dcat:downloadURL`), `.about` (`dcat:landingPage`), `.metadata` (`rdfs:seeAlso`), `.access` (`dcat:accessURL`)
- `id` (str | None): YAML `"@id"` (DOI as `https://doi.org/<doi>`, or another IRI)
- `attributed_to` (str | Agent): YAML `prov:wasAttributedTo` (legacy free text; empty string when absent)
- `acquired_at` (str | None): dataset `prov:generatedAtTime`
- `acquisition_method` (str | None): dataset `prov:wasGeneratedBy.dct:type`
- `license` (str | None): `dct:license`
- `publisher` (SourceAgent | None): `dct:publisher`; `SourceAgent(label, alt_label=None, id=None)` maps `rdfs:label`, `skos:altLabel`, `"@id"`
- `creator` (list[SourceAgent] | None): `dct:creator`
- `issued`, `updated`, `bibliographic_citation` (str | None): `dct:issued`, `dct:modified`, `dct:bibliographicCitation`
- `is_part_of` (dict | None): `dct:isPartOf` node as written, e.g. `{"rdfs:label": "Aquaculture Reports 26"}`

Function signatures (slug: str, location: str, license: Optional[str]) are Python parameter names and stay unchanged. Add one sentence under add_output_dataset: "Writes the entry in the new key form (title, name, path, schema.fields, licenses)."

  • [ ] Step 3: troubleshooting.md

Rewrite every datasets.yaml snippet to the new form: slug: → name:, location: → path:, name: (human-readable) → title:; update the prose next to them ("Typo in slug" → "Typo in name", grep "slug:" datasets.yaml → grep "name:" datasets.yaml, "Verify the slug matches exactly" → "Verify the name matches exactly"). The indentation example near line 415 becomes name: dataset-name # 4 spaces (item properties). Lines 472–488 (duplicate-slug examples) use name:. Lines 528–537 (absolute vs relative) use path:. Keep the minimum-version lines at 1.13 only in the "Verify installation" step if they refer to the data-platform plugin; otherwise raise them to 1.20 to match SKILL.md.

Add a troubleshooting entry at the end of the file:

## Lint reports R301 "unknown key"

The key is not a Data Package property, a config key or an RDF property. Either it is an old sunstone key (run `sunstone migrate`), or it is invented. Find the right key:

```bash
sunstone vocab search "<what the key means>" --at <path from the violation, without [n]>
```

Use a returned `curie` as the key. R302 means the prefix is not declared: add it under `rdfPrefixes:` or use a standard prefix (`dct`, `dcat`, `prov`, `schema`, `skos`, `rdfs`, `qudt`, `si`, `dcat-si`). R303 means the term does not exist in that vocabulary: search again and pick a listed term.

## Lint reports R102, R311 or R315 on a source

The source is still free text or has a DOI in the wrong key. R102 (error): `dct:publisher` must be an object with `rdfs:label`, and the source needs a link (`"@id"`, `dcat:downloadURL` or `dcat:landingPage`) and `dct:license`; a bare `dct:publisher: Name` from before 1.20 is rewritten to `{rdfs:label: Name}` by `sunstone migrate`. R315 (error): move the `doi.org` URL from `dcat:landingPage`/`dcat:downloadURL` to `"@id"`. R311 (warning): add `skos:altLabel` on the publisher, `dct:issued`, `dct:modified`, and for a paper `dct:creator` and `"@id"`. Follow "Restructuring sources" in SKILL.md; the source is done when `sunstone lint --json --warnings-as-errors` reports nothing under its path.

## The same publisher appears many times

Write the object once with an anchor and reuse it with an alias in the same file:

```yaml
      dct:publisher: &ssb
        rdfs:label: Statistics Norway
        skos:altLabel: SSB
# later, in the same file
      dct:publisher: *ssb
```

Anchors do not cross include files; each include file anchors its own. Saving through sunstone keeps anchors and aliases as written.

docs.title: Datapackage Conformance (sunstone-cms, C12) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: The CMS import reads the new IRI keys that sunstone-py 1.20 emits in datapackage.json (methodology, field unit/source, structured source parts) while keeping the old keys as fallbacks, stores the source parts on tableSources, and renders a source at three levels of detail (compact, standard, full) with the templates from sunstone-cms issue #610.

Architecture: Four pure functions already isolate the key matching: extractSchema and extractTableSources in src/collections/DataPackages/endpoints/import.ts, toSourceRecords in src/utilities/datasets/sourcesFromSchemaFields.ts, and getMethodology in src/services/data/methodology-service.ts. Each gains the new IRI with the old key as fallback. toSourceRecords stores every part of a source (identifier, title, publisher full and short name, creators, year, container, citation, links, license, legacy attribution) as plain keys on a DatasetSourceRecord; a new module renderSource.ts turns a record into display text at a chosen level, and normalizeSources / resolveDatasetSources call it, so every existing consumer (Sources, DownloadLink, the visual embeds) keeps receiving { title, url }. A new exported methodologyFilenameOf lifts the package-level methodology lookup out of runImport so it is testable. All new values land in existing json columns; no DB migration.

Tech Stack: TypeScript, Payload CMS 3, Vitest (npx vitest run <file>), ESLint (npm run lint), npx tsc --noEmit for type checking.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-datapackage-conformance-design.md in sunstone-py (sections "Source references", "C12. sunstone-cms" and "C5. Write hook" for the emitted keys) and sunstone-cms issue #610 (gh issue view 610 -R sunstoneinstitute/sunstone-cms) for the render templates. #610 is a draft the author may still edit; this plan follows its text as of 2026-10-16 (field table, three levels, templates, fallbacks). Re-read the issue before Task 3b and apply any edits to the templates there, not to the stored parts.

docs.title: Spec conflicts and open questions
docs.text:
• SC1. No old key exists for source attribution or license. Spec C12.3 says "each keeping the old key as a fallback", but sunstone-py never emitted an attribution or license key on datapackage.json sources (only title, path, dcat:*, dct:publisher). Resolution: read the IRIs only; plain attributedTo/license on a source object stay ignored (the existing test "reads a singular source object with a name and location" pins that).
  • SC2. MethodologyResponse.sources shape changes on the public endpoint. /api/data/data-package/:slug/methodology returns sources in the old datasets.yaml shape (name, location, attributedTo). No frontend component renders it (DataPackageTabs.tsx declares the type, uses only resources). Resolution: change the response to DatasetSourceRecord[] as the spec says, update the frontend type and context/data-api.md. A consumer renders the full level with renderSource(record, 'full').
  • SC3. #610 question 3 (store parts, or rendered strings per level) is open. Resolution: store the parts on tableSources (no migration, jsonb) and render at display time, which is what C12.3 says. If the author answers "rendered strings", add the three strings next to the parts at import time in Task 3b; nothing else changes. Flagged in the PR.
  • SC4. #610 question 1 (where each level is used) is open, and the CMS has no dataset page. Pages today: datapackages/[slug] (resources list through DownloadLink), visual embeds (Sources component), the methodology endpoint. Resolution: the resources list and the embeds render compact; the methodology endpoint returns records (full is rendered by whoever displays them); standard is implemented and tested but wired nowhere until a dataset page exists. Flagged in the PR.
  • SC5. {link} order in #610 differs from the CMS's sourceLink. #610: @id, landing page, download URL, path. sourceLink today: url, landing page, path, download URL, location. Resolution: records follow #610 (id, landingPage, downloadURL, path, then legacy url/location); field-level sources (toDatasetSource, not restructured by sunstone-py) keep today's order. Every existing normalizeSources test still passes because its fixtures have path === downloadURL or only one of them.

docs.title: Source record shape (Task 3) and render levels (Task 3b)
docs.text:
DatasetSourceRecord after Task 3 (all optional; undefined keys are dropped before storage):

Key From datapackage.json #610 part id @id Identifier (DOI) title title, else name Work title publisher dct:publisher node rdfs:label; legacy string or {name|title} Publisher full name publisherShort dct:publisher node skos:altLabel Publisher short name publisherId dct:publisher node @id (kept, not rendered) creators dct:creator list, each node's rdfs:label (strings accepted) Authors issued dct:issued (string or number, stored as string) Year container dct:isPartOf node rdfs:label (string accepted) Container citation dct:bibliographicCitation Full citation attribution prov:wasAttributedTo string, or node rdfs:label Legacy attribution license dct:license License url, path, landingPage, downloadURL, location as today Links

A record is kept when it has at least one of title, publisher, creators, attribution. toSourceRecords is idempotent on stored records (it reads its own plain keys first).

Templates (from #610, verbatim), [ ... ] is dropped with its punctuation when a placeholder inside is missing:

Level Template Link compact {attribution}[ ({year})] {link} standard {title}[ · {attribution}][, {year}] {link} full citation if present, else {author}.[ ({year}).] {title}.[ {container}.][ {link}] none (the link is in the text)

Placeholders: {creatorsShort} surname of one creator, two joined with &, three or more as first surname + et al.; {creators} all labels joined with ,, the last with &; {publisher} short name else full name; {publisherFull} full name; {attribution} {creatorsShort} when there are creators, else {publisher}; {author} {creators} when present, else {publisherFull}; {year} first four characters of issued; {link} first of id, landingPage, downloadURL, path, url, location.web, location.data, location (string). Fallbacks: no creators and no publisher, compact uses title and standard drops the attribution segment; no title either, every level uses the attribution text; full with no author uses the title as the first segment. Segments are joined without doubling a period (Ytrestoyl, T. + (2022)., not Ytrestoyl, T.. (2022).).

const SI_UNIT = 'https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#unit'

Replace the extractSchema doc comment and body with:

/**
 * Extracts only the allowed schema fields (name, type, description, unit, unitIri,
 * source, label, title) from a Frictionless Data resource schema. `unit` and
 * `source` come from the sunstone IRIs (`vocab#unit`, `vocab#sourceField`,
 * sunstone-py >= 1.20) when present, else the short keys; `source` also falls
 * back to the Dublin Core source. `unitIri` is the QUDT unit (`qudt:hasUnit`).
 * `title` comes from the Dublin Core title when present, else the Frictionless `title`.
 */
export function extractSchema(resource: { schema?: { fields?: DataPackageResourceSchemaField[] } }) {
  if (!resource.schema?.fields) return undefined

  const allowedKeys = ['name', 'type', 'description', 'unit', 'source', 'label'] as const
  return resource.schema.fields.map((field) => {
    const picked: Record<string, unknown> = {}
    for (const key of allowedKeys) {
      if (field[key] !== undefined) {
        picked[key] = field[key]
      }
    }
    if (field[SI_UNIT] !== undefined) {
      picked.unit = field[SI_UNIT]
    }
    if (field[SI_SOURCE_FIELD] !== undefined) {
      picked.source = field[SI_SOURCE_FIELD]
    } else if (picked.source === undefined && field[DC_SOURCE] !== undefined) {
      picked.source = field[DC_SOURCE]
    }
    const unitIri = field[QUDT_HAS_UNIT]
    if (typeof unitIri === 'string' && unitIri.trim()) {
      picked.unitIri = unitIri
    }
    const title = field[DC_TITLE] ?? field.title
    if (typeof title === 'string' && title.trim()) {
      picked.title = title
    }
    return picked
  })
}

  • [ ] Step 4: Implement

In sourcesFromSchemaFields.ts, replace the three constants and sourcePublisher with:

const RDFS_LABEL = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label'
const SKOS_ALT_LABEL = 'http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#altLabel'
const DC_PUBLISHER = 'http://purl.org/dc/terms/publisher'
const DC_CREATOR = 'http://purl.org/dc/terms/creator'
const DC_ISSUED = 'http://purl.org/dc/terms/issued'
const DC_IS_PART_OF = 'http://purl.org/dc/terms/isPartOf'
const DC_BIBLIOGRAPHIC_CITATION = 'http://purl.org/dc/terms/bibliographicCitation'
const DC_LICENSE = 'http://purl.org/dc/terms/license'
const PROV_WAS_ATTRIBUTED_TO = 'http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#wasAttributedTo'
const DCAT_LANDING_PAGE = 'http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#landingPage'
const DCAT_DOWNLOAD_URL = 'http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#downloadURL'

const isNode = (value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> =>
  Boolean(value) && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value)

/**
 * A label from a string, or from a JSON-LD node's `rdfs:label` (legacy
 * objects: `name`, then `title`).
 */
function labelOf(value: unknown): string | undefined {
  if (nonEmptyString(value)) return value
  if (isNode(value)) {
    for (const key of [RDFS_LABEL, 'name', 'title']) {
      const candidate = value[key]
      if (nonEmptyString(candidate)) return candidate
    }
  }
  return undefined
}

const nodeString = (value: unknown, key: string): string | undefined =>
  isNode(value) && nonEmptyString(value[key]) ? value[key] : undefined

const scalarString = (value: unknown): string | undefined =>
  nonEmptyString(value) ? value : typeof value === 'number' ? String(value) : undefined

/** Reads a source's publisher label (Dublin Core `publisher`, else a plain `publisher`). */
function sourcePublisher(source: Record<string, unknown>): string | undefined {
  return labelOf(source[DC_PUBLISHER] ?? source.publisher)
}

(sourceLink, toDatasetSource, dedupeByTitle, normalizeSources, sourcesFromSchemaFields, resolveDatasetSources are unchanged in this task.) Replace toSourceRecords with:

/**
 * Converts a table-level (Frictionless resource) source value — a string, an
 * object, or an array of either — into records for storage: the structured
 * parts sunstone-py emits (identifier, title, publisher full and short name,
 * creators, year, container, citation, legacy attribution, license) and every
 * link, read from the Dublin Core / DCAT / PROV IRIs into plain keys. Reads its
 * own plain keys first, so stored records pass through unchanged. Entries with
 * no title, publisher, creators or attribution are dropped.
 */
export function toSourceRecords(input: unknown): DatasetSourceRecord[] {
  const items = Array.isArray(input) ? input : [input]
  return items.flatMap((item): DatasetSourceRecord[] => {
    if (nonEmptyString(item)) return [{ title: item }]
    if (!isNode(item)) return []
    const source = item
    const { location } = source
    const publisher = source[DC_PUBLISHER] ?? source.publisher
    const publisherLabel = labelOf(publisher)
    const creatorsRaw = source.creators ?? source[DC_CREATOR]
    const creators = (Array.isArray(creatorsRaw) ? creatorsRaw : creatorsRaw === undefined ? [] : [creatorsRaw])
      .map(labelOf)
      .filter(nonEmptyString)
    const record: DatasetSourceRecord = {
      id: [source.id, source['@id']].find(nonEmptyString),
      title: [source.title, source.name].find(nonEmptyString),
      publisher: publisherLabel,
      // Short name and IRI only make sense next to a label; a node without rdfs:label is ignored whole.
      publisherShort: publisherLabel ? [source.publisherShort, nodeString(publisher, SKOS_ALT_LABEL)].find(nonEmptyString) : undefined,
      publisherId: publisherLabel ? [source.publisherId, nodeString(publisher, '@id')].find(nonEmptyString) : undefined,
      creators: creators.length > 0 ? creators : undefined,
      issued: [source.issued, source[DC_ISSUED]].map(scalarString).find(nonEmptyString),
      container: [source.container, labelOf(source[DC_IS_PART_OF])].find(nonEmptyString),
      citation: [source.citation, source[DC_BIBLIOGRAPHIC_CITATION]].find(nonEmptyString),
      attribution: [source.attribution, labelOf(source[PROV_WAS_ATTRIBUTED_TO])].find(nonEmptyString),
      license: [source.license, source[DC_LICENSE]].find(nonEmptyString),
      url: [source.url].find(nonEmptyString),
      path: [source.path].find(nonEmptyString),
      landingPage: [source[DCAT_LANDING_PAGE], source.landingPage].find(nonEmptyString),
      downloadURL: [source[DCAT_DOWNLOAD_URL], source.downloadURL].find(nonEmptyString),
      location: nonEmptyString(location) || isNode(location) ? (location as DatasetSourceRecord['location']) : undefined,
    }
    if (!record.title && !record.publisher && !record.creators && !record.attribution) return []
    return [Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(record).filter(([, value]) => value !== undefined)) as DatasetSourceRecord]
  })
}

import type { DatasetSource, DatasetSourceRecord, SourceDetail } from '@/types/data-transforms'

/**
 * Renders a stored source record at one of the three levels of detail from
 * sunstone-cms#610:
 *
 *   compact   {attribution}[ ({year})]                         datasets list
 *   standard  {title}[ · {attribution}][, {year}]              dataset page, linked
 *   full      citation, else {author}.[ ({year}).] {title}.[ {container}.][ {link}]
 *
 * A paper is credited to its authors, a statistics release to its publisher.
 * Optional segments are dropped with their punctuation when a placeholder is
 * missing. Fallbacks for sources that have not been restructured: no creators
 * and no publisher, use the title; no title either, use the attribution text.
 */

export interface RenderedSource {
  text: string
  link?: string
}

const nonEmpty = (value: unknown): value is string => typeof value === 'string' && value.trim().length > 0

/** "Aas, T. S." -> "Aas"; "Tor Aas" -> "Aas"; a single word stays as is. */
export function surname(label: string): string {
  const trimmed = label.trim()
  const comma = trimmed.indexOf(',')
  if (comma > 0) return trimmed.slice(0, comma).trim()
  const words = trimmed.split(/\s+/)
  return words[words.length - 1] ?? trimmed
}

/** One surname, two with " & ", three or more as the first plus " et al.". */
export function creatorsShort(creators: string[]): string {
  const names = creators.map(surname)
  if (names.length === 1) return names[0]!
  if (names.length === 2) return `${names[0]} & ${names[1]}`
  return `${names[0]} et al.`
}

/** All labels joined with ", ", the last with " & ". */
export function creatorsLong(creators: string[]): string {
  if (creators.length <= 1) return creators[0] ?? ''
  return `${creators.slice(0, -1).join(', ')} & ${creators[creators.length - 1]}`
}

/** First of @id, landing page, download URL, path, then the legacy url / location keys. */
export function recordLink(record: DatasetSourceRecord): string | undefined {
  const { location } = record
  const candidates = [
    record.id,
    record.landingPage,
    record.downloadURL,
    record.path,
    record.url,
    typeof location === 'object' && location ? location.web : undefined,
    typeof location === 'object' && location ? location.data : undefined,
    typeof location === 'string' ? location : undefined,
  ]
  return candidates.find(nonEmpty)
}

const year = (record: DatasetSourceRecord): string | undefined =>
  nonEmpty(record.issued) ? record.issued.trim().slice(0, 4) : undefined

const publisher = (record: DatasetSourceRecord): string | undefined =>
  [record.publisherShort, record.publisher].find(nonEmpty)

/** {attribution}: authors (short) when present, else the publisher. */
const attribution = (record: DatasetSourceRecord): string | undefined =>
  record.creators && record.creators.length > 0 ? creatorsShort(record.creators) : publisher(record)

/** {author}: all authors when present, else the publisher's full name. */
const author = (record: DatasetSourceRecord): string | undefined =>
  record.creators && record.creators.length > 0 ? creatorsLong(record.creators) : [record.publisher].find(nonEmpty)

/** Adds a trailing period unless the segment already ends with one. */
const sentence = (segment: string): string => (segment.trim().endsWith('.') ? segment.trim() : `${segment.trim()}.`)

function compact(record: DatasetSourceRecord): string {
  const who = attribution(record) ?? [record.title, record.attribution].find(nonEmpty) ?? ''
  const y = year(record)
  return y ? `${who} (${y})` : who
}

function standard(record: DatasetSourceRecord): string {
  const who = attribution(record)
  const title = [record.title].find(nonEmpty)
  if (!title && !who) return [record.attribution].find(nonEmpty) ?? ''
  const head = title ?? who ?? ''
  const withWho = title && who ? `${head} · ${who}` : head
  const y = year(record)
  return y ? `${withWho}, ${y}` : withWho
}

function full(record: DatasetSourceRecord): string {
  if (nonEmpty(record.citation)) return record.citation.trim()
  const who = author(record)
  const title = [record.title, record.attribution].find(nonEmpty)
  const y = year(record)
  const segments = [
    who ? sentence(who) : undefined,
    y ? `(${y}).` : undefined,
    title ? sentence(title) : undefined,
    nonEmpty(record.container) ? sentence(record.container) : undefined,
    recordLink(record),
  ]
  return segments.filter(nonEmpty).join(' ')
}

export function renderSource(record: DatasetSourceRecord, level: SourceDetail): RenderedSource {
  const link = recordLink(record)
  switch (level) {
    case 'compact':
      return link ? { text: compact(record), link } : { text: compact(record) }
    case 'standard':
      return link ? { text: standard(record), link } : { text: standard(record) }
    case 'full':
      return { text: full(record) }
  }
}

/** The `{ title, url? }` shape the `Sources` and `DownloadLink` components read. */
export function toDatasetSourceAt(record: DatasetSourceRecord, level: SourceDetail): DatasetSource {
  const { text, link } = renderSource(record, level)
  return link ? { title: text, url: link } : { title: text }
}

In sourcesFromSchemaFields.ts, add import { toDatasetSourceAt } from './renderSource' and SourceDetail to the type import. Replace normalizeSources and resolveDatasetSources with:

/**
 * Normalises a table-level (Frictionless resource) source value — a string,
 * an object, an array of either, or stored `DatasetSourceRecord`s — into a
 * de-duplicated list of `{ title, url? }` entries rendered at `level`
 * (sunstone-cms#610; compact by default).
 */
export function normalizeSources(input: unknown, level: SourceDetail = 'compact'): DatasetSource[] {
  return dedupeByTitle(toSourceRecords(input).map((record) => toDatasetSourceAt(record, level)))
}

/**
 * Resolves the sources to show for a dataset: an explicit `sources` override
 * wins (returned as-is); otherwise sources are derived from the referenced
 * schema fields, with table-level sources (rendered at `level`) filling in
 * for fields that have no source of their own.
 */
export function resolveDatasetSources({
  override,
  tableSources,
  fields,
  level = 'compact',
}: {
  override?: unknown
  tableSources?: unknown
  fields: SchemaFieldWithSource[] | null | undefined
  level?: SourceDetail
}): DatasetSource[] {
  if (Array.isArray(override) && override.length > 0) return override as DatasetSource[]
  return sourcesFromSchemaFields(fields, normalizeSources(tableSources, level))
}

toDatasetSource (field-level sources) and sourceLink stay for sourcesFromSchemaFields; toDatasetSource's allowTitle parameter is now unused by normalizeSources, so remove the parameter and the allowTitle ? record.title : undefined branch (fields never carry a Frictionless title). Pre-existing normalizeSources tests keep passing: a string source becomes { title } (compact uses the title when there is no publisher), the herbicide fixture renders its publisher label with the landing page link, and the no-landing-page case links to path (which equals its download URL).

import { readFileFromGCS, readJSONFromGCS } from '../../lib/api/gcs-storage'
import { resolveDatasetPath } from '@/utilities/datasets/resolveDatasetPath'
import { toSourceRecords } from '@/utilities/datasets/sourcesFromSchemaFields'
import type { DatasetSourceRecord } from '@/types/data-transforms'
import { logger } from '@/lib/logger'

interface Datapackage {
  sources?: unknown
  [key: string]: unknown
}

// Methodology text + package-level sources only. The downloadable resources are
// fetched separately from the Datasets collection (see the methodology endpoint).
// Sources use the same record shape as dataset `tableSources` (structured parts);
// render them with `renderSource(record, 'full')` for a references list.
export interface MethodologyResponse {
  methodology: string
  sources: DatasetSourceRecord[]
}

export async function getMethodology(
  methodologyUrl: string | null, // path to the METHODOLOGY.md (null if not defined)
  metadataUrl: string, // path to datapackage.json
): Promise<MethodologyResponse> {
  if (!metadataUrl) {
    throw new Error('metadataUrl is required')
  }

  try {
    const methodologyContent = methodologyUrl
      ? await readFileFromGCS(resolveDatasetPath(methodologyUrl))
      : ''
    const datapackage = (await readJSONFromGCS(resolveDatasetPath(metadataUrl))) as Datapackage

    return {
      methodology: methodologyContent,
      sources: datapackage.sources === undefined ? [] : toSourceRecords(datapackage.sources),
    }
  } catch (error) {
    logger.error('Error fetching methodology', error)
    throw new Error(
      `Failed to fetch methodology: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error'}`,
    )
  }
}

Datapackage Conformance (sunstone-py, C1–C9) Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Every key in datasets.yaml, datasets.lock.yaml and generated datapackage.json is a DP 2.0 property, a sunstone config key, or an RDF property from a known vocabulary; old keys are normalized on read, rewritten by sunstone migrate, and agents find terms with sunstone vocab search.

Architecture: A data layer (sunstone/vocab/*.json, generated by scripts/sync_vocab.py) feeds a rule registry (rules.py) and a validator (conformance.py) that walk plain dicts. aliases.py renames old keys to new keys in place on ruamel documents (comments kept) and is shared by the DatasetsManager read hook, lint and sunstone migrate. The write hook (build_datapackage, push_group) emits new keys as expanded IRIs and validates the descriptor. Lint, vocab search and the schema generator are thin consumers of the same data.

Tech Stack: Python 3.12, ruamel.yaml (round-trip), typer, frictionless 5, pint; rdflib only in the vocab dependency group for the sync script.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-datapackage-conformance-design.md (read it first; it is the source of truth).

docs.title: Spec conflicts
docs.text:
Each conflict names the spec text, what the code does today, and the resolution this plan uses.

  • SC1. Skill location. Resolved: the skill is at claude-plugins/plugins/sunstone-core/skills/dataset/ on origin/main (the local checkout was 25 commits behind). Plan 2 must start from an up-to-date origin/main.
  • SC2. In-memory normalization rewrites datasets.yaml on the next save. Spec C4 normalizes aliases in _load ("one model for the rest of the code"). DatasetsManager._save() dumps self._data, so any write (add_output_dataset, set_dataset_strict, _ensure_min_version) writes the new key form. Resolution: accept it. The normalizer is ruamel-aware and keeps comments and order, so a save after load produces exactly what sunstone migrate would. Document in CHANGELOG. The spec's MUST (new-form files set min_sunstone_version >= 1.20.0) is enforced by aliases.ensure_min_version, called from _save() and sunstone migrate, and checked by rule R306. Versions >= 1.8.0 then refuse the file with their existing "requires sunstone-py >= 1.20.0" error.
  • SC3. Lock-file keys are neither DP, config, nor RDF. The config-key list in the spec covers datasets.yaml only. Lock entries use slug, file_hash, data_hash, created_at, sources, activity, field_derivations, context, transformation_params, fields. Resolution: vocab/dp.json carries a lock key list per lock level (entry, source); the extras rule checks lock entries and lock sources against it. Deeper lock structures (activity, field_derivations) are machine-written and not key-checked.
  • SC4. Dataset-level source: block. Not in the spec's config list, not DP (DP has sources, a list), not RDF. Resolution: source is a dataset-level config key (it maps to DP sources[0] on emission).
  • SC5. Package-level license. The alias table covers dataset license → licenses only, but package.license and packages[].license would fail the extras rule. Resolution: alias license → licenses (DP list form) at package level too, same transform. datapackage.json keeps emitting license (existing key) and adds licenses.
  • SC6. Keys emitted today that are not DP 2.0. Resolved by the spec's C5 dual-emission table: package license + licenses, field unit + si:unit IRI (+ qudt:hasUnit), field source + si:sourceField IRI, package vocab#methodology + data#methodology. The table's "resource license" row is the package-level license key (no resource-level license is emitted today; see _package_metadata_to_dict). Mechanism: dp.json has a legacy_emitted allowlist per level, honoured in datapackage scope only while ENFORCE_MUST is False.
  • SC13. Resource scheme is emitted by frictionless and is not in the C5 table. build_resource_dict copies scheme (e.g. file) from frictionless; it is not a DP 2.0 resource property. Proposed resolution: keep it in legacy_emitted for 1.x and strip it in 2.0 together with the C5 left column; add a "resource scheme | (none; 2.0 strips it)" row to the spec table.
  • SC14. Two small additions the spec does not list. (a) The C2 category list has no home for the Methodology rules; the plan adds Category.METHODOLOGY. (b) C9's source order omits sosa; the plan sorts it after qudt, before si. Both are proposed spec edits, not design changes.
  • SC7. R102 severity. The spec makes source title, dcat:downloadURL/dcat:landingPage, prov:wasAttributedTo, dct:license MUST (lint error). R102 ("source block missing required keys") is a WARNING today. Resolution: R102 keeps its ID and becomes MUST (error) with the new key list. R101 (no source block at all) stays SHOULD.
  • SC8. Source.acquired_at, acquisition_method, license are required str. In the new form they come from the dataset (prov:generatedAtTime, prov:wasGeneratedBy.dct:type) and may be absent (R312/R102 report it). Resolution: the three become Optional[str] with no default (field order unchanged, keyword construction unchanged).
  • SC9. YAML dates. ruamel loads acquiredAt: 2025-10-08 as datetime.date; once hoisted to prov:generatedAtTime it reaches json.dumps in datapackage.json. Resolution: the normalizer stringifies date/datetime values of prov:generatedAtTime and dct:modified (isoformat()), and expand_custom_properties converts any remaining date/datetime value the same way.
  • SC11. Resolved: the spec now uses dct:type on the prov:wasGeneratedBy activity node.
  • SC12. R102 and R104 severities. Spec makes source MUST keys and kebab-case name MUST (lint error); both rules are warnings today. They keep their IDs and become errors.
  • SC15. Source.publisher and Source.creator are Optional[str] today. The spec's "Source references" makes dct:publisher an agent object and dct:creator a list of them. Resolution: new dataclass lineage.SourceAgent(label, alt_label=None, id=None); Source.publisher: Optional[SourceAgent], Source.creator: Optional[list[SourceAgent]] (same positions, type change only; nothing in src/ reads them except _parse_source and _source_entry). Source gains id, issued, is_part_of, bibliographic_citation with None defaults, appended after creator.
  • SC16. String-valued dct:publisher / dct:creator. Twelve org sources write dct:publisher: <free text> today, and the old fixtures in this plan did too. The spec now requires an agent object with rdfs:label, and C7 lists only the DOI move and attributedTo as mechanical migrations. Proposed spec addition (C7): sunstone migrate wraps a string dct:publisher into {rdfs:label: <string>} and a string or list-of-strings dct:creator into [{rdfs:label: <string>}, ...]. No text is split, so it is mechanical. Task 2 implements it in normalize_document and reports it as Rename(path, "dct:publisher", "dct:publisher.rdfs:label") (R304 on read, like any alias). Every fixture in this plan writes agents as objects.
  • SC17. YAML anchors for repeated agents. The spec relies on ruamel keeping &fao / *fao across round-trip and on aliases loading as the same object. The coordinator verified both. Consequence for the normalizer: a shared agent object is visited once per use, and since nothing inside an agent object is renamed, repeated visits are harmless. Task 2 and Task 8 pin anchors with tests. Anchors never cross include files; DatasetsManager._merge_includes already loads each include separately, so nothing to do there.
  • SC10. Sync needs network and a rdf-registry checkout. Task 1 downloads eight vocabularies and reads two Turtle files from ~/git/sunstone/rdf-registry, which must be at an origin/main that already contains C11 (dcat-si:methodology in rdf/data.ttl; plan 2026-10-16-datapackage-conformance-rdf-registry.md). If a download fails, the checkout is missing, or dcat-si.json lacks methodology, the task stops and reports; it does not hand-write vocabulary JSON.

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Semantic versioning; this plan is the 1.20.0 minor release scope. ENFORCE_MUST = False. pyproject.toml stays at 1.19.0 until /release bumps it; the version gate in DatasetsManager._load treats the checkout as at least 1.20.0 (Task 4).
  • MUST / MUST NOT violations: one FutureWarning per loaded file on read/write (count, first five with paths, "run sunstone lint for all of them; these become errors in sunstone-py 2.0"), plus one FutureWarning per file with alias keys naming sunstone migrate; lint error. SHOULD: lint warning. MAY: not checked. DeprecationWarning is never used for conformance (Python hides it inside libraries); it stays for deprecated Python APIs only. pyproject.toml has no filterwarnings, so a FutureWarning stays a warning in the test suite.
  • Existing lint IDs R001–R202 keep their numbers. New rules use R3xx.
  • Paths written to files use path.as_posix() (Windows CI).
  • Run tests with uv run pytest --no-cov (add -q). Before each commit: uv run ruff check src/sunstone && uv run ruff format src/sunstone tests scripts && uv run --extra polars mypy src/sunstone.
  • Runtime never fetches vocabularies; rdflib lives in the vocab dependency group only.
  • CHANGELOG entries: one short line each, under ## [Unreleased], categories Added/Changed/Deprecated/Removed/Fixed.
  • Commit messages: conventional prefix (feat:, refactor:, test:, docs:), no Co-authored-by lines.
  • Never remove or change an existing datapackage.json key; add new ones alongside (spec C5 table).
  • A datasets.yaml in new form sets min_sunstone_version to 1.20.0 or higher (aliases.MIN_NEW_FORM_VERSION); every write path raises it, rule R306 checks it.
  • Shipped vocabularies: si, dcat-si, dct, dcat, prov, schema, qudt, rdfs, skos, sosa.
  • Source MUST keys (spec "Provenance"): title; dct:publisher object with rdfs:label; a link ("@id", dcat:downloadURL or dcat:landingPage); dct:license. prov:wasAttributedTo is MAY. A doi.org URL in dcat:downloadURL / dcat:landingPage is MUST NOT (it goes in "@id").
  • Agent object (spec "Source references"): rdfs:label (full name), optional skos:altLabel (short name), optional "@id". Repeated agents use YAML anchors (&fao / *fao) within one file; never a lookup table.
  • Do not widen scope: no refactors outside the files each task names.

Files: - Create: src/sunstone/vocab/__init__.py, src/sunstone/vocab/dp.json, src/sunstone/vocab/aliases.json, scripts/sync_vocab.py - Generate: src/sunstone/vocab/{dct,dcat,prov,schema,skos,rdfs,qudt,sosa,si,dcat-si}.json - Modify: pyproject.toml (package-data, vocab dependency group), src/sunstone/__init__.py:39-54 (add dcat-si prefix) - Test: tests/test_vocab.py

Interfaces: - Produces (used by Tasks 3, 7, 8, 9):

DP_PROFILE_URL: str              # "https://datapackage.org/profiles/2.0/datapackage.json"
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Term: curie: str; iri: str; label: str; definition: str; source: str; levels: tuple[str, ...]
def load_vocab(prefix: str) -> dict[str, Any]          # raw JSON for one shipped vocab
def term_exists(prefix: str, local: str) -> bool
def namespace_of(prefix: str) -> str
def all_terms() -> list[Term]                           # RDF terms + DP keys (source "dp") + config keys (source "config")
def dp_keys(level: str) -> frozenset[str]
def config_keys(level: str) -> frozenset[str]
def lock_keys(level: str) -> frozenset[str]
def legacy_emitted_keys(level: str) -> frozenset[str]

def key_definition(level: str, key: str) -> str         # "" when unknown
def level_children(level: str) -> dict[str, str]
def level_for_path(path: str) -> str | None             # "" -> "document", "inputs.schema.fields" -> "field"
def aliases() -> dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]]        # contents of aliases.json

In pyproject.toml:

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
sunstone = [

and under [dependency-groups] add:

vocab = [
    "rdflib>=7.0",
]

"""Shipped vocabulary data: DP 2.0 property sets, config keys and RDF terms.

All data is read from the JSON files next to this module. Nothing here
touches the network; ``scripts/sync_vocab.py`` regenerates the RDF files.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

_DIR = Path(__file__).parent

SHIPPED_VOCABS: tuple[str, ...] = ("dct", "dcat", "prov", "schema", "skos", "rdfs", "qudt", "sosa", "si", "dcat-si")
"""Vocabularies whose terms are checked for existence (spec: Extras MUST)."""

# YAML level -> DP profile level used for key lookup.
_DP_LEVEL_ALIAS = {"dataset": "resource"}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Term:
    curie: str
    iri: str
    label: str
    definition: str
    source: str
    """Vocabulary prefix, or ``"dp"`` / ``"config"`` for descriptor keys."""
    levels: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    """Levels where a DP/config key is allowed; empty for RDF terms (allowed anywhere)."""


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def _dp() -> dict[str, Any]:
    with open(_DIR / "dp.json", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return json.load(f)


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def aliases() -> dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]]:
    with open(_DIR / "aliases.json", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return json.load(f)


DP_PROFILE_URL: str = _dp()["profile"]


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def load_vocab(prefix: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if prefix not in SHIPPED_VOCABS:
        raise KeyError(prefix)
    with open(_DIR / f"{prefix}.json", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return json.load(f)


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def _locals(prefix: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    ns = load_vocab(prefix)["namespace"]
    return frozenset(t["iri"][len(ns) :] for t in load_vocab(prefix)["terms"])


def namespace_of(prefix: str) -> str:
    return str(load_vocab(prefix)["namespace"])


def term_exists(prefix: str, local: str) -> bool:
    return prefix in SHIPPED_VOCABS and local in _locals(prefix)


def dp_keys(level: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    return frozenset(_dp()["dp"].get(_DP_LEVEL_ALIAS.get(level, level), {}))


def config_keys(level: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    return frozenset(_dp()["config"].get(level, {}))


def lock_keys(level: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    return frozenset(_dp()["lock"].get(level, []))


def legacy_emitted_keys(level: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    return frozenset(_dp()["legacy_emitted"].get(_DP_LEVEL_ALIAS.get(level, level), []))


def recommended_keys(level: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Spec "Recommended properties": key -> "SHOULD" or "MAY" at this level."""
    return dict(_dp()["recommended"].get(level, {}))


def duplicate_keys(level: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Spec "Duplicate properties" (MUST NOT): key -> what to use instead. ``output`` adds to ``dataset``."""
    return dict(_dp()["duplicates"].get(level, {}))


def key_definition(level: str, key: str) -> str:
    dp_level = _DP_LEVEL_ALIAS.get(level, level)
    return str(_dp()["dp"].get(dp_level, {}).get(key) or _dp()["config"].get(level, {}).get(key) or "")


def level_children(level: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    return dict(_dp()["children"].get(level, {}))


def level_for_path(path: str) -> str | None:
    """Resolve a dotted ``datasets.yaml`` path (no array markers) to a level name."""
    level = "document"
    for part in [p for p in path.strip().strip(".").split(".") if p]:
        child = level_children(level).get(part)
        if child is None:
            return None
        level = child
    return level


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def all_terms() -> list[Term]:
    terms: list[Term] = []
    dp = _dp()
    by_key: dict[tuple[str, str], list[str]] = {}
    for kind in ("dp", "config"):
        for level, keys in dp[kind].items():
            for key, definition in keys.items():
                by_key.setdefault((kind, key), []).append(level)
    for (kind, key), levels in sorted(by_key.items()):
        definition = next((dp[kind][lvl][key] for lvl in levels if dp[kind][lvl].get(key)), "")
        terms.append(Term(curie=key, iri="", label=key, definition=definition, source=kind, levels=tuple(levels)))
    for prefix in SHIPPED_VOCABS:
        for t in load_vocab(prefix)["terms"]:
            terms.append(
                Term(curie=t["curie"], iri=t["iri"], label=t.get("label", ""), definition=t.get("definition", ""), source=prefix)
            )
    return terms

"""Regenerate src/sunstone/vocab/<prefix>.json from upstream vocabularies.

Usage:
    uv run --group vocab python scripts/sync_vocab.py [--rdf-registry PATH] [--only PREFIX ...]

Upstream files are pinned below. ``si`` and ``dcat-si`` are read from a local
rdf-registry checkout (default: ~/git/sunstone/rdf-registry).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import rdflib
from rdflib import OWL, RDF, RDFS, SKOS, DCTERMS, Namespace, URIRef

OUT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "src" / "sunstone" / "vocab"

# prefix -> (namespace recorded in JSON, source, rdflib format, extra namespace spellings accepted in the file)
SOURCES: dict[str, tuple[str, str, str, tuple[str, ...]]] = {
    "dct": ("http://purl.org/dc/terms/", "https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/dublin_core_terms.ttl", "turtle", ()),
    "dcat": ("http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#", "https://www.w3.org/ns/dcat.ttl", "turtle", ()),
    "prov": ("http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#", "https://www.w3.org/ns/prov-o.ttl", "turtle", ()),
    "schema": ("http://schema.org/", "https://schema.org/version/latest/schemaorg-current-https.ttl", "turtle", ("https://schema.org/",)),
    "skos": ("http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#", "https://www.w3.org/2009/08/skos-reference/skos.rdf", "xml", ()),
    "rdfs": ("http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#", "https://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema.ttl", "turtle", ()),
    "qudt": ("http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/", "https://qudt.org/3.1.4/schema/qudt.ttl", "turtle", ()),
    "sosa": ("http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/", "https://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/sosa.ttl", "turtle", ()),
    "si": ("https://sunstone.institute/rdf/vocab#", "rdf/vocab.ttl", "turtle", ()),
    "dcat-si": ("https://sunstone.institute/rdf/data#", "rdf/data.ttl", "turtle", ()),
}

PROPERTY_TYPES = {RDF.Property, OWL.ObjectProperty, OWL.DatatypeProperty, OWL.AnnotationProperty, OWL.FunctionalProperty}
LABEL_PREDICATES = (RDFS.label, DCTERMS.title, SKOS.prefLabel)
DEFINITION_PREDICATES = (RDFS.comment, SKOS.definition, DCTERMS.description)


def _first_literal(g: rdflib.Graph, s: URIRef, predicates: tuple) -> str:
    for p in predicates:
        values = [o for o in g.objects(s, p) if isinstance(o, rdflib.Literal)]
        if not values:
            continue
        english = [v for v in values if (v.language or "en").startswith("en")]
        chosen = english[0] if english else values[0]
        return " ".join(str(chosen).split())
    return ""


def build(prefix: str, registry: Path) -> dict:
    namespace, source, fmt, extra_ns = SOURCES[prefix]
    location = str(registry / source) if not source.startswith("http") else source
    g = rdflib.Graph()
    g.parse(location, format=fmt)
    accepted = (namespace,) + extra_ns
    terms: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for s in set(g.subjects(RDF.type, None)):
        if not isinstance(s, URIRef):
            continue
        if not any(t in PROPERTY_TYPES for t in g.objects(s, RDF.type)):
            continue
        iri = str(s)
        ns_hit = next((ns for ns in accepted if iri.startswith(ns)), None)
        if ns_hit is None:
            continue
        local = iri[len(ns_hit) :]
        if not local or "/" in local or "#" in local:
            continue
        terms[local] = {
            "curie": f"{prefix}:{local}",
            "iri": namespace + local,
            "label": _first_literal(g, s, LABEL_PREDICATES),
            "definition": _first_literal(g, s, DEFINITION_PREDICATES),
        }
    return {
        "prefix": prefix,
        "namespace": namespace,
        "source": source,
        "terms": [terms[k] for k in sorted(terms)],
    }


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--rdf-registry", default=str(Path.home() / "git" / "sunstone" / "rdf-registry"))
    ap.add_argument("--only", nargs="*", default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    registry = Path(args.rdf_registry)
    for prefix in args.only or SOURCES:
        data = build(prefix, registry)
        if not data["terms"]:
            print(f"error: no properties found for {prefix}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        out = OUT_DIR / f"{prefix}.json"
        out.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"{prefix}: {len(data['terms'])} terms -> {out.relative_to(OUT_DIR.parent.parent.parent)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Rename: path: str; old: str; new: str      # path = container path, e.g. "inputs[0].source"
@dataclass
class NormalizeResult: renames: list[Rename]; ambiguous: list[str]; new_form: bool = False   # ambiguous = dataset paths with both slug and title; new_form = input used any new-form key before normalization
MIN_NEW_FORM_VERSION: str = "1.20.0"
def make_yaml() -> YAML                           # round-trip YAML with datasets.py settings
def detect_form(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Literal["old", "new", "ambiguous", "untitled"]
def uses_new_form(data: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool  # any new-form key present (spec: MUST set min_sunstone_version)
def version_key(v: str) -> tuple[int, ...]       # "1.20.0" -> (1, 19, 0); non-digits dropped
def ensure_min_version(data: MutableMapping[str, Any], required: str = MIN_NEW_FORM_VERSION) -> bool  # insert/raise min_sunstone_version; True when changed
def normalize_document(data: MutableMapping[str, Any]) -> NormalizeResult   # datasets.yaml or an include file, in place
def normalize_lock(lock: MutableMapping[str, Any]) -> NormalizeResult
def rename_key(m: MutableMapping[str, Any], old: str, new: str, path: str, result: NormalizeResult) -> None
def is_doi_url(value: str) -> bool               # https://doi.org/..., http://doi.org/..., https://dx.doi.org/...
- Besides alias renames, normalize_document makes the mechanical source fixes from spec C7 and SC16: a doi.org URL in old location.data / location.web / location.about moves to the source's "@id" (inserted as the first key; recorded as Rename("<src>.location", "<old>", "@id")), and a string dct:publisher becomes {rdfs:label: <string>} (Rename("<src>", "dct:publisher", "dct:publisher.rdfs:label")); a string or list-of-strings dct:creator becomes a list of {rdfs:label} objects (Rename("<src>", "dct:creator", "dct:creator[].rdfs:label")). A DOI in new-form dcat:downloadURL / dcat:landingPage is not moved; rule R315 reports it.

    name: raw
    path: inputs/raw.csv
    description: Raw rows.
    source:
      title: Example Source
      dcat:downloadURL: https://e.org/raw.csv
      dcat:landingPage: https://e.org
      rdfs:seeAlso: https://e.org/meta.md
      prov:wasAttributedTo: Example Org
      dct:license: CC-BY-4.0
      dct:modified: '2026-01-01'
    prov:generatedAtTime: '2026-01-02'
    prov:wasGeneratedBy:
      '@type': prov:Activity
      dct:type: manual-download
    schema:
      fields:
        - name: gdp
          type: number
          si:unit: USD

outputs:
