    licenses:
      - name: CC-BY-4.0
    schema:
      fields:
        - name: id
          type: string
"""


def _dump(data) -> str:
    import io

    buf = io.StringIO()
    make_yaml().dump(data, buf)
    return buf.getvalue()


def test_normalize_old_form_matches_expected_yaml() -> None:
    data = make_yaml().load(OLD)
    result = normalize_document(data)
    assert _dump(data) == NEW
    assert result.ambiguous == []
    renamed = {(r.path, r.old, r.new) for r in result.renames}
    assert ("inputs[0]", "slug", "name") in renamed
    assert ("inputs[0]", "name", "title") in renamed
    assert ("inputs[0].source", "attributedTo", "prov:wasAttributedTo") in renamed
    assert ("inputs[0].source", "acquiredAt", "prov:generatedAtTime") in renamed
    assert ("inputs[0].source.location", "data", "dcat:downloadURL") in renamed
    assert ("inputs[0].schema.fields[0]", "unit", "si:unit") in renamed
    assert ("package", "license", "licenses") in renamed
    assert ("", "si:methodology", "dcat-si:methodology") in renamed
    assert result.new_form is False


def test_normalize_is_idempotent() -> None:
    data = make_yaml().load(NEW)
    result = normalize_document(data)
    assert result.renames == []
    assert result.new_form is True
    assert _dump(data) == NEW


def test_uses_new_form() -> None:
    assert not uses_new_form(make_yaml().load(OLD))
    assert uses_new_form(make_yaml().load(NEW))
    assert not uses_new_form({"inputs": [{"slug": "x", "name": "X", "location": "a.csv"}]})
    assert uses_new_form({"outputs": [{"name": "x", "title": "X", "path": "a.csv"}]})
    assert uses_new_form({"dcat-si:methodology": "M.md"})
    assert uses_new_form({"inputs": [{"slug": "x", "name": "X", "location": "a.csv", "source": {"name": "S", "prov:wasAttributedTo": "E"}}]})
    assert not uses_new_form({"inputs": [], "outputs": []})


def test_version_key_and_ensure_min_version() -> None:
    assert version_key("1.20.0") == (1, 19, 0)
    assert version_key("1.20.0rc1") == (1, 19, 0)
    assert version_key("2.0") > version_key("1.20.0")
    data = make_yaml().load("# top\ninputs: []\n")
    assert ensure_min_version(data) is True
    assert list(data) == ["min_sunstone_version", "inputs"] and data["min_sunstone_version"] == "1.20.0"
    assert _dump(data) == "# top\nmin_sunstone_version: 1.20.0\ninputs: []\n"
    assert ensure_min_version(data) is False
    low = {"min_sunstone_version": "1.10.0", "inputs": []}
    assert ensure_min_version(low) is True and low["min_sunstone_version"] == "1.20.0"
    high = {"min_sunstone_version": "2.0.0"}
    assert ensure_min_version(high) is False and high["min_sunstone_version"] == "2.0.0"

"""Rename old datasets.yaml / lock keys to their DP 2.0 or RDF names, in place.

Works on plain dicts and on ruamel ``CommentedMap`` objects (comments and key
order kept). Used by ``DatasetsManager._load``, lint and ``sunstone migrate``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, datetime
from typing import Any, Literal, Mapping, MutableMapping

from ruamel.yaml import YAML
from ruamel.yaml.comments import CommentedMap, CommentedSeq


def make_yaml() -> YAML:
    yaml = YAML()
    yaml.preserve_quotes = True
    yaml.default_flow_style = False
    yaml.width = 4096
    yaml.indent(mapping=2, sequence=4, offset=2)
    return yaml


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Rename:
    path: str
    old: str
    new: str


@dataclass
class NormalizeResult:
    renames: list[Rename] = field(default_factory=list)
    ambiguous: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    new_form: bool = False
    """True when the input already used a new-form key (before renaming)."""


MIN_NEW_FORM_VERSION = "1.20.0"
"""First sunstone-py version that reads the new key form (spec: Extras MUST)."""

Form = Literal["old", "new", "ambiguous", "untitled"]

_NEW_FORM_DATASET_KEYS = frozenset({"path", "schema", "licenses", "prov:generatedAtTime", "prov:wasGeneratedBy"})
_NEW_FORM_SOURCE_KEYS = frozenset(
    {"prov:wasAttributedTo", "dct:license", "dct:modified", "dcat:downloadURL", "dcat:landingPage", "dcat:accessURL", "rdfs:seeAlso",
     "@id", "dct:issued", "dct:isPartOf", "dct:bibliographicCitation"}
)

_DOI_PREFIXES = ("https://doi.org/", "http://doi.org/", "https://dx.doi.org/", "http://dx.doi.org/")


def is_doi_url(value: str) -> bool:
    """True for a resolvable DOI URL (spec: a DOI goes in ``"@id"``, never in a DCAT link)."""
    return value.startswith(_DOI_PREFIXES)
_NEW_FORM_FIELD_KEYS = frozenset({"si:unit", "si:sourceField", "qudt:hasUnit"})


def uses_new_form(data: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """True when any new-form key is present. Call before normalizing."""
    if "dcat-si:methodology" in data:
        return True
    for section in ("inputs", "outputs"):
        for entry in data.get(section) or []:
            if not isinstance(entry, Mapping):
                continue
            if _NEW_FORM_DATASET_KEYS & set(entry) or ("title" in entry and "slug" not in entry):
                return True
            src = entry.get("source")
            if isinstance(src, Mapping) and _NEW_FORM_SOURCE_KEYS & set(src):
                return True
            schema = entry.get("schema")
            fields = schema.get("fields") if isinstance(schema, Mapping) else entry.get("fields")
            for fld in fields or []:
                if isinstance(fld, Mapping) and _NEW_FORM_FIELD_KEYS & set(fld):
                    return True
    for pkg in [data.get("package"), *(data.get("packages") or [])]:
        if isinstance(pkg, Mapping) and "licenses" in pkg:
            return True
    return False


def version_key(v: str) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    parts = []
    for p in str(v).split("."):
        digits = "".join(ch for ch in p if ch.isdigit())
        parts.append(int(digits) if digits else 0)
    return tuple(parts)


def ensure_min_version(data: MutableMapping[str, Any], required: str = MIN_NEW_FORM_VERSION) -> bool:
    """Insert or raise ``min_sunstone_version``; never lowers it. Returns True when the document changed."""
    current = data.get("min_sunstone_version")
    if current is not None and version_key(str(current)) >= version_key(required):
        return False
    if "min_sunstone_version" in data:
        data["min_sunstone_version"] = required
    else:
        _insert(data, 0, "min_sunstone_version", required)
    return True


def detect_form(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Form:
    has_slug, has_title = "slug" in entry, "title" in entry
    if has_slug and has_title:
        return "ambiguous"
    if has_slug:
        return "old"
    if has_title:
        return "new"
    return "untitled"


def _new_map() -> MutableMapping[str, Any]:
    return CommentedMap()


def _new_seq() -> list:
    return CommentedSeq()


def _insert(m: MutableMapping[str, Any], idx: int, key: str, value: Any) -> None:
    if isinstance(m, CommentedMap):
        m.insert(idx, key, value)
        return
    items = list(m.items())
    m.clear()
    for i, (k, v) in enumerate(items):
        if i == idx:
            m[key] = value
        m[k] = v
    if key not in m:
        m[key] = value


def _move_comment(m: MutableMapping[str, Any], old: str, new: str) -> None:
    ca = getattr(m, "ca", None)
    if ca is None:
        return
    item = ca.items.pop(old, None)
    if item is not None:
        ca.items[new] = item


def rename_key(m: MutableMapping[str, Any], old: str, new: str, path: str, result: NormalizeResult) -> None:
    """Rename ``old`` to ``new`` keeping position and comment. Drops ``old`` when ``new`` exists."""
    if old not in m:
        return
    value = m[old]
    idx = list(m.keys()).index(old)
    if new in m:
        del m[old]
    else:
        _insert(m, idx, new, value)
        del m[old]
        _move_comment(m, old, new)
    result.renames.append(Rename(path, old, new))


def _set_at(m: MutableMapping[str, Any], idx: int, key: str, value: Any) -> None:
    if key in m:
        return
    _insert(m, idx, key, value)


def _iso(value: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(value, (date, datetime)):
        return value.isoformat()
    return value


def _license_list(value: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(value, list) or value is None:
        return value
    seq = _new_seq()
    entry = _new_map()
    entry["name"] = value
    seq.append(entry)
    return seq


_LOCATION_KEYS = (
    ("data", "dcat:downloadURL"),
    ("dcat:downloadURL", "dcat:downloadURL"),
    ("about", "dcat:landingPage"),
    ("dcat:landingPage", "dcat:landingPage"),
    ("web", "dcat:landingPage"),
    ("metadata", "rdfs:seeAlso"),
    ("access", "dcat:accessURL"),
    ("dcat:accessURL", "dcat:accessURL"),
)


def _normalize_source(src: MutableMapping[str, Any], path: str, result: NormalizeResult) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
    """Normalize a source block. Returns (acquired_at, acquisition_method) popped from it."""
    rename_key(src, "name", "title", path, result)
    rename_key(src, "license", "dct:license", path, result)
    rename_key(src, "updated", "dct:modified", path, result)
    if "dct:modified" in src:
        src["dct:modified"] = _iso(src["dct:modified"])

    if "attributedTo" in src:
        raw = src["attributedTo"]
        idx = list(src.keys()).index("attributedTo")
        if isinstance(raw, Mapping):
            node = _new_map()
            if "id" in raw:
                node["@id"] = raw["id"]
            if "type" in raw:
                node["@type"] = raw["type"]
            if raw.get("label"):
                node["rdfs:label"] = raw["label"]
            del src["attributedTo"]
            _set_at(src, idx, "prov:wasAttributedTo", node)
            if raw.get("version") is not None:
                _set_at(src, idx + 1, "version", raw["version"])
                result.renames.append(Rename(path, "attributedTo.version", "version"))
            result.renames.append(Rename(path, "attributedTo", "prov:wasAttributedTo"))
        else:
            rename_key(src, "attributedTo", "prov:wasAttributedTo", path, result)

    # Agent objects (SC16): a string publisher / creator becomes {rdfs:label: <string>}; nothing is split.
    if isinstance(src.get("dct:publisher"), str):
        node = _new_map()
        node["rdfs:label"] = src["dct:publisher"]
        src["dct:publisher"] = node  # same key, same position
        result.renames.append(Rename(path, "dct:publisher", "dct:publisher.rdfs:label"))
    creator = src.get("dct:creator")
    if isinstance(creator, str) or (isinstance(creator, list) and any(isinstance(c, str) for c in creator)):
        seq = _new_seq()
        for c in [creator] if isinstance(creator, str) else creator:
            if isinstance(c, str):
                node = _new_map()
                node["rdfs:label"] = c
                seq.append(node)
            else:
                seq.append(c)
        src["dct:creator"] = seq
        result.renames.append(Rename(path, "dct:creator", "dct:creator[].rdfs:label"))

    loc = src.get("location")
    if isinstance(loc, MutableMapping):
        # DOI move (spec C7): a doi.org URL is an identifier, not a link.
        for old in ("data", "web", "about"):
            value = loc.get(old)
            if isinstance(value, str) and is_doi_url(value):
                del loc[old]
                if "@id" not in src:
                    _insert(src, 0, "@id", value)
                result.renames.append(Rename(f"{path}.location", old, "@id"))
        idx = list(src.keys()).index("location")
        for old, new in _LOCATION_KEYS:
            if old in loc:
                value = loc.pop(old)
                if new not in src:
                    _insert(src, idx, new, value)
                    idx += 1
                result.renames.append(Rename(f"{path}.location", old, new))
        if not loc:
            del src["location"]

    acquired_at = src.pop("acquiredAt", None)
    if acquired_at is not None:
        result.renames.append(Rename(path, "acquiredAt", "prov:generatedAtTime"))
    method = src.pop("acquisitionMethod", None)
    if method is not None:
        result.renames.append(Rename(path, "acquisitionMethod", "prov:wasGeneratedBy"))
    return acquired_at, method


def _normalize_field(fld: MutableMapping[str, Any], path: str, result: NormalizeResult) -> None:
    if "unit" in fld:
        from .units import is_qudt_uri, parse_unit_string

        raw = fld["unit"]
        rename_key(fld, "unit", "si:unit", path, result)
        if isinstance(raw, str) and is_qudt_uri(raw):
            try:
                pint_unit, _ = parse_unit_string(raw)
                fld["si:unit"] = str(pint_unit)
            except Exception:
                fld["si:unit"] = raw
            if "qudt:hasUnit" not in fld:
                _insert(fld, list(fld.keys()).index("si:unit") + 1, "qudt:hasUnit", raw)
    rename_key(fld, "source", "si:sourceField", path, result)
    rename_key(fld, "dct:title", "title", path, result)


def _normalize_dataset(entry: MutableMapping[str, Any], path: str, result: NormalizeResult) -> None:
    form = detect_form(entry)
    if form == "ambiguous":
        result.ambiguous.append(path)
    elif form == "old":
        rename_key(entry, "name", "title", path, result)
        rename_key(entry, "slug", "name", path, result)
    rename_key(entry, "location", "path", path, result)
    if "license" in entry:
        entry["license"] = _license_list(entry["license"])
        rename_key(entry, "license", "licenses", path, result)

    for old in ("fields", "primaryKey"):
        if old in entry:
            value = entry[old]
            idx = list(entry.keys()).index(old)
            schema = entry.get("schema")
            if not isinstance(schema, MutableMapping):
                schema = _new_map()
                _insert(entry, idx, "schema", schema)
            if old not in schema:
                schema[old] = value
            del entry[old]
            result.renames.append(Rename(path, old, f"schema.{old}"))

    acquired_at = method = None
    src = entry.get("source")
    if isinstance(src, MutableMapping):
        acquired_at, method = _normalize_source(src, f"{path}.source", result)
        idx = list(entry.keys()).index("source") + 1
        if acquired_at is not None and "prov:generatedAtTime" not in entry:
            _insert(entry, idx, "prov:generatedAtTime", _iso(acquired_at))
            idx += 1
        if method is not None and "prov:wasGeneratedBy" not in entry:
            node = _new_map()
            node["@type"] = "prov:Activity"
            node["dct:type"] = method
            _insert(entry, idx, "prov:wasGeneratedBy", node)
    if "prov:generatedAtTime" in entry:
        entry["prov:generatedAtTime"] = _iso(entry["prov:generatedAtTime"])

    schema = entry.get("schema")
    if isinstance(schema, Mapping):
        fields = schema.get("fields")
        if isinstance(fields, list):
            for i, fld in enumerate(fields):
                if isinstance(fld, MutableMapping):
                    _normalize_field(fld, f"{path}.schema.fields[{i}]", result)


def _normalize_package(pkg: MutableMapping[str, Any], path: str, result: NormalizeResult) -> None:
    if "license" in pkg:
        pkg["license"] = _license_list(pkg["license"])
        rename_key(pkg, "license", "licenses", path, result)


def normalize_document(data: MutableMapping[str, Any]) -> NormalizeResult:
    result = NormalizeResult(new_form=uses_new_form(data))
    rename_key(data, "si:methodology", "dcat-si:methodology", "", result)
    for section in ("inputs", "outputs"):
        items = data.get(section)
        if isinstance(items, list):
            for i, entry in enumerate(items):
                if isinstance(entry, MutableMapping):
                    _normalize_dataset(entry, f"{section}[{i}]", result)
    pkg = data.get("package")
    if isinstance(pkg, MutableMapping):
        _normalize_package(pkg, "package", result)
    pkgs = data.get("packages")
    if isinstance(pkgs, list):
        for i, pkg in enumerate(pkgs):
            if isinstance(pkg, MutableMapping):
                _normalize_package(pkg, f"packages[{i}]", result)
    return result


def normalize_lock(lock: MutableMapping[str, Any]) -> NormalizeResult:
    result = NormalizeResult()
    for section in ("inputs", "outputs"):
        for i, entry in enumerate(lock.get(section) or []):
            if not isinstance(entry, MutableMapping):
                continue
            for j, src in enumerate(entry.get("sources") or []):
                if isinstance(src, MutableMapping):

"""Rule registry: every lint/conformance rule with its RFC 2119 level and scope."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Optional

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .conformance import ConformanceContext, Violation


class Severity(str, Enum):
    ERROR = "error"
    WARNING = "warning"
    INFO = "info"


class Level(str, Enum):
    MUST = "MUST"
    MUST_NOT = "MUST NOT"
    SHOULD = "SHOULD"
    MAY = "MAY"
    """Not checked; only used to label recommended keys in ``KEY_LEVELS``."""
    INFO = "INFO"


class Category(str, Enum):
    EXTRAS = "extras"
    PROVENANCE = "provenance"
    LINEAGE = "lineage"
    TYPES = "types"
    UNITS = "units"
    NAMING = "naming"
    DESCRIPTION = "description"
    METHODOLOGY = "methodology"
    CONFIG = "config"


@dataclass
class Rule:
    id: str
    level: Level
    category: Category
    scope: frozenset[str]
    title: str
    message: str
    fix: str
    deprecation: bool = False
    """True for MUST NOT rules that only warn while ``ENFORCE_MUST`` is False (1.x)."""
    check: Optional[Callable[["ConformanceContext"], Iterator["Violation"]]] = None

    @property
    def severity(self) -> Severity:
        from .conformance import ENFORCE_MUST

        return severity_for(self, ENFORCE_MUST)


def severity_for(rule: Rule, enforce_must: bool) -> Severity:
    if rule.level in (Level.MUST, Level.MUST_NOT):
        if rule.deprecation and not enforce_must:
            return Severity.WARNING
        return Severity.ERROR
    if rule.level is Level.SHOULD:
        return Severity.WARNING
    return Severity.INFO


def _r(id: str, level: Level, category: Category, scope: str, title: str, message: str, fix: str, deprecation: bool = False) -> Rule:
    return Rule(id, level, category, frozenset(scope.split()), title, message, fix, deprecation)

def register_check(rule_id: str) -> Callable[[Any], Any]:
    def deco(fn: Any) -> Any:
        RULES[rule_id].check = fn
        return fn

    return deco

"""Conformance validator for datasets.yaml, datasets.lock.yaml and datapackage.json.

Checks run over plain dicts in the new key form (see ``aliases.py``). Each
check is registered on its rule in ``rules.RULES`` and yields ``Violation``s.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import re
import warnings
from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Literal, Optional

from . import STANDARD_RDF_PREFIXES
from .aliases import MIN_NEW_FORM_VERSION, Rename, is_doi_url, normalize_document, normalize_lock, version_key
from .rules import RULES, Level, Severity, register_check, severity_for
from .vocab import (
    SHIPPED_VOCABS,
    config_keys,
    dp_keys,
    duplicate_keys,
    legacy_emitted_keys,
    level_children,
    lock_keys,
    namespace_of,
    recommended_keys,
    term_exists,
)

ENFORCE_MUST = False
"""False in 1.x (MUST violations warn), True in 2.0 (they raise ConformanceError)."""


class ConformanceError(Exception):
    """Raised on read/write for MUST violations when ``ENFORCE_MUST`` is True."""


@dataclass
class Violation:
    rule_id: str
    level: Level
    path: str
    message: str
    fix: Optional[str]
    severity: Severity

    @property
    def location(self) -> str:
        return self.path

    @property
    def fix_hint(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return self.fix

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "rule_id": self.rule_id,
            "level": self.level.value,
            "severity": self.severity.value,
            "path": self.path,
            "message": self.message,
            "fix": self.fix,
            "location": self.path,
            "fix_hint": self.fix,
        }


Kind = Literal["yaml", "lock", "datapackage"]


@dataclass
class ConformanceContext:
    kind: Kind
    data: Mapping[str, Any]
    lock: Mapping[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    renames: list[Rename] = field(default_factory=list)
    ambiguous: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    prefixes: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    field_types: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
    new_form: bool = False
    """The yaml document used new-form keys before normalization (R306)."""

    def violation(self, rule_id: str, path: str, message: str, fix: Optional[str] = None) -> Violation:
        rule = RULES[rule_id]
        return Violation(rule_id, rule.level, path, message, fix or rule.fix, severity_for(rule, ENFORCE_MUST))

    def datasets(self) -> Iterator[tuple[str, int, Mapping[str, Any], str]]:
        for section, kind in (("inputs", "input"), ("outputs", "output")):
            items = self.data.get(section)
            if not isinstance(items, list):
                continue
            for i, ds in enumerate(items):
                if isinstance(ds, Mapping):
                    yield kind, i, ds, f"{section}[{i}]"

    def dataset_names(self) -> set[str]:
        return {str(ds.get("name")) for _, _, ds, _ in self.datasets() if ds.get("name")}

    def lock_entry(self, name: Any) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
        for entry in self.lock.get("outputs") or []:
            if isinstance(entry, Mapping) and entry.get("slug") == name:
                return entry
        return {}

    def locked_units(self, name: Any) -> set[str]:
        units: set[str] = set()
        for section in ("inputs", "outputs"):
            for entry in self.lock.get(section) or []:
                if isinstance(entry, Mapping) and entry.get("slug") == name:
                    for fld in entry.get("fields") or []:
                        if isinstance(fld, Mapping) and fld.get("name") and (fld.get("unit") or fld.get("si:unit")):
                            units.add(str(fld["name"]))
        return units

    def packages(self) -> Iterator[tuple[Mapping[str, Any], str, bool]]:
        """Yield (package dict, path, publish enabled)."""
        pkg = self.data.get("package")
        if isinstance(pkg, Mapping):
            yield pkg, "package", _publish_enabled(self.data.get("publish"))
        pkgs = self.data.get("packages")
        if isinstance(pkgs, list):
            for i, p in enumerate(pkgs):
                if isinstance(p, Mapping):
                    yield p, f"packages[{i}]", _publish_enabled(p.get("publish"))

    def is_published(self, ds: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
        if "publish" in ds:
            return _publish_enabled(ds.get("publish"))
        for pkg, _, enabled in self.packages():
            datasets = pkg.get("datasets")
            if enabled and isinstance(datasets, list) and ds.get("name") in datasets:
                return True
        return "packages" not in self.data and _publish_enabled(self.data.get("publish"))

    def is_publishing(self) -> bool:
        """True when ``publish`` is enabled at the top level or on any ``packages[]`` entry (spec: Methodology MUST)."""
        if _publish_enabled(self.data.get("publish")):
            return True
        return any(enabled for _, _, enabled in self.packages())

    def package_license_for(self, name: Any) -> tuple[Any, str]:
        for pkg, path, _ in self.packages():
            datasets = pkg.get("datasets")
            covers = datasets is None or (isinstance(datasets, list) and name in datasets)
            lic = _first_license(pkg.get("licenses"))
            if covers and lic:
                return lic, f"{path}.licenses"
        return None, "package.licenses"


def _publish_enabled(raw: Any) -> bool:
    if isinstance(raw, bool):
        return raw
    if isinstance(raw, Mapping):
        return bool(raw.get("enabled"))
    return False


def _first_license(value: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(value, list) and value and isinstance(value[0], Mapping):
        return value[0].get("name")
    return None


_ARRAY_RE = re.compile(r"\[\d+\]")
_CAMEL_RE = re.compile(r"(?<=[a-z0-9])(?=[A-Z])|(?<=[A-Z])(?=[A-Z][a-z])")


def split_camel(name: str) -> str:
    return _CAMEL_RE.sub(" ", name).replace("_", " ").replace("-", " ").lower()


def _is_rdf_key(key: str) -> bool:
    return key.startswith(("http://", "https://")) or ":" in key


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Extras: R301 / R302 / R303 / R304 / R305
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def _check_key(ctx: ConformanceContext, key: str, level: str, path: str) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    kpath = f"{path}.{key}" if path else key
    if key in ("@id", "@type"):
        return
    if ctx.kind == "yaml" and key in config_keys(level):
        return
    if ctx.kind == "lock":
        if key in lock_keys(level):
            return
    elif level != "node" and key in dp_keys(level):
        return
    if ctx.kind == "datapackage" and not ENFORCE_MUST and key in legacy_emitted_keys(level):
        return
    if key.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
        for prefix in SHIPPED_VOCABS:
            ns = namespace_of(prefix)
            if key.startswith(ns):
                local = key[len(ns) :]
                if not term_exists(prefix, local):
                    yield ctx.violation("R303", kpath, f"'{prefix}:{local}' is not a term in the {prefix} vocabulary")
                return
        return
    if ":" in key:
        prefix, local = key.split(":", 1)
        if prefix not in ctx.prefixes:
            yield ctx.violation("R302", kpath, f"prefix '{prefix}' is not declared")
        elif prefix in SHIPPED_VOCABS and not term_exists(prefix, local):
            yield ctx.violation("R303", kpath, f"'{key}' is not a term in the {prefix} vocabulary")
        return
    at = _ARRAY_RE.sub("", path)
    yield ctx.violation(
        "R301",
        kpath,
        f"unknown key '{key}' at level '{level}'",
        f'Run `sunstone vocab search "{split_camel(key)}" --at {at or "."}` and use a listed key.',
    )


def _walk(ctx: ConformanceContext, m: Mapping[str, Any], level: str, path: str) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    children = level_children(level)
    for key, value in m.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str):
            continue
        yield from _check_key(ctx, key, level, path)
        kpath = f"{path}.{key}" if path else key
        child = children.get(key)
        if child is not None:
            if isinstance(value, list):
                for i, item in enumerate(value):
                    if isinstance(item, Mapping):
                        yield from _walk(ctx, item, child, f"{kpath}[{i}]")
            elif isinstance(value, Mapping):
                yield from _walk(ctx, value, child, kpath)
        elif _is_rdf_key(key):
            if isinstance(value, Mapping):
                yield from _walk(ctx, value, "node", kpath)
            elif isinstance(value, list):
                for i, item in enumerate(value):
                    if isinstance(item, Mapping):
                        yield from _walk(ctx, item, "node", f"{kpath}[{i}]")


@register_check("R301")
def _r301(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    if ctx.kind == "yaml":
        yield from (v for v in _walk(ctx, ctx.data, "document", "") if v.rule_id == "R301")
    elif ctx.kind == "datapackage":
        yield from (v for v in _walk(ctx, ctx.data, "package", "") if v.rule_id == "R301")
    else:
        yield from (v for v in _walk_lock(ctx) if v.rule_id == "R301")


@register_check("R302")
def _r302(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    yield from (v for v in _all_key_violations(ctx) if v.rule_id == "R302")


@register_check("R303")
def _r303(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    yield from (v for v in _all_key_violations(ctx) if v.rule_id == "R303")


def _all_key_violations(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    if ctx.kind == "yaml":
        yield from _walk(ctx, ctx.data, "document", "")
    elif ctx.kind == "datapackage":
        yield from _walk(ctx, ctx.data, "package", "")
    else:
        yield from _walk_lock(ctx)


def _walk_lock(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    for section in ("inputs", "outputs"):
        for i, entry in enumerate(ctx.lock.get(section) or []):
            if not isinstance(entry, Mapping):
                continue
            path = f"{section}[{i}]"
            for key in entry:
                if isinstance(key, str):
                    yield from _check_key(ctx, key, "entry", path)
            for j, src in enumerate(entry.get("sources") or []):
                if isinstance(src, Mapping):
                    for key in src:
                        if isinstance(key, str):
                            yield from _check_key(ctx, key, "source", f"{path}.sources[{j}]")


@register_check("R304")
def _r304(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    for r in ctx.renames:
        path = f"{r.path}.{r.old}" if r.path else r.old
        yield ctx.violation("R304", path, f"deprecated key '{r.old}', use '{r.new}'")


@register_check("R305")
def _r305(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    for path in ctx.ambiguous:
        yield ctx.violation("R305", path, "entry has both 'slug' and 'title'")


@register_check("R306")
def _r306(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    if ctx.kind != "yaml" or not ctx.new_form:
        return
    raw = ctx.data.get("min_sunstone_version")
    if raw is None or version_key(str(raw)) < version_key(MIN_NEW_FORM_VERSION):
        found = "missing" if raw is None else f"found {raw!r}"
        yield ctx.violation("R306", "min_sunstone_version", f"new-form keys need min_sunstone_version >= {MIN_NEW_FORM_VERSION} ({found})")


def _duplicates(ctx: ConformanceContext, m: Mapping[str, Any], level: str, path: str) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    for key, instead in duplicate_keys(level).items():
        if key in m:
            yield ctx.violation("R307", f"{path}.{key}", f"'{key}' duplicates '{instead}'", f"Remove '{key}'; use {instead}.")


@register_check("R307")
def _r307(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    if ctx.kind != "yaml":
        return
    for kind, _, ds, path in ctx.datasets():

        if kind == "output":

        src = ds.get("source")
        if isinstance(src, Mapping):
            yield from _duplicates(ctx, src, "source", f"{path}.source")
    for _, _, fld, path in _fields(ctx):
        yield from _duplicates(ctx, fld, "field", path)

def _license_of(ctx: ConformanceContext, kind: str, ds: Mapping[str, Any], path: str) -> tuple[Any, str]:
    if kind == "input":
        src = ds.get("source")
        if isinstance(src, Mapping):
            return src.get("dct:license"), f"{path}.source.dct:license"
        return None, f"{path}.source.dct:license"
    own = _first_license(ds.get("licenses"))
    if own:
        return own, f"{path}.licenses"
    return ctx.package_license_for(ds.get("name"))

def _fields(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> Iterator[tuple[str, Mapping[str, Any], Mapping[str, Any], str]]:

        if not isinstance(fields, list):

        for i, fld in enumerate(fields):

@register_check("R101")
def _r101(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    if not _yaml_only(ctx):
        return
    for kind, _, ds, path in ctx.datasets():
        if kind == "input" and "source" not in ds:
            yield ctx.violation("R101", f"{path}.source", "input has no 'source' block")


@register_check("R102")
def _r102(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    if not _yaml_only(ctx):
        return
    for kind, _, ds, path in ctx.datasets():
        if kind != "input" or "source" not in ds:
            continue
        src = ds.get("source")
        if not isinstance(src, Mapping):
            yield ctx.violation("R102", f"{path}.source", "source block must be a mapping")
            continue
        missing = [k for k in ("title", "dct:license") if not src.get(k)]
        publisher = src.get("dct:publisher")
        if not (isinstance(publisher, Mapping) and publisher.get("rdfs:label")):
            missing.append("dct:publisher with rdfs:label")
        if not (src.get("@id") or src.get("dcat:downloadURL") or src.get("dcat:landingPage")):
            missing.append('a link ("@id", dcat:downloadURL or dcat:landingPage)')
        if missing:
            yield ctx.violation("R102", f"{path}.source", f"source block missing keys: {', '.join(missing)}")


def _is_publication(src: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
    return bool(src.get("dct:isPartOf") or src.get("dct:bibliographicCitation"))


@register_check("R311")
def _r311(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    if not _yaml_only(ctx):
        return
    for kind, _, ds, path in ctx.datasets():
        src = ds.get("source")
        if kind != "input" or not isinstance(src, Mapping):
            continue
        missing = []
        publisher = src.get("dct:publisher")
        if isinstance(publisher, Mapping) and not publisher.get("skos:altLabel"):
            missing.append("dct:publisher.skos:altLabel")
        missing += [k for k in ("dct:issued", "dct:modified") if not src.get(k)]
        if _is_publication(src):
            missing += [k for k in ("dct:creator", "@id") if not src.get(k)]
        if missing:
            yield ctx.violation("R311", f"{path}.source", f"source block missing recommended keys: {', '.join(missing)}")


def _doi_in_links(ctx: ConformanceContext, src: Mapping[str, Any], path: str, keys: tuple[str, ...]) -> Iterator[Violation]:
    for key in keys:
        value = src.get(key)
        if isinstance(value, str) and is_doi_url(value):
            yield ctx.violation("R315", f"{path}.{key}", f"'{key}' holds a DOI ({value}); put it in \"@id\"")

def _r315(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> Iterator[Violation]:

            if isinstance(src, Mapping):
                yield from _doi_in_links(ctx, src, f"{path}.source", ("dcat:downloadURL", "dcat:landingPage"))
    elif ctx.kind == "datapackage":
        dcat = STANDARD_RDF_PREFIXES["dcat"]
        for r, path in _resources(ctx):

                if isinstance(src, Mapping):

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Runner and public API
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

KEY_LEVELS: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[Level, Optional[str]]] = {
    ("document", "min_sunstone_version"): (Level.MUST, "R306"),
    ("document", "dcat-si:methodology"): (Level.SHOULD, "R361"),
    ("dataset", "title"): (Level.MUST, "R001"),
    ("dataset", "name"): (Level.MUST, "R002"),
    ("dataset", "path"): (Level.MUST, "R003"),
    ("dataset", "description"): (Level.SHOULD, "R004"),
    ("dataset", "licenses"): (Level.MUST, "R005"),
    ("dataset", "source"): (Level.SHOULD, "R101"),
    ("dataset", "prov:generatedAtTime"): (Level.MUST, "R312"),
    ("dataset", "prov:wasGeneratedBy"): (Level.MUST, "R312"),
    ("source", "title"): (Level.MUST, "R102"),
    ("source", "dct:publisher"): (Level.MUST, "R102"),
    ("source", "@id"): (Level.MUST, "R102"),
    ("source", "dcat:downloadURL"): (Level.MUST, "R102"),
    ("source", "dcat:landingPage"): (Level.MUST, "R102"),
    ("source", "dct:license"): (Level.MUST, "R102"),
    ("source", "dct:issued"): (Level.SHOULD, "R311"),
    ("source", "dct:modified"): (Level.SHOULD, "R311"),
    ("source", "dct:creator"): (Level.SHOULD, "R311"),
    ("source", "dct:isPartOf"): (Level.MAY, None),
    ("source", "dct:bibliographicCitation"): (Level.MAY, None),
    ("source", "prov:wasAttributedTo"): (Level.MAY, None),
    ("source", "dcat:accessURL"): (Level.MAY, None),
    ("source", "rdfs:seeAlso"): (Level.MAY, None),
    ("source", "version"): (Level.MAY, None),
    ("field", "name"): (Level.MUST, "R007"),
    ("field", "type"): (Level.MUST, "R008"),
    ("field", "description"): (Level.SHOULD, "R105"),
    ("field", "si:unit"): (Level.SHOULD, "R103"),
    ("package", "title"): (Level.MUST, "R351"),
    ("package", "licenses"): (Level.MUST, "R005"),
}
"""Keys with a presence rule, for ``vocab search --at`` and the reference doc.

The three source links (``@id``, ``dcat:downloadURL``, ``dcat:landingPage``) are alternatives: R102 asks for one of them.
"""

# Spec "Recommended properties": SHOULD rows are checked by R314 (dataset level), MAY rows are listed only.
for _level in ("dataset", "source", "field"):
    for _key, _rfc in recommended_keys(_level).items():
        KEY_LEVELS.setdefault((_level, _key), (Level[_rfc], "R314" if _rfc == "SHOULD" else None))


def run_checks(ctx: ConformanceContext) -> list[Violation]:
    out: list[Violation] = []
    for rule in RULES.values():
        if rule.check is None or not any(s.startswith(ctx.kind + ":") for s in rule.scope):
            continue
        out.extend(rule.check(ctx))
    return out


def _collect_prefixes(data: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
    prefixes = dict(STANDARD_RDF_PREFIXES)
    defaults = data.get("defaults")
    for block in (data.get("rdfPrefixes"), defaults.get("rdfPrefixes") if isinstance(defaults, Mapping) else None):
        if isinstance(block, Mapping):
            prefixes.update({str(k): str(v) for k, v in block.items()})
    for section in ("inputs", "outputs"):
        for ds in data.get(section) or []:
            block = ds.get("rdfPrefixes") if isinstance(ds, Mapping) else None
            if isinstance(block, Mapping):
                prefixes.update({str(k): str(v) for k, v in block.items()})
    return prefixes


def _default_field_types() -> frozenset[str]:
    from .field_types import FieldTypeRegistry

    return frozenset(FieldTypeRegistry().known())


def validate_datasets_yaml(
    data: Mapping[str, Any],
    *,
    lock: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None,
    field_types: Optional[Any] = None,
    normalize: bool = True,
    result: Any = None,
) -> list[Violation]:
    """Validate a datasets.yaml document.

    With ``normalize=True`` (default) the document is deep-copied and alias
    keys are normalized first; ``data`` is never mutated. Pass
    ``normalize=False`` with the ``NormalizeResult`` from an earlier
    ``normalize_document`` call when the caller already normalized in place.
    """
    if normalize:
        data = copy.deepcopy(data)
        result = normalize_document(data)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    renames = list(result.renames) if result is not None else []
    ambiguous = list(result.ambiguous) if result is not None else []
    ctx = ConformanceContext(
        kind="yaml",
        data=data,
        lock=lock or {},
        renames=renames,
        ambiguous=ambiguous,
        prefixes=_collect_prefixes(data),
        field_types=frozenset(field_types) if field_types is not None else _default_field_types(),
        new_form=bool(result.new_form) if result is not None else False,
    )
    return run_checks(ctx)


def validate_lock(
    lock: Mapping[str, Any],
    data: Mapping[str, Any],
    *,
    normalize: bool = True,
    result: Any = None,
) -> list[Violation]:
    """Validate datasets.lock.yaml against the (normalized) datasets.yaml document."""
    if normalize:
        lock = copy.deepcopy(lock)
        result = normalize_lock(lock)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    ctx = ConformanceContext(
        kind="lock",
        data=data,
        lock=lock,
        renames=list(result.renames) if result is not None else [],
        prefixes=_collect_prefixes(data),
    )
    return run_checks(ctx)


def validate_datapackage(descriptor: Mapping[str, Any]) -> list[Violation]:
    """Validate a finished datapackage.json descriptor (keys are expanded IRIs)."""
    ctx = ConformanceContext(kind="datapackage", data=descriptor, prefixes=dict(STANDARD_RDF_PREFIXES))
    return run_checks(ctx)


SHOWN_IN_WARNING = 5
"""How many MUST violations the per-file FutureWarning lists (spec C4)."""


def enforce(violations: list[Violation], *, where: str, stacklevel: int = 3) -> None:
    """Apply the release policy to MUST violations: one FutureWarning per file in 1.x, ConformanceError in 2.0.

    FutureWarning, not DeprecationWarning: Python hides DeprecationWarning raised inside a library.
    """
    must = [v for v in violations if v.level in (Level.MUST, Level.MUST_NOT)]
    if not must:
        return
    if ENFORCE_MUST:
        lines = [f"[{v.rule_id}] {v.path}: {v.message}" for v in must]
        raise ConformanceError(f"{where}: " + "; ".join(lines))
    aliases = [v for v in must if v.rule_id == "R304"]
    others = [v for v in must if v.rule_id != "R304"]
    if others:
        shown = "; ".join(f"[{v.rule_id}] {v.path}: {v.message}" for v in others[:SHOWN_IN_WARNING])
        more = f" (+{len(others) - SHOWN_IN_WARNING} more)" if len(others) > SHOWN_IN_WARNING else ""
        warnings.warn(
            f"{where}: {len(others)} MUST violation(s): {shown}{more}; "
            "run `sunstone lint` for all of them; these become errors in sunstone-py 2.0",
            FutureWarning,
            stacklevel=stacklevel,
        )
    if aliases:
        warnings.warn(
            f"{where}: {len(aliases)} deprecated key(s) (e.g. {aliases[0].path}); run `sunstone migrate`; "
            "these become errors in sunstone-py 2.0",
            FutureWarning,
            stacklevel=stacklevel,
        )

def _assert_subset(before: Any, after: Any, path: str = "") -> None:
    if isinstance(before, dict):
        assert isinstance(after, dict), path
        for k, v in before.items():
            assert k in after, f"{path}.{k} removed"
            _assert_subset(v, after[k], f"{path}.{k}")
    elif isinstance(before, list):
        assert isinstance(after, list) and len(after) == len(before), path
        for i, (b, a) in enumerate(zip(before, after)):
            _assert_subset(b, a, f"{path}[{i}]")
    else:
        assert before == after, path

def _agent_node(agent: SourceAgent) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Spec "Source references" agent object with expanded keys (sunstone-cms#610 reads these IRIs literally)."""
    node: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if agent.id:
        node["@id"] = agent.id
    node[f"{_RDFS}label"] = agent.label
    if agent.alt_label:
        node[f"{_SKOS}altLabel"] = agent.alt_label
    return node


def _source_entry(source: Source) -> dict[str, Any]:
    entry: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if source.id:
        entry["@id"] = source.id
    entry["title"] = source.name
    loc = source.location
    path = loc.data or loc.about or loc.metadata or loc.access or source.id  # spec: derived, "@id" is the last fallback
    if path:
        entry["path"] = path
    dcat = STANDARD_RDF_PREFIXES["dcat"]
    for prop, value in (("downloadURL", loc.data), ("accessURL", loc.access), ("landingPage", loc.about)):
        if value:
            entry[f"{dcat}{prop}"] = value
    if loc.metadata:
        entry[f"{_RDFS}seeAlso"] = loc.metadata
    if source.publisher:
        entry[f"{_DCT}publisher"] = _agent_node(source.publisher)
    if source.creator:
        entry[f"{_DCT}creator"] = [_agent_node(a) for a in source.creator]
    if source.issued:
        entry[f"{_DCT}issued"] = source.issued
    if source.is_part_of:
        entry[f"{_DCT}isPartOf"] = _expand_value(source.is_part_of, STANDARD_RDF_PREFIXES)
    if source.bibliographic_citation:
        entry[f"{_DCT}bibliographicCitation"] = source.bibliographic_citation
    agent = source.attributed_to
    if isinstance(agent, Agent):
        node: dict[str, Any] = {"@id": agent.id, "@type": expand_rdf_prefixes(agent.type.value, STANDARD_RDF_PREFIXES)}
        if agent.label:
            node[f"{_RDFS}label"] = agent.label
        entry[f"{_PROV}wasAttributedTo"] = node
        if agent.version:
            entry["version"] = agent.version
    elif agent:
        entry[f"{_PROV}wasAttributedTo"] = str(agent)
    for prop, value in (("license", source.license), ("modified", source.updated)):
        if value:
            entry[f"{_DCT}{prop}"] = value
    return entry

    """Add datasets.yaml field metadata to a descriptor field. Legacy keys stay (1.x)."""
    if f.description and "description" not in field_dict:

    if f.constraints and "constraints" not in field_dict:

"""Linter for ``datasets.yaml`` against the Sunstone conformance rules.

Rules live in :mod:`sunstone.rules`; checks in :mod:`sunstone.conformance`.
This module loads the files, runs the checks and applies ``lint.disable``
suppressions. Entry point: :func:`lint_project` / ``sunstone lint``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from .aliases import make_yaml, normalize_document, normalize_lock
from .conformance import Violation, validate_datasets_yaml, validate_lock
from .rules import RULES, Rule, Severity

__all__ = ["RULES", "Rule", "Severity", "Violation", "LintReport", "lint_project", "report_to_json"]

_yaml = make_yaml()

LintReport is unchanged. lint_project becomes:

def lint_project(
    project_path: Path | str,
    *,
    datasets_file: str = "datasets.yaml",
    rules: set[str] | None = None,
) -> LintReport:
    project = Path(project_path).resolve()
    if project.is_file():
        yaml_path = project
        project = project.parent
    else:
        yaml_path = project / datasets_file

    if not yaml_path.exists():
        return LintReport(project_path=project)

    with open(yaml_path, "r") as f:
        data = _yaml.load(f) or {}
    result = normalize_document(data)

    lock_path = project / "datasets.lock.yaml"
    lock_data: dict[str, Any] = {}
    lock_result = None
    if lock_path.exists():
        with open(lock_path, "r") as f:
            lock_data = _yaml.load(f) or {}
        lock_result = normalize_lock(lock_data)

    from .plugins import PluginRegistry

    field_types = PluginRegistry.get(project).field_types.known()

    report = LintReport(project_path=project)
    suppressions, config_violations = _parse_lint_config(data.get("lint"))
    report.suppressions = suppressions

    enabled = (lambda rid: rules is None or rid in rules)

    # R009 violations are NEVER suppressed — that's how we keep lint.disable honest.
    for v in config_violations:
        if enabled(v.rule_id):
            report.add(v)

    violations = validate_datasets_yaml(data, lock=lock_data, field_types=field_types, normalize=False, result=result)
    if lock_result is not None:
        violations += validate_lock(lock_data, data, normalize=False, result=lock_result)

    for v in violations:
        if not enabled(v.rule_id):
            continue
        if v.rule_id in suppressions:
            report.suppressed.append(v)
        else:
            report.add(v)
    return report

Delete _apply_violation and _LintContext. In _parse_lint_config, construct R009 violations with the conformance dataclass:

from .rules import Level

def _r009(message: str, location: str, hint: str) -> Violation:
    return Violation("R009", Level.MUST, location, message, hint, Severity.ERROR)

and replace each Violation(rule_id="R009", severity=..., message=..., location=..., fix_hint=...) with _r009(message, location, hint).

import json

from typer.testing import CliRunner

from sunstone.cli import app
from sunstone.vocab_search import explain, search


def test_attributed_finds_prov_first() -> None:
    hits = search("attributed")
    assert hits[0].curie == "prov:wasAttributedTo"


def test_multi_word_query_requires_every_word() -> None:
    hits = search("download url")
    assert hits[0].curie == "dcat:downloadURL"
    assert all("download" in (h.curie + h.label + h.definition).lower() for h in hits)


def test_tier_then_source_order() -> None:
    hits = search("title", at="inputs.source")
    assert (hits[0].source, hits[0].curie) == ("dp", "title")
    assert "dct:title" in [h.curie for h in hits]


def test_at_filters_dp_keys_but_not_rdf() -> None:
    assert not [h for h in search("slug") if h.source in ("dp", "config")]
    field_hits = search("name", at="inputs.schema.fields")
    assert ("dp", "name") in {(h.source, h.curie) for h in field_hits}
    assert ("config", "include") not in {(h.source, h.curie) for h in field_hits}
    assert any(h.source == "schema" for h in field_hits)


def test_limit() -> None:
    assert len(search("a", limit=5)) == 5


def test_unknown_path_raises() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        search("x", at="inputs.fields")


def test_explain_fields_level() -> None:
    keys = {k.key: k for k in explain("inputs.schema.fields")}
    assert keys["name"].rule_level == "MUST" and keys["name"].cls == "dp"
    assert keys["type"].rule_level == "MUST"
    assert keys["description"].rule_level == "SHOULD"

"""Linear-scan search over shipped vocabularies and descriptor keys (``sunstone vocab search``)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Optional

from .conformance import KEY_LEVELS, split_camel
from .rules import Level
from .vocab import Term, all_terms, config_keys, dp_keys, key_definition, level_for_path

SOURCE_ORDER: tuple[str, ...] = ("dp", "config", "dct", "dcat", "prov", "schema", "skos", "rdfs", "qudt", "sosa", "si", "dcat-si")
_RULE_ORDER = {"MUST": 0, "MUST NOT": 0, "SHOULD": 1, "MAY": 2}
_JSONLD_DEFINITIONS = {
    "@id": "JSON-LD identifier of the node. On a source: the DOI as https://doi.org/<doi>, or another persistent IRI.",
    "@type": "JSON-LD type of the node, e.g. prov:Activity.",
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KeyInfo:
    key: str
    cls: str
    level: str
    rule_level: str
    rule_id: Optional[str]
    definition: str


def _match_fields(term: Term) -> tuple[str, str, str, str]:
    local = term.curie.split(":", 1)[1] if term.iri else term.curie
    return (f"{local} {split_camel(local)}".lower(), term.curie.lower(), term.label.lower(), term.definition.lower())


def _tier(word: str, fields: tuple[str, str, str, str]) -> Optional[int]:
    if word in fields[0] or word in fields[1]:
        return 1
    if word in fields[2]:
        return 2
    if word in fields[3]:
        return 3
    return None


def _resolve_level(at: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    if at is None:
        return None
    level = level_for_path(at)
    if level is None:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown datasets.yaml path: {at!r}")
    return level


def search(query: str, *, at: Optional[str] = None, limit: int = 20) -> list[Term]:
    words = query.lower().split()
    level = _resolve_level(at)
    scored: list[tuple[int, int, str, Term]] = []
    for term in all_terms():
        if level is not None and term.source in ("dp", "config") and level not in term.levels:
            continue
        fields = _match_fields(term)
        tiers = [_tier(w, fields) for w in words]
        if not words or any(t is None for t in tiers):
            continue
        best = min(t for t in tiers if t is not None)
        scored.append((best, SOURCE_ORDER.index(term.source), term.curie, term))
    scored.sort(key=lambda s: s[:3])
    return [s[3] for s in scored[:limit]]


def explain(at: str) -> list[KeyInfo]:
    level = _resolve_level(at)
    assert level is not None
    infos: dict[str, KeyInfo] = {}
    for key in dp_keys(level):
        infos[key] = KeyInfo(key, "dp", level, "MAY", None, key_definition(level, key))
    for key in config_keys(level):
        infos[key] = KeyInfo(key, "config", level, "MAY", None, key_definition(level, key))
    for (lvl, key), (rule_level, rule_id) in KEY_LEVELS.items():
        if lvl != level:
            continue
        existing = infos.get(key)
        cls = existing.cls if existing else ("config" if key in config_keys(level) else "jsonld" if key.startswith("@") else "rdf")
        definition = existing.definition if existing else _JSONLD_DEFINITIONS.get(key) or _rdf_definition(key)
        infos[key] = KeyInfo(key, cls, level, rule_level.value, rule_id, definition)
    return sorted(infos.values(), key=lambda k: (_RULE_ORDER[k.rule_level], k.key))


def _rdf_definition(curie: str) -> str:
    for term in all_terms():
        if term.curie == curie and term.iri:
            return term.definition
    return ""


def term_to_dict(term: Term) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "curie": term.curie,
        "iri": term.iri,
        "label": term.label,
        "definition": term.definition,
        "source": term.source,
        "levels": list(term.levels),
    }


def key_info_to_dict(info: KeyInfo) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"key": info.key, "class": info.cls, "level": info.level, "rule": info.rule_level, "rule_id": info.rule_id, "definition": info.definition}


__all__ = ["KeyInfo", "SOURCE_ORDER", "explain", "key_info_to_dict", "search", "term_to_dict", "Level"]

"""``sunstone migrate``: rewrite datasets.yaml, its include files and datasets.lock.yaml to the new key form."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from .aliases import NormalizeResult, ensure_min_version, make_yaml, normalize_document, normalize_lock
from .conformance import split_camel, validate_datasets_yaml

LOCK_HEADER = "# Auto-generated by sunstone. Do not edit manually.\n"
_ARRAY_RE = re.compile(r"\[\d+\]")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class UnknownKey:
    path: str
    key: str
    suggestions: list[str]


@dataclass
class MigrationReport:
    changed: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    unknown: list[UnknownKey] = field(default_factory=list)
    dry_run: bool = False


def _write(path: Path, data: Any, *, header: str = "") -> None:
    yaml = make_yaml()
    ca = getattr(data, "ca", None)
    if header and ca is not None:
        ca.comment = None
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        if header:
            f.write(header)
        yaml.dump(data, f)


def _suggest(key: str, path: str) -> list[str]:
    from .vocab import level_for_path
    from .vocab_search import search

    at = _ARRAY_RE.sub("", path)
    at = at if level_for_path(at) is not None else None
    return [t.curie for t in search(split_camel(key), at=at, limit=3)]


def migrate_project(project_path: Path | str, *, datasets_file: str = "datasets.yaml", dry_run: bool = False) -> MigrationReport:
    project = Path(project_path).resolve()
    main_path = project / datasets_file
    yaml = make_yaml()
    report = MigrationReport(dry_run=dry_run)

    with open(main_path, "r") as f:
        main = yaml.load(f) or {}
    main_result = normalize_document(main)
    main_changes = len(main_result.renames)
    if (main_result.renames or main_result.new_form) and ensure_min_version(main):
        main_changes += 1
    if main_changes:
        report.changed[main_path.name] = main_changes
        if not dry_run:
            _write(main_path, main)

    for rel in main.get("include") or []:
        inc_path = (main_path.parent / str(rel)).resolve()
        if not inc_path.exists():
            continue
        with open(inc_path, "r") as f:
            inc = yaml.load(f) or {}
        inc_result = normalize_document(inc)
        if inc_result.renames:
            report.changed[Path(str(rel)).as_posix()] = len(inc_result.renames)
            if not dry_run:
                _write(inc_path, inc)

    lock_path = main_path.parent / "datasets.lock.yaml"
    if lock_path.exists():
        with open(lock_path, "r") as f:
            lock = yaml.load(f) or {}
        lock_result = normalize_lock(lock)
        if lock_result.renames:
            report.changed[lock_path.name] = len(lock_result.renames)
            if not dry_run:
                _write(lock_path, lock, header=LOCK_HEADER)

    for v in validate_datasets_yaml(main, normalize=False, result=NormalizeResult()):
        if v.rule_id != "R301":
            continue
        container, _, key = v.path.rpartition(".")
        report.unknown.append(UnknownKey(v.path, key, _suggest(key, container)))
    return report

@app.command("migrate")
def migrate_cmd(
    datasets_file: str = typer.Option("datasets.yaml", "-f", "--file", help="Path to datasets.yaml"),
    dry_run: bool = typer.Option(False, "--dry-run", help="Report what would change without writing."),
) -> None:
    """Rewrite datasets.yaml, its include files and datasets.lock.yaml to the current key names.

    Comments and key order are kept. Safe to run repeatedly. Keys that are neither
    Data Package properties, config keys nor RDF properties are listed with suggestions.
    """
    from .migrate import migrate_project

    yaml_path = Path(datasets_file).resolve()
    if not yaml_path.exists():
        typer.echo(f"Error: {datasets_file} not found", err=True)
        sys.exit(1)
    report = migrate_project(yaml_path.parent, datasets_file=yaml_path.name, dry_run=dry_run)
    verb = "would rename" if dry_run else "renamed"
    if not report.changed:
        typer.echo("Nothing to migrate.")
    for name, count in report.changed.items():
        typer.echo(f"{name}: {count} key(s) {verb}")
    if report.unknown:
        typer.echo("Unknown keys (not DP, config or RDF):")
        for u in report.unknown:
            hint = ", ".join(u.suggestions) if u.suggestions else "no suggestion"
            typer.echo(f"  {u.path}: try {hint}")
    typer.echo("Run `sunstone lint` to review remaining findings.")

"""Render JSON Schemas and the key reference from the vocabulary data. Run via scripts/gen_schemas.py."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from . import DP_PROFILE_URL, aliases, config_keys, dp_keys, key_definition, legacy_emitted_keys, level_children

SCHEMA_BASE = "https://sunstoneinstitute.github.io/sunstone-py/schemas/"
RDF_KEY_PATTERNS: dict[str, Any] = {"^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:[^\\s]+$": {}, "^https?://": {}}
ARRAY_KEYS = frozenset({"inputs", "outputs", "packages", "contributors", "sources", "licenses", "fields", "resources"})
YAML_LEVELS = ("document", "dataset", "source", "schema", "field", "constraints", "license", "dialect", "package", "contributor", "publish", "lint", "defaults", "node")
DP_LEVELS = ("package", "resource", "source", "schema", "field", "constraints", "license", "dialect", "contributor", "node")

def _level_schema(level: str, keys: set[str], defs_available: set[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    props: dict[str, Any] = {}
    children = level_children(level)
    for key in sorted(keys):
        child = children.get(key)
        if child in defs_available:
            ref = {"$ref": f"#/definitions/{child}"}
            props[key] = {"type": "array", "items": ref} if key in ARRAY_KEYS else ref
        else:
            props[key] = {}
    out: dict[str, Any] = {"type": "object", "properties": props, "patternProperties": dict(RDF_KEY_PATTERNS), "additionalProperties": False}
    if level == "node":
        out["properties"] = {"@id": {"type": "string"}, "@type": {"type": "string"}}
    return out


def render_datasets_schema() -> dict[str, Any]:
    levels = set(YAML_LEVELS)
    defs = {lvl: _level_schema(lvl, set(dp_keys(lvl)) | set(config_keys(lvl)), levels) for lvl in YAML_LEVELS}
    return {
        "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
        "$id": SCHEMA_BASE + "datasets.schema.json",
        "title": "sunstone datasets.yaml",
        "description": "Keys are Data Package 2.0 properties, sunstone config keys, or RDF properties (prefix:local or IRI).",
        "$ref": "#/definitions/document",
        "definitions": defs,
    }


def render_datapackage_profile() -> dict[str, Any]:
    levels = set(DP_LEVELS)
    defs = {lvl: _level_schema(lvl, set(dp_keys(lvl)) | set(legacy_emitted_keys(lvl)), levels) for lvl in DP_LEVELS}
    return {
        "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
        "$id": SCHEMA_BASE + "datapackage-profile.json",
        "title": "sunstone Data Package profile",
        "description": f"Data Package 2.0 ({DP_PROFILE_URL}) with extras restricted to prefixed names or IRIs.",
        "$ref": "#/definitions/package",
        "definitions": defs,
    }


def render_reference_md() -> str:
    from ..rules import RULES
    from ..vocab_search import explain

    lines = [
        "# datasets.yaml key reference",
        "",
        "Generated by `scripts/gen_schemas.py` from `src/sunstone/vocab/`. Do not edit by hand.",
        "",
        "Every key is one of: a Data Package 2.0 property (`dp`) for its level, a sunstone config key (`config`), or an RDF property (`rdf`: `prefix:local` or an absolute IRI). RDF properties are allowed at every level; the rows marked `rdf` below are the ones a rule asks for. Rule levels follow RFC 2119 (`MUST`, `SHOULD`, `MAY`).",
        "",
        "Editor support: add `# yaml-language-server: $schema=" + SCHEMA_BASE + "datasets.schema.json` as the first line of `datasets.yaml`.",
        "",
        "Agent objects (`dct:publisher`, each `dct:creator` entry) carry `rdfs:label` (full name), optional `skos:altLabel` (short name) and optional `\"@id\"` (IRI). Repeat an agent within one file with a YAML anchor: `dct:publisher: &fao {rdfs:label: ..., skos:altLabel: FAO}` on first use, `dct:publisher: *fao` after. Anchors do not cross include files.",
        "",
    ]
    for level in YAML_LEVELS:
        if level in ("node",):
            continue
        lines += [f"## {level.capitalize()}", "", f"Path: `{LEVEL_PATHS[level]}`", "", "| Key | Class | Rule | Description | Example |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for info in explain(_example_path(level)):
            example = EXAMPLES.get((level, info.key), f"{info.key}: ...")
            lines.append(f"| `{info.key}` | {info.cls} | {info.rule_level} | {info.definition} | `{example}` |")
        lines.append("")
    lines += ["## Aliases (old key to new key)", "", "| Level | Old | New |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for level, entries in aliases().items():
        for e in entries:
            lines.append(f"| {level} | `{e['old']}` | `{e['new']}` |")
    lines += ["", "## Rules", "", "| Rule | Level | Category | Title |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    for rule in RULES.values():
        lines.append(f"| {rule.id} | {rule.level.value} | {rule.category.value} | {rule.title} |")
    lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _example_path(level: str) -> str:
    return {
        "document": "", "dataset": "inputs", "source": "inputs.source", "schema": "inputs.schema", "field": "inputs.schema.fields",
        "constraints": "inputs.schema.fields.constraints", "license": "inputs.licenses", "dialect": "inputs.dialect",
        "package": "package", "contributor": "package.contributors", "publish": "publish", "lint": "lint", "defaults": "defaults",
    }[level]


def write_all(root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    import json

    out = [
        (root / "schemas" / "datasets.schema.json", json.dumps(render_datasets_schema(), indent=2) + "\n"),
        (root / "schemas" / "datapackage-profile.json", json.dumps(render_datapackage_profile(), indent=2) + "\n"),
        (root / "docs" / "datasets-yaml-reference.md", render_reference_md()),
    ]
    for path, text in out:
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return [p for p, _ in out]

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A plugin system for sunstone-py that supports three plugin types: authentication providers, URL handlers, and format handlers. Plugins are discovered via Python entry points, configured in pyproject.toml, and composed in a pipeline that extends sunstone's read/write operations.

docs.title: Design Decisions
docs.text:
• Typed Protocols (structural typing) for plugin contracts — no inheritance required
  • Entry point discovery via sunstone.plugins group in pyproject.toml
  • Pipeline composition with defined phases: resolve URL -> authenticate -> fetch -> read format
  • Cascading plugin config — pyproject.toml -> datasets.yaml -> env vars, so projects use whichever they have
  • Plugins take priority over builtins — a custom CSV handler overrides the default
  • Zero overhead when no plugins installed — existing code paths run unchanged

docs.title: Plugin Discovery & Registry
docs.text: Plugins are discovered via Python entry points and managed by a central PluginRegistry.

docs.title: Entry point registration
docs.text:
# In a plugin's pyproject.toml
[project.entry-points."sunstone.plugins"]
s3 = "sunstone_s3:S3Plugin"

docs.title: Registry
docs.text:
# sunstone/plugins.py
class PluginRegistry:
    """Discovers and manages plugins."""

    _instance: PluginRegistry | None = None

    @classmethod
    def get(cls) -> PluginRegistry:
        """Singleton - lazy-loads plugins on first access."""
        if cls._instance is None:
            cls._instance = cls()
            cls._instance._discover()
        return cls._instance

    def _discover(self) -> None:
        """Load plugins from entry points."""
        for ep in importlib.metadata.entry_points(group="sunstone.plugins"):
            plugin_cls = ep.load()
            config = self._load_config(ep.name)  # cascading: pyproject.toml -> datasets.yaml -> env vars
            plugin = plugin_cls(config) if config else plugin_cls()
            self._register(ep.name, plugin)

    def _register(self, name: str, plugin: object) -> None:
        """Classify plugin by protocol conformance."""
        if isinstance(plugin, AuthProvider):
            self._auth_providers.append(plugin)
        if isinstance(plugin, URLHandler):
            self._url_handlers.append(plugin)
        if isinstance(plugin, FormatHandler):
            self._format_handlers.append(plugin)

docs.title: Config loading
docs.text:
Plugin config uses a cascading lookup. Sources are checked in order, with later sources overriding earlier ones:

  1. pyproject.toml — [tool.sunstone.plugins.<name>] section. For Python-packaged projects.
  2. datasets.yaml — plugins: top-level key. For notebook-only projects without a pyproject.toml.
  3. Environment variables — SUNSTONE_PLUGIN_<NAME>_<KEY>=value. For CI/Docker overrides.
# Option 1: pyproject.toml
[tool.sunstone.plugins.s3]
region = "eu-west-1"
role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::123:role/data-reader"

# Option 2: datasets.yaml
plugins:
  s3:
    region: eu-west-1
    role_arn: arn:aws:iam::123:role/data-reader

# Option 3: environment variables (override any file-based config)
SUNSTONE_PLUGIN_S3_REGION=eu-west-1
SUNSTONE_PLUGIN_S3_ROLE_ARN=arn:aws:iam::123:role/data-reader

The merged config dict is passed to the plugin constructor. Plugins that need no config accept no arguments. Environment variables use uppercase plugin name and key, with hyphens converted to underscores (e.g. bearer-auth becomes SUNSTONE_PLUGIN_BEARER_AUTH_).

docs.title: Protocol Definitions
docs.text:
Three @runtime_checkable protocols define plugin contracts.

from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable

@runtime_checkable
class AuthProvider(Protocol):
    """Provides authentication for HTTP requests."""

    def authenticate(self, url: str, headers: dict[str, str],
                     dataset: DatasetMetadata) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Return modified headers dict. Called before every HTTP fetch."""
        ...

@runtime_checkable
class URLHandler(Protocol):
    """Resolves custom URL schemes to local file paths."""

    def can_handle(self, url: str) -> bool:
        """Return True if this handler can resolve the given URL."""
        ...

    def fetch(self, url: str, dest: Path) -> Path:
        """Download/resolve URL to a local file. Return path to the file."""
        ...

@runtime_checkable
class FormatHandler(Protocol):
    """Reads and writes data formats not built into sunstone."""

    def can_read(self, path: Path, format: str | None) -> bool:
        """Return True if this handler can read the given file/format."""
        ...

    def read(self, path: Path, **kwargs) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Read file into a pandas DataFrame."""
        ...

    def can_write(self, path: Path, format: str | None) -> bool:
        """Return True if this handler can write the given file/format."""
        ...

    def write(self, df: pd.DataFrame, path: Path, **kwargs) -> None:
        """Write DataFrame to file."""
        ...

Design notes:

  • @runtime_checkable enables isinstance() checks in the registry for structural typing at runtime.
  • AuthProvider returns headers (not a requests object) to stay transport-agnostic. URL handlers that use non-HTTP transports (e.g. boto3 for S3) handle their own auth by also implementing AuthProvider.
  • URLHandler.fetch takes a dest path so the caller decides file location (consistent with existing fetch_from_url behavior). Config is received via the constructor, not passed per-call.
  • FormatHandler splits can_read/can_write because a plugin might support reading but not writing a format (or vice versa).
  • FormatHandler does not handle lineage. Sidecar .lineage.json is a core feature, not a plugin responsibility.

docs.title: Read pipeline
docs.text:
resolve URL -> authenticate -> fetch -> read format -> (lineage tracking)

def _resolve_and_fetch(self, dataset: DatasetMetadata, dest: Path) -> Path:
    url = dataset.source.location.data
    registry = PluginRegistry.get()

    # Find a URL handler for this scheme
    handler = registry.find_url_handler(url)

    if handler:
        # Plugin handles fetch (e.g. s3://, gs://, sftp://)
        return handler.fetch(url, dest)

    # Fall back to built-in HTTP fetch
    if not _is_public_url(url):
        raise ValueError(...)

    headers = {}
    # Run all auth providers for HTTP URLs
    for auth in registry.get_auth_providers():
        headers = auth.authenticate(url, headers, dataset)

    return self._http_fetch(url, dest, headers=headers)

def _read_file(self, path: Path, format: str | None, **kwargs) -> pd.DataFrame:
    registry = PluginRegistry.get()

    # Check plugin format handlers first
    handler = registry.find_format_handler(path, format, mode="read")
    if handler:
        return handler.read(path, **kwargs)

    # Fall back to built-in readers (csv, json, excel, parquet, tsv)
    reader = self._builtin_readers.get(format)
    if reader is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported format '{format}'...")
    return reader(path, **kwargs)

docs.title: Key behaviors
docs.text:
• Plugins take priority over builtins — registering a custom CSV handler overrides the default.
  • Auth providers stack — all matching auth providers run, each adding/modifying headers.
  • URL handlers are exclusive — first handler where can_handle(url) returns True wins.
  • Write pipeline mirrors read — same pattern: find format handler, plugin or builtin, then lineage/sidecar tracking (always core).
  • No plugins installed = no overhead — PluginRegistry.get() finds no entry points and existing code paths run unchanged.

docs.title: Integration Points
docs.text: Changes to existing code are minimal:

docs.title: dataframe.py:read_dataset() (line ~149-194)
docs.text: Currently has inline format detection and reader dispatch. Refactor to: - Extract _resolve_and_fetch() — replaces the direct manager.fetch_from_url() call - Extract _read_file() — replaces the format_map / reader_map dicts

docs.title: dataframe.py:read_csv() (line ~264 onward)
docs.text: Currently calls pd.read_csv() directly after resolving the path. Route through _read_file() so format plugins can intercept.

docs.title: datasets.py:fetch_from_url() (line ~721)
docs.text: Becomes the _http_fetch() fallback inside _resolve_and_fetch(), with auth provider headers injected. SSRF protection stays exactly where it is — it only applies to HTTP fetches, not plugin-handled URLs (S3/GCS plugins handle their own security).

docs.title: dataframe.py:to_csv() and future write methods
docs.text: Mirror the read pipeline: check for format handler plugin, fall back to builtin. Sidecar .lineage.json is written by core after the format handler's write() returns.

docs.title: What doesn't change
docs.text:
• DatasetsManager — still owns datasets.yaml, lineage persistence, strict/relaxed mode
  • LineageSession — still accumulates reads and flushes on write
  • pandas.py — still the user-facing API, delegates to DataFrame methods
  • SSRF protection — stays in datasets.py, untouched

docs.title: Auth plugin — Bearer token from environment
docs.text:
# sunstone_auth_bearer/plugin.py
class BearerAuthPlugin:
    def __init__(self, config: dict | None = None):
        self.env_var = (config or {}).get("env_var", "SUNSTONE_API_TOKEN")
        self.url_pattern = (config or {}).get("url_pattern", None)

    def authenticate(self, url: str, headers: dict[str, str],
                     dataset: DatasetMetadata) -> dict[str, str]:
        if self.url_pattern and self.url_pattern not in url:
            return headers
        token = os.environ.get(self.env_var)
        if token:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
        return headers

# Project's pyproject.toml
[tool.sunstone.plugins.bearer-auth]
env_var = "DATA_PORTAL_TOKEN"
url_pattern = "data.sunstone.institute"

docs.title: URL handler — S3
docs.text:
# sunstone_s3/plugin.py
class S3Plugin:
    def __init__(self, config: dict | None = None):
        self.region = (config or {}).get("region", "us-east-1")

    def can_handle(self, url: str) -> bool:
        return url.startswith("s3://")

    def fetch(self, url: str, dest: Path) -> Path:
        import boto3
        bucket, key = self._parse_s3_url(url)
        s3 = boto3.client("s3", region_name=self.region)
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        s3.download_file(bucket, key, str(dest))
        return dest

docs.title: Format handler — HDF5 (addresses issue #8)
docs.text:
# sunstone_hdf5/plugin.py
class HDF5Plugin:
    def __init__(self, config: dict | None = None):
        self.default_key = (config or {}).get("key", "data")

    def can_read(self, path: Path, format: str | None) -> bool:
        return format == "hdf5" or path.suffix in (".h5", ".hdf5")

    def read(self, path: Path, **kwargs) -> pd.DataFrame:
        key = kwargs.pop("key", self.default_key)
        return pd.read_hdf(path, key=key, **kwargs)

    def can_write(self, path: Path, format: str | None) -> bool:
        return format == "hdf5" or path.suffix in (".h5", ".hdf5")

    def write(self, df: pd.DataFrame, path: Path, **kwargs) -> None:
        key = kwargs.pop("key", self.default_key)
        df.to_hdf(path, key=key, **kwargs)

docs.title: Core infrastructure tests (in sunstone-py)
docs.text:
• Registry discovery — mock entry points, verify plugins classified by protocol
  • Pipeline fallback — no plugins installed, existing behavior unchanged
  • Plugin priority — plugin format handler beats builtin for same extension
  • Auth stacking — two auth providers both modify headers
  • URL handler routing — correct handler selected by can_handle()
  • Config loading — [tool.sunstone.plugins.foo] passed to constructor correctly
  • Bad plugins — plugin implementing no protocol logs warning, doesn't crash

docs.title: Test doubles
docs.text:
class FakeAuthProvider:
    def authenticate(self, url, headers, dataset):
        headers["X-Test"] = "injected"
        return headers

class FakeURLHandler:
    def can_handle(self, url): return url.startswith("fake://")
    def fetch(self, url, dest):
        dest.write_text("col1,col2\na,b\n")
        return dest

class FakeFormatHandler:
    def can_read(self, path, format): return path.suffix == ".fake"
    def read(self, path, **kwargs): return pd.DataFrame({"x": [1, 2, 3]})
    def can_write(self, path, format): return path.suffix == ".fake"
    def write(self, df, path, **kwargs): df.to_csv(path)

These live in sunstone-py's test suite. Plugin packages have their own tests for actual S3/GCS/HDF5 behavior.

docs.title: In scope (v1)
docs.text:
• sunstone/plugins.py module — PluginRegistry, three Protocol definitions, pipeline helpers
  • Refactor dataframe.py read/write methods to call through the pipeline
  • Add auth header injection to datasets.py HTTP fetch
  • Cascading config loading from pyproject.toml, datasets.yaml, and environment variables
  • Test suite for plugin infrastructure with test doubles
  • Sidecar .lineage.json for plugin-handled formats (core feature, not plugin)

docs.title: Deferred — future plugin types
docs.text:
• Lineage enrichers (on_write hooks)
  • License rule providers (issue #13)
  • Validation hooks (pre-read / post-write)
  • Publishing destinations (issue #33)
  • Reference data providers (issue #9)
  • Attribution generators (issue #14)
  • Event hook system (generic version of the above)

docs.title: Deferred — ecosystem
docs.text:
• Actual S3/GCS/HDF5 plugin packages (infrastructure first, plugins later)
  • Plugin versioning / compatibility checks
  • CLI commands for listing installed plugins (sunstone plugin list)
  • Sandboxing or permission model for untrusted plugins

The deferred plugin types all follow the same pattern: add a new Protocol, add a phase to the pipeline, add isinstance check in the registry. The architecture supports this without breaking existing plugins.

docs.title: Stream-Based Plugin IO Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-04-03 Status: Draft Supersedes: Portions of 2026-03-29-plugin-architecture-design.md (URLHandler and FormatHandler protocols)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
The plugin system introduced in v1.3.1+ handles local-file IO well but has no abstraction for remote IO. Specific gaps:

  1. GCS upload logic is hardcoded in cli.py (push_group_to_gcs). Adding S3 or R2 support means editing the CLI directly.
  2. No universal file-like interface. URLHandler only supports fetch(url, dest) -> Path (download to local file). There's no way to open() a remote URL and get a stream that works with print(..., file=), json.dump(..., f), or other standard Python IO.
  3. Two-step fetch-then-read is wasteful for large files. Streaming directly from URL to pandas avoids the temp file.

docs.title: Design Decisions
docs.text:
• Approach C (stream-first with fetch convenience): open() is the core protocol method. fetch() becomes a default utility on PluginRegistry implemented in terms of open(). Plugin authors only implement open().
  • Mirror Python's open() semantics: open(url, "rb") -> BinaryIO, open(url, "r") -> TextIO, and write modes likewise.
  • AuthProvider stays separate. HTTP-oriented handlers call auth providers internally. Cloud-native handlers (GCS, S3) use their own credential systems.
  • Optional extras for cloud dependencies: sunstone-py[gcs] and sunstone-py[s3].
  • Drop requests dependency. HttpURLHandler uses urllib.request from the stdlib.

docs.title: URLHandler
docs.text:
from typing import BinaryIO, Literal, TextIO, Protocol, overload, runtime_checkable

@runtime_checkable
class URLHandler(Protocol):
    def can_handle(self, url: str) -> bool: ...

    @overload
    def open(self, url: str, mode: Literal["r"]) -> TextIO: ...
    @overload
    def open(self, url: str, mode: Literal["rb"]) -> BinaryIO: ...
    @overload
    def open(self, url: str, mode: Literal["w"]) -> TextIO: ...
    @overload
    def open(self, url: str, mode: Literal["wb"]) -> BinaryIO: ...
    def open(self, url: str, mode: str = "rb") -> BinaryIO | TextIO: ...
